News.title: Hilarious moment lazy sea lion boards ship and climbs into captain’s bed to take a nap
News.content:
THIS is the adorable moment a sea lion flops onto a captain’s bed to doze off on a shipping vessel in Argentina.

The social media footage taken on Aug 2 shows the flippered mammal laying on the bed while a man is stuck on the top bunk.



The sea lion can be seen moving around in his new temporary abode among the pillows and blankets trying to find a comfortable spot to take a quick kip.

Laughing crew members took pictures in the doorway while the sea lion was unfazed by the commotion.



One social media user commented that the crew had gained a new “team member.”

It is understood that sea lions often stay around Argentinian ports, becoming a familiar sight around these harbours.

They hop on boats as a safe haven to escape from orcas and sharks that roam the surrounding waters.

They know that these marine predators avoid human vessels.

Over time they are quick to learn that these ships are associated with free food, making it cosier for these exhausted animals to get an easy snack.

Experts are reminding people to remain a safe distance to avoid disturbing these wild animals.

News.title: Serial sexual predator guilty of murdering two sex workers and dumping their bodies across city after raping a third
News.content:
A SERIAL sexual predator has been found guilty of murdering two sex workers months after raping a third.

“Sexually motivated” Simon Levy, 40, began his sick eight-month spree in January last year when he strangled a woman unconscious before raping her in a car park.



The court was told he could have been carrying out daily attacks for years, with dozens more victims out there. The Met Police has referred itself to the Independent Office of Police Conduct.

Today the “predatory monster” was found guilty of two counts of rape, two of murder, one of GBH and one of intentional suffocation.



An Old Bailey jury reached verdicts after deliberating for 13 hours.

Levy, who wore sunglasses in court, made no reaction as the verdicts were delivered and members of the victims’ families wept.

Jurors were told the woman he raped in January was left “as good as dead” after Levy, from Tottenham, London, jumped on her with all his weight – breaking her collarbone.

Two months later, he killed Carmenza Valencia Trujillo, 54, before dumping her body in the stairwell of a derelict building in Peckham, South East London.



The “salsa dance loving grandmother” was found unresponsive at a property on the Aylesbury Estate on March 17.

Emergency crews rushed to respond and tried desperately to save Carmenza’s life.

Tragically, despite the best efforts of medics, she was pronounced dead at the scene, and her cause of death remains a mystery.

Levy was arrested on suspicion of murder on April 1 and released on bail.



He had lived nearby for a number of months in 2023 and would have known the area, the court heard.

His blood was found on a pipe in the stairwell area near where her body was found and his DNA was discovered on the body, jurors were told.

A third victim, Sheryl Wilkins, 39, was found dead near a B&M store in Tottenham, North London, on August 24.

She was found in the same car park where the January rape took place. Sheryl tragically couldn’t be saved and was declared dead at the scene.



Levy was detained for her murder and re-arrested in connection with Carmenza’s death.

Jurors heard that Levy was already a registered sex offender. He sexually assaulted two women in 2018 and was jailed in 2021.

After he was released in 2023, he carried on preying on women, and earlier this year was convicted of 11 counts of sexual assault in a separate trial at Inner London Crown Court.

Ten of the victims were young women who were using the Tube and London Overground, and the 11th was a prison officer, assaulted while he was previously behind bars in 2022.



Prosecutor Tom Little KC previously said both killings were sexually motivated, and that while sexual activity with the women may have started out being consensual, it did not stay that way.

He added: “What is this case that you are now trying all about?

“It involves, we say, a series of predatory sexual attacks from the first eight months of 2025 on three women, each in their own way very vulnerable.

“We say there was one attacker, the defendant.



“Apart from being attacked by the defendant, all three had something else in common. Not in an identical sense, each was either a sex worker or on occasions would perform sexual services in return for money or drugs.

“That’s no coincidence in this case. That’s why and how the defendant encountered them. That’s also why we suggest he attacked them, no doubt hoping and thinking he could get away with it.”

Four days after the woman was raped in January, she was arrested for breach of a community order while on her way to hospital for treatment for the injury to her collarbone.

The woman told police she had been raped but was not well enough to be interviewed at the time because she was withdrawing from heroin.

But in September that year, she told officers how she was attacked and gave a physical description of Levy.



She later picked him out of a police identity parade and he was arrested.

Lisa Ramsarran, chief crown prosecutor for the CPS, said: “Our deepest condolences remain with the families and loved ones of Sheryl Wilkins and Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, and with the third victim who survived a horrific and violent rape at the hands of Simon Levy.

“Our team has met with them throughout proceedings and it is clear it has had a devastating effect on them all.

“Nothing can undo the harm caused, but we hope these convictions provide some measure of justice.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Earlier this year following a trial, the defendant was also found guilty of sexual offences against a number of other women, most of whom were targeted and assaulted whilst travelling on public transport in London.



“His actions have undoubtedly had a profound and lasting impact on all the victims, and we would like to thank them for coming forward.”

News.title: Brits reveal top 20 to-do list tasks they always put off including calling the bank, defrosting freezer & cleaning oven
News.content:
CHORE BORE Brits reveal top 20 to-do list tasks they always put off including calling the bank, defrosting freezer & cleaning oven

Credit: Alamy

BRITS are battling huge to-do lists with the average household putting off up to ten outstanding tasks.

A study found 85 per cent of people feel overwhelmed by the number of jobs they need to get done, while more than half say they have a double-digit list of jobs to sort.

The nation’s top 20 most-postponed tasks include cleaning the oven, sorting drawers and defrosting the freezer, according to research by British Gas.



Booking a boiler service also features alongside calling the bank, sewing on a missing button and fixing a dripping tap.



One in five Brits also admit they postpone arranging a boiler service for up to three months, only remembering to do it when something goes wrong.

Instead of tackling outstanding jobs, four in five admit they procrastinate, including 44 per cent who said they’d rather watch a film.

Others said they were better off binging TV or reading a book.



Brits are most likely to tackle items on their to-do list at the weekend (26 per cent), during days off (14 per cent) or over the summer months (14 per cent).

Nathan Martin-Nicholls, Technical Repair Engineer at British Gas, said: “I think most people have a to-do list that never quite gets any shorter. Every time you cross one thing off, another couple of jobs seem to appear.

“It’s understandable that some tasks get pushed back, especially when life is busy.

“But some jobs are more important than others, and boiler servicing is one that’s easy to overlook during the summer.



“While it’s warm outside, your boiler is probably the last thing on your mind, but summer is actually one of the best times to have it serviced.

“A simple annual check can help identify any issues before winter and give you confidence that your heating is ready when you need it most.”

“With the Summer Sale now live, British Gas is encouraging households to make the most of the longer days and quieter weekends to get ahead before winter.”

News.title: English school abruptly closes leaving hundreds of children without school places ‘despite every effort’
News.content:
AN ENGLISH school has abruptly closed, leaving hundreds of children without places for September.

The prep school, which teaches students aged between three and 11, will not reopen next month or accept any new pupils.



Avon House Preparatory School in Woodford Green, Essex, has now shuttered for good.

Parents were sent an email on August 4, confirming that it would no longer be open, according to Essex Live.



“Despite every effort to secure a sustainable future for the school, including exploring opportunities for investment, merger and sale, it has not been possible to find a financially viable way forward,” it read.

Google reviews for the school, first founded in 1965 and located near Epping Forest, also show that it is now permanently closed.

The private school, which charges up to £17,895 a year for students to attend, fell into financial trouble.

Labour has imposed a 20 per cent VAT on school fees since Janu­ary 2025, adding extra financial strain to many of these educational institutions.

The move is expected to raise £1.8billion a year by 2029/30, but has hit private schools hard.

Earlier this week, it was also confirmed that Sompting Abbotts, will close for good after the end of the academic year.



The school was founded in 1921 on a 30-acre site near Lancing, and consists of around 100 pupils, aged between two and 13.

At the start of the year, Rendcomb College, also confirmed it could no longer remain open, bringing an end to 106-year education history.

The Sun has approached Avon House Preparatory School for comment.

News.title: Moment masked thieves break into OAP’s home & order her to stay quiet – before taking off with cash and jewellery
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment thieves storm into an OAP’s home and order her to keep quiet as they make off with cash and jewellery.

A group of four men were caught on video as they burst into the property in Hayes, West London.



An 83-year-old woman was sleeping when the group smashed their way into her home.

She can be seen waking up and trying to stand from her bed as the group, clad in balaclavas and black clothes, make their way into her house.



One of the men, wielding what appears to be a blade of some sort, walks towards her and orders her to keep quiet.

The group then sets about ransacking the woman’s home, stealing anything valuable they can carry.

With the blade still in his hand, one of the thugs can be seen saying something to the woman.

As they continue to take items from the woman’s home she sits on the bed and watches on, helpless to stop them.



The thugs bag up their items and then sprint out of the property, leaving the terrified woman alone.

She stands up from her bed and goes to check in on her possessions as the video comes to an end.

The robbers remained in her property for two minutes as they carried out the terrifying raid.

Police have since launched an investigation into the harrowing incident which is understood to have happened on July 29.

Cops said that several pieces of jewellery and around £500 in cash was stolen from the woman’s property.



Despite one of the intruders seemingly being armed, no injuries were reported.

A Met spokesperson said: “We are aware of a video circulating online showing a burglary in Hayes. We understand the concern that incidents like this can cause for those affected and the wider community.

“Detectives are conducting a thorough investigation and are pursuing all lines of enquiry.

“On Monday, 29 June at 21:57hrs police were called to reports of a burglary on Judge Heath Lane, Hayes.

“Officers attended but the suspects had fled the scene. They spoke with the victim, an 83-year-old woman. One suspect was captured on CCTV carrying a weapon, but no injuries were reported.



“It is believed that several items of jewellery, as well as around £500 in cash was stolen from the property.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“No arrests have been made at this stage. Enquiries continue and anyone with information that may assist police is asked to call 101 quoting CAD 9067/29July.

“Information can also be provided anonymously to independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Moment boy, 6, shouts ‘I CAN’T’ to laughing mum after getting stuck in railing he tried to slide down in shopping centre
News.content:
THIS is the hilarious moment a six-year-old boy shouts in frustration at his giggling mum after getting his head stuck in a railing.

Little Jason Duxbury got his noggin caught after sliding down the metal rails at Accrington Arndale Centre in Lancashire.



The youngster had been out shopping with his family for clothes and toys last Wednesday ahead of their camping trip to Newquay, Cornwall.

Jason was desperate to slide down instead of taking the stairs, despite his mum’s hesitation to let him slide down.



But as he reached the bottom of the railings, he fell through the gap, managing to get himself stuck and unable to free himself.

And Jason’s mum, Toni Millen, 38, admitted the sight of her lad with his cranium trapped between bars left her in fits of giggles.



She can be heard laughing at her son before asking him to “get out”, to which Jason then replies in frustration, “I can’t”.

Recalling the moment, she said: “Jason had climbed on top of a set of hand rails on a ramp and was saying to me ‘Mum please can I slide down’.



“I told him ‘no’ but he kept asking so I agreed as it was the end of a long day.

“When he got to the bottom he slipped through the middle and managed to get himself stuck the poor thing.

“He then couldn’t pull himself back out. I couldn’t stop laughing when I realised.

“I only recording the video to show his dad what he had done.”

The stay at home mum said after a couple of moments she told him to put his arms in the air so she could lift him out.



Toni said: “He lost a shoe in the process of me getting him out.

“I’m sure he won’t be sliding down a railing again anytime soon.”

Despite his cries for help, Jason was eventually “laughing about it” when he got home, his mum added.

He then asked her to post it on TikTok to see if it would go viral.

Toni said Jason now “thinks he is famous” after the hilarious eight second clip has since been seen by over 6 million people.



Viewers joked that the shopping centre was offering “child parking” aftet watching the video.

One said: “I’d leave him there if he shouted at me like that.”

Another added: “How did he get in there then.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A third said said: “Didn’t know there was child parking so you could shop in peace, that idea will definitely catch on.”

While another commenter said: “Look, just tell him your off to Maccies, he’ll free himself.”

News.title: Law student, 25, charged over intercepted Semtex bomb near Irish border appears in court after ‘manipulated’ claim
News.content:
A LAW student charged in relation to a bomb intercepted in a car near the Irish border has appeared in court.

Isobella Perrie Sullivan, 25, of Abbeylands Park, Clane, Co Kildare, had previously been granted bail after being charged with possession of explosives.



Ms Perrie Sullivan attended a brief hearing at Monaghan District Court today.

She stood when her case was called. The matter was adjourned until September 28 after a garda officer said the DPP is waiting for updates.



At a previous hearing, her defence solicitor said she had been asked to take a bag to the north and had not been aware what was in it, adding that she had been “manipulated”.

The car was stopped on the N2 at Aclint, Carrickmacross, Co Monaghan, in July.

During a search of the vehicle, a bag was discovered in the rear seat that contained an amount of Semtex military grade explosive and a detonator.

In court previously, Ms Perrie Sullivan was granted bail with conditions, including that she not have any contact with anyone in Saoradh or the New IRA.



Also charged in relation to the bomb interception is Simon O’Donovan, an employee at a Dublin museum.

The 44-year-old is charged with possession of an explosive substance at St Laurence’s Road in Chapelizod in the city on Wednesday July 22.

He has been remanded in custody until October 5.

News.title: OAP, 75, admits assaulting her neighbour who has late-stage cancer after ‘poisoning him with ant killer’ in driveway row
News.content:
A PENSIONER has admitted assaulting her neighbour after she allegedly poisoned him with ant killer.

Sally Beaney assaulted her neighbour Matthew Perry – who has late-stage cancer – in a row over their shared driveway.



The 75-year-old pensioner was previously charged with poisoning him with ant killer.

Beaney appeared at Southampton Crown Court and admitted to causing assault occasioning actual bodily harm to Matthew.



They share a driveway in Southampton, Hampshire, and the OAP assaulted him on October 13, 2025.

Matthew, who has “late stage cancer”, was left with swelling on his eye and a “mild corneal injury”, the court heard.

Defending Beaney, Annabel Hazlitt said the assault was caught on camera.

The pensioner kept her not guilty plea of maliciously using ant killer to poison him on October 13, 2025, “with intent to injure, aggrieve, or annoy”.



She will not be sentenced for the ant killer charge but it will lie on the file in case a similar incident happens in the future.

A charge of harassment has been dropped.

Prosecutor Gaylene Coles said: “[Matthew] is certainly at late-stage cancer, so he is still with us if I can put it in those terms.”

Talking about the damage to his eye, Ms Hazlitt said: “In terms of his eye in relation to this offence, it says there seems to be a mild reaction in the right eye, there is a little bit of swelling in the left eye.

“There is relatively mild corneal injury.”



A previous hearing was told Beaney allegedly accused her neighbour of trespassing and wrongdoing.

The homeowner is said to have repeatedly parked her car to block access to his home and placed plant pots, wooden structures and other obstacles across their shared driveway.

Ms Hazlitt said: “Ms Beaney is now 75. She has got no previous convictions.”

She said that prior to sentencing she will be assessed for a mental health treatment requirement.

Judge Nigel Peters KC said: “I think this should be dealt with at sentencing hearing. It is a neighbour dispute that has gone very badly wrong for this defendant.”



Beaney remains on unconditional bail and will be sentenced on September 18.

News.title: Police missed 11 chances to catch serial sex predator Simon Levy before murdering 2 women
News.content:
Police missed 11 chances to catch serial sex predator Simon Levy before murdering 2 women

Details of the shocking catalogue of failings can be revealed today after partially blind Levy, 40, was found guilty of killing Sheryl Wilkins, 39, and Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53

View 6 Images Simon Levy is facing a whole life sentence (Image: Met Police)

The authorities missed at least eleven chances to stop serial sex predator Simon Levy as he murdered two vulnerable women and left a third for dead.

Details of the shocking catalogue of failings can be revealed today after partially blind Levy, 40, was found guilty of killing Sheryl Wilkins, 39, and Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53. He was also convicted by a jury at the Old Bailey of two counts of rape, assault occasioning grievous bodily harm (GBH) with intent and non-fatal suffocation over a sex attack in Janaury 2025, which the victim survived. The Old Bailey jury reached verdicts after deliberating for 13 hours. Levy, who wore sunglasses in court, made no reaction as the verdicts were delivered and members of the victims' families wept.

The "prolific predatory monster" was bailed four times during a year-long reign of terror despite being a convicted sex offender suspected of murder and charged with groping eight women. Judges were not told by Crown Prosecution Service lawyers that he was under investigation for Carmenza's killing when he missed two hearings after repeatedly breaking bail conditions. Levy, who faces a whole life sentence, murdered mum-of-three Sheryl in August last year, 13 days after the final court date.

6 View 6 Images Mum-of-three Sheryl Wilkins was killed in August after a string of failings (Image: SWNS.com) 6 View 6 Images Grandmother Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, was murdered in March last year

And earlier delays by British Transport Police officers meant he had been free to kill grandmother Carmenza in March last year. A bus driver's lost Oyster card that gave unemployed Levy free travel around London as he murdered and sexually assaulted women was not seized when he was arrested four times.

The police watchdog is investigating two Met officers over how Levy was monitored as a registered sex offender. Deniz Ugur, Deputy Director of the End Violence Against Women Coalition, said: "As countless inquiries and reviews of the police and justice system response to violence against women have found, there must be early intervention and prevention-focused responses, particularly regarding management of known serial offenders. The cost of not doing so is women losing their lives.”

Ex-Met DCI David McKelvery said: "What message does this send out? Police have been talking about how seriously they take violence against women and girls and that's all it is, talk. "Here's another example of a violent sex offender being allowed to carry on targeting women despite overwhelming evidence he was a serial abuser."

View 6 Images Levy is arrested in his Spiderman pyjamas in April only to be released under investigation (Image: Met Office)

Met Deputy Assistant Commissioner Kevin Southworth apologised to the victims and admitted there had been a "collective system failure". He said: "There's absolutely significant learning for all parties in this case. I say that not lightly, when we talk about learning, two people have lost their lives and others have had significant sexual offences at the hands of a prolific predatory monster. Obviously this has got to be a point of serious reflection for all of us."

Shocking Catalogue of Failings

Levy was first accused of a sex attack in September 2017 when he was arrested on suspicion of assault by penetration. He had allegedly targeted a woman at a party in Battersea, South London, but the CPS concluded there was insufficient evidence to charge him.

Levy was jailed in 2021 for three years for sexual assault and assault by penetration. He had groped one woman at the Notting Hill Carnival in 2018 after following the other victim from a gathering a few weeks earlier and repeatedly grabbing her. Police and prosecutors failed to review the first attack in light of the other two despite the striking similarities. Levy was released in February 2023, having been accused of sexually assaulting a female guard while in Brixton prison. He lived in approved premises in Walworth, South East London, for a month before moving in with his mum in Tottenham, North London.

Levy carried out his first Tube sex attack on the Jubilee line in October 2023. His victim reported the offence at the time and CCTV was recovered but he was not identified. Levy was interviewed by his probation officer on March 18, 2024, when he claimed he never paid for sex. In May 2024 he was accused of raping a woman in Tottenham and was recalled to prison to serve the rest of his 2021 sentence. Levy then lost his left eye after he was attacked. A source said the assault was suspected to have been carried out in retribution for the alleged rape. No arrests have been made in relation to the attack.

Levy was next arrested on November 4, 2024, on suspicion of sexually assaulting two women in separate attacks on the Central Line the month before. He denied the offences and was released by British Transport Police officers who claim they did not have enough evidence to charge him.

View 6 Images Levy was left blind in his right eye following an attack in 2024 (Image: Met Police)

Levy was bailed until January 22 on condition he did not travel on the Central Line but delays in the investigation meant ID procedures were not requested for nearly two months after his arrest. That resulted in his bail being extended to April 16 last year, leaving him free to kill.

On January 21 Levy violently raped a trafficked sex worker near his home in the car park of a B&M store in Tottenham. The terrified victim, who can't be named, had lost consciousness after he jumped on her back, breaking her collarbone. Levy would murder Sheryl eight months later in the same spot.

The rape victim was arrested for an unrelated matter five days later when she told police she had been attacked by a Black man who she knew by sight. The victim, a homeless drug addict, correctly described to officers the house where he lived but police did not go to the address or identify Levy. She was unable to help with the investigation at the time due to suffering from drug withdrawal symptoms.

While still on bail three months later, Levy murdered Colombian-born Carmenza, 53, on March 16, in a disused block of flats in Walworth, South East London. A pipe smeared with his blood was found next to the salsa-loving victim, also a sex worker, and his DNA was on her body.

Eleven days after the murder, Levy was visited by a police officer managing him on the Violent and Sex Offencer Register (ViSOR). He lied to the PC claiming that he was homebound due to his eye injury and "mental health" issues. Two officers, a PC and a Sergeant, have been referred to the independent Office for Police Conduct over alleged failings in monitoring the convicted sex offender.

Levy was arrested on suspicion of Carmenza's murder three days later, on April 1. He answered "no comment" when asked about the attack. Carmenza had suffered a neck compression and facial injuries but her cause of death was deemed to be "unascertained".

‌



Police failed to seize Levy's stolen Oyster card which showed he had been in the area at around the time of her murder. And phone data had captured a handset linked to him calling his mother at 6.39pm close to where Carmenza was found dead. Despite this evidence, police did not consult the CPS over whether he should be charged because of difficulties in ascertaining the cause of death. Levy, who was among five suspects arrested for the murder, was released under investigation.

Ten days later he was again identified on CCTV shortly after sexually assaulting another woman, this time on the Victoria Line. British Transport Police officers planned to arrest him on April 3 only to discover he had been detained and released by Met detectives over Carmenza's murder. His bail date for the BTP investigation was extended to May 1 and he was not arrested.

Levy was then identified over three further Tube sex attacks on April 7 and 26 and on May 1. He was detained on the day of the final incident, charged with five assaults and remanded into custody.

‌



Levy was one of 18 cases that appeared at a "chaotic" Highbury Corner Magistrates' court on Saturday May 3 where he was released for a third time. No application was made to remand him despite BTP officers requesting that bail be opposed. They told the CPS that Levy was being investigated for murder and rape, adding he was a "danger to the public and at high-risk of re-offending".

View 6 Images Sheryl Wilkins was murdered in August last year after Levy repeatedly escaped remand (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

A document sent to the prosecutor said: "Police have significant concerns that if granted bail, Levy will continue in his predatory sexual offending against female members of [the] public." Levy was bailed on condition he did not travel on the Tube at rush hour.

‌



Five days later the police investigation into the January car park rape was closed without the victim having been spoken to. She had been unwilling to assist the investigation due to drug withdrawal symptoms but later gave evidence at the murder trial.

On June 20 Levy was detained for a fourth time, for yet more Tube sex offences, this time committed on April 8 and May 29 as well as breach of bail. He was then charged with eight separate sexual assaults on lone women on the Tube network and one breach of bail.

Levy appeared at Highbury Corner Magistrates' court June 21 before JPs Jacqueline Scott, Marta Corti and Gerry Teague when he pleaded not guilty to the nine charges. Prosecutor Jyothi Somavarapu made an application for him to be remanded but sources said "not all relevant information was put before the court".

‌



A document sent to the CPS by the BTP failed to mention he was under investigation for murder and rape. He was released for a fourth time with the same bail conditions. Magistrates do not record transcripts of their hearings so there is no record of what was said or how the JPs came to the decision. Levy then failed to turn up for a hearing at Inner London Crown Court on June 3 but no warrant was issued for his arrest after the prosecutor declined to request one. Again the judge was not told he was a murder and rape suspect.

On July 18 Levy again failed to appear at Inner London Crown Court after neither he, nor his solicitor, were made aware of the hearing date. Levy was scheduled for yet another appearance at the same court before judge Ian Darling on August 11 and again he failed to show. No warrant was requested or issued for his arrest. Once again the court was not told about the murder and rape investigations.

Levy murdered Sheryl 13 days later, on August 24. Her body was discovered behind a wall in the B&M carpark in Tottenham. The 39-year-old was found face down with 83 injuries to her face and head, upper body and arms and legs. Levy was identified by murder cops on September 3 and arrested two days later when he was finally remanded into custody. Detectives then uncovered phone evidence placing Levy close to where Carmenza was murdered. They also discovered a lost Oyster card he was using put him in the area on the afternoon of her death.

Article continues below

In total he carried out 13 sex attacks between 2018 and 2025. Among them were ten women aged between 18 and 32 who were attacked on the Tube. Levy had denied two counts of murder, rape, grievous bodily harm with intent and non-fatal suffocation.

BTP Det Supt Peter Fulton said a DC had been removed from investigation work due to "incompetence". Mr Fulton apologised for the delay in bringing Levy to justice, saying: "It should have been done much quicker and much more efficiently."

Lisa Ramsarran, Chief Crown Prosecutor for the CPS, apologised for failing not providing courts with relevant information when Levy was repeatedly bailed. She said: “Our actions fell short of the standards that victims, families and the public are entitled to expect. In particular, there were points where we could and should have taken a more robust approach to representations about bail, based on the information available. We recognise our responsibility and we are sorry for the shortcomings we have identified."

News.content:
