News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

Sports.title: Southampton captain Jack Stephens admits points deduction for Spygate scandal has fired Saints up to ‘put things right’
Sports.content:
SOUTHAMPTON skipper Jack Stephens insists the club’s four-point deduction for spying on rivals has fired him up to “put things right”.

Saints will start the season with work to do just to get back to zero, but they are laser-focused on promotion three months after Spygate saw them booted out of the play-offs.



Manager Tonda Eckert admitted he was responsible for the snooping missions, and the FA charged him for “bringing the game into disrepute”.

The German boss, 33, received death threats and still faces the possibility of a touchline ban – but will go again after retaining the backing of Southampton owner Dragan Solak.



And now Stephens is desperate to achieve what was painfully snatched away from Saints in May.

He told SunSport: “The way the season ended was disappointing for everyone involved.

“It was important for everyone to get away, clear their heads, forget about what happened and come back with a clean slate, fully focused on this season.

“We’ve all come back with a mindset that we want to get promoted. We felt like we deserved it last season but that counts for nothing. We need to go and prove it this season.

“We’re not starting from scratch, we’re starting from minus four. It’s going to be a little bit of an uphill task but it’s one we’re very much looking forward to.

“I’d rather not have the four points deducted but that’s where we are.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We have spoken about it as a group and we’re well aware of the challenge ahead. But we’re also very keen to use that to drive us forward.

“We’ve got the bit between our teeth, we want to put that right for the football club.

“We’re very confident but we have to start again and use this as the driving force behind our season.”

Spygate was a chaotic end to a campaign that promised so much when Eckert masterminded a 19-match unbeaten run that took Saints from 21st to fourth in the league.



No manager in the Championship has picked up more points than Eckert since he was appointed last December.

So for Stephens, 32, there is no question about whether the boss and the squad are strong enough to be in the mix again.

He said: “100 per cent. The evidence is there from last season.

“I’ve got no doubts that we’re going to give it absolutely everything and be very close to promotion.

“Our squad has stayed pretty much the same, in comparison to the teams who have come down from the Premier League, who have a lot to sort out with their squads.



“We’re extremely motivated to put those four points right and we want to do it as quickly as we can.”

Eckert himself has admitted the saga and his punishment are still looming at the back of his mind – and English football fans surely won’t let him forget.

Saints would be wise to expect hostile welcomes from most grounds this season.



So it will have been a relief for Eckert and the squad to get away from it all on a pre-season trip to Germany, where they sharpened up with friendlies against first, second and third-tier opposition.

Their first competitive assignment is against fourth-tier Colchester on Saturday, but Stephens and his team-mates are not taking their quirky Carabao Cup start lightly.

He said: “It’s slightly different but it doesn’t really change anything for us. We’ve approached this game as an important game, which it is.

“We’re looking to go and win and get through to the next round of the cup.”

Sports.title: South Korea’s FA accused of providing referees with sex massages in astonishing claim
Sports.content:
SOUTH KOREA’S FA have sensationally been accused of providing referees with sex massages before games.

The shock claims are alleged to have occurred between 2011 and 2012, according to South Korean TV station JTBC and news agency Yonhap.



The KFA are said to have paid for foreign referees to attend massage parlours in Seoul and other South Korean cities hosting international fixtures.

The matches reportedly included 2014 World Cup and 2012 London Olympic qualifying.



The revelations were based on credit card statements and documents from a government audit report from 2016.

It claimed 20 match officials – who were from Japan, the UAE, Iran, Bahrain and Uzbekistan – were provided with sexual entertainment across seven matches.

South Korea went on an unbeaten run during this period, winning five and drawing twice.

In one period, the team beat Oman 2-0 in an Olympic qualifier on September 21, 2011, before a 2-0 victory over Kuwait in a 2014 World Cup qualifier.

Another Olympic qualifier against Qatar ended in a goalless draw the following month – but the team had already qualified by this point.

South Korea were strong favourites for all three games.



The report from JTBC claimed some referees expected the favours from the KFA and it was “common practice at the time” to cater to them.

According to the Korea Times, the KFA could escape Fifa sanctions as breaches of its ethics code cannot be prosecuted after five years – and ten years for bribery and corruption cases.

SunSport has reached out to the KFA for comment.



It comes during a time of crisis for the KFA after a disastrous World Cup saw South Korea players boycott the media after a video slur towards captain Son Heung-min.

The team were later dumped out in the group stage before coach Hong Myung-bo resigned from his role.

Police then raided KFA offices this week over the initial appointment of Hong in 2024.

Local media said officers were looking into whether KFA chiefs violated internal rules with the hiring of Hong due to “obstruction of business”.

The team’s performance at the World Cup under Hong was so poorly received the coach has been banned from some shops in South Korea.



Hong announced his resignation one day after South Korea’s elimination.

He said: “Over the past two years I asked myself the same question whenever I had to make important decisions, select players or prepare for training session and matches: ‘Is this the right choice for Korean football?’

“I can not say every decision has been the right one, but I can tell you that I have made every decision with Korean football in mind.”

Sports.title: Messi suicide bomb, Ronaldo hotel alert & ref’s 6,000 texts…scale of World Cup threats revealed in leaked police dossier
Sports.content:
A CHILLING police dossier has revealed major security threats made during the World Cup including a horror warning from a suicide bomber.

The bombshell document, seen by Informacion.es, details multiple terrifying terror attempts – with Argentina‘s national team a particular target.



Before their match against Jordan, a man is believed to have rang up Dallas airport and said he and two others would storm the stadium with “homemade bombs and an AR-15”.

The suspected bomber threatened to attack “police officers and players from both teams” but made “special mention” of killing Lionel Messi, according to reports.



Argentina’s match against Egypt was also a target after one suspected terrorist wrote on X: “I’m about to enter Atlanta’s stadium and blow up Messi with four bombs strapped to my body.”

During the game another man called police and announced that

he had left “three bombs” inside trash cans across the stands.

The double threat sparked a major hunt across the stadium by bomb specialists and sniffer dogs.

Messi’s rival Cristiano Ronaldo was also an alleged victim of World Cup attack fears.

A FIFA employee raised the alarm after a “suspicious man” was asking for “details” about the Portuguese superstar’s World Cup accommodation.

Another rabid superfan broke into the footballer’s hotel and tried to get into an elevator with him.



When cops handcuffed the man, he claimed that he just wanted to take a selfie with Ronaldo.

Referee François Letexier was hounded by more than 6,000 “threatening messages” on his personal WhatsApp after his controversial rulings at the Argentina-Egypt match.

Egyptian fans also bombarded video assistant referee (VAR) Willy Delajod with furious messages including death threats.



In yet another disturbing incident, a strawman labelled as “Mbappe” was burned by Paraguay fans after the nation’s defeat by France.

The Real Madrid star was the target of racist attacks, including a sickening tirade from a Paraguayan senator.

Players who made mistakes also received death threats.



Alexander Sorloth and his wife received death threats after the Norway striker failed to play Erling Haaland into goal during their quarter-final clash with England.

Colombian player Jaminton Campaz also faced threats for missing a penalty and was unable to return to the country with the rest of the team after their exit.

Colombia are all too aware of the dangers their players face, after defender Andrés Escobar was executed by a drug cartel after scoring an own goal at the 1994 World Cup.

The South Korea national team also received heavy police protection after their underwhelming group stage exit.

Exiled coach Hong Myung-bo has since been the subject of intense public anger, with police even probing his hiring process.



The England team’s media centre also experienced a worrying security breach.

A man holding a wrench wandered in and began shouting as surprised members of the media.

The Three Lions squad was shielded by three rings of security at their US base at the most fortified World Cup ever.

Their hotel will become a “virtual fortress” surrounded by a cordon of concrete barriers and screens to block the line of sight of potential snipers.

A no-fly zone was enforced to thwart drone attacks and a command centre opposite 54-room, £260-a-night The Inn at Meadowbrook Hotel.



Armed police, security officers and private security guards also patrolled the perimeter of the complex in Prairie Village, Kansas.

Sports.title: David Sullivan set to defy advice to stay away from West Ham matches and attend Carabao Cup clash vs Portsmouth
Sports.content:
WARNING IGNORED David Sullivan set to defy advice to stay away from West Ham matches and attend Carabao Cup clash vs Portsmouth

DAVID SULLIVAN is set to attend West Ham’s clash with Portsmouth on Saturday despite being advised to steer clear of London Stadium.

Sullivan, 77, is the Hammers’ largest single shareholder but quit as co-chair in June when accusations of preying on women for sex came to light.



The Carabao Cup first-round game is West Ham‘s first home fixture since the allegations were levelled at Sullivan, who categorically denies them.

London Stadium chiefs had ‘recommended‘ that Sullivan should NOT attend the match due to concerns over fan backlash.



They also asked for ‘advance notice’ of Sullivan attending so they can ramp up safety measures.

But according to BBC Sport, the former porn and newspaper mogul is planning to ignore the advice and turn up anyway.



Sullivan retains a 38.8 per cent stake in West Ham, who were relegated from the Premier League last campaign.

But there is expected to be a lively attendance this weekend after a whopping 55,000 season tickets were snapped up during the off-season.

Seven women accused Sullivan of abusing his power and preying on them for sex following a joint investigation from The Times and BBC Panorama.

All women were in their late teens or early twenties at the time the alleged incidents took place, with some dating back to the 1980s.



And all were aspiring models hoping to work for Sullivan’s newspapers.

London Stadium operators said earlier this week: “Given the potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators, we have recommended to the club that he does not attend.

“We have also requested advance notice of any planned attendance so that appropriate safety and operational measures can be put in place.”

The West Ham Fan Advisory Board also called on Sullivan to stay away, urging him not to put “personal interest before the good of the club”.

Part of Sullivan’s June statement read: “I have recently become aware that factually incorrect and entirely false, decades-old allegations concerning my personal life are due to be broadcast and published.



“After a lifetime spent building businesses in the adult industry in which I have met thousands of women, it is sadly inevitable that a small number of improper conduct claims are being made against me. I categorically deny these claims.”

Sports.title: Man Utd’s £50m goalkeeper gamble failed in worst transfer window ever but academy sale can provide new blueprint
Sports.content:
BOTH GOALKEEPERS Manchester United signed three years ago are now gone.

That Andre Onana and Altay Bayindir have merely secured season-long loan agreements reflects doubly badly on United.



In fairness to the current regime, Onana and Bayindir were bought by their predecessors. United paid more than £50m for them.

United’s current decision-makers will point the finger at legacy deals behind their continued inability to sell senior players, but Bayindir only cost £4.1million on deadline day in 2023.



That was the same summer United signed Mason Mount, Rasmus Hojlund, Sofyan Amrabat, Sergio Reguilon and Jonny Evans. Little wonder they had their worst season in 34 years.

Even someone as small fry as Bayindir has had his reputation harmed by association with United. Seventeen games, 31 goals conceded and one good performance (Arsenal away in the FA Cup).

Celta Vigo have an option to buy Bayindir for £3.5m. The numbers do not add up when he will have one year left on his United deal come next summer and last played in September 2025.

Bayindir wore the number one, was signed as a number two but should have been the number three for United.

Turkey has produced some stylish mavericks. Bayindir’s old Fenerbahce teammate Arda Guler is one of them. Turkey is not renowned for its quality ‘keepers.

United did sell a goalie this week – Radek Vitek to Middlesbrough for an initial £7m, potentially rising to £14m.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Vitek has never played for United, hence why his resale value is high. He came through the academy and excelled on loan in the Championship and is now Boro bound.

If United are to start milking the academy cash cow then Vitek is the blueprint. Develop good prospects with no believable pathway into the first team, secure a second-tier loan, keep them at arm’s length from the first team and sell.

Leeds have agreed a £45m fee for James Trafford as he came through the Manchester City academy during Pep Guardiola’s golden period. Trafford has Premier League experience, was good enough to be re-signed by City and is an England international.

United’s academy sells but it is not at the level of City’s. Significant first team success will always have a bearing on how junior talents are viewed from the outside.



Ironically, United’s director of football helped enhanced City’s reputation. Jason Wilcox held the same title at Southampton when they signed Taylor Harwood-Bellis, Shea Charles and Josh McNamara from City.

At least United’s goalkeeping department looks its best in six years. Senne Lammens has been a revelation and a bargain, Karl Darlow has ample Premier League pedigree as a number two and Tom Heaton was namechecked by the outgoing Casemiro as one of the club’s most important players.

In 2020, United had David de Gea, Dean Henderson and Sergio Romero on their books. Impeccable cover but too senior a trio.

Romero resented his demotion for the Europa League semi-final defeat to Sevilla in August 2020 yet United failed to facilitate a transfer. So Romero spent a miserable final season unused, the isolation exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic.



Henderson was a credible challenger to De Gea and would have succeeded him but for Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s infamous indecision.

The luckless Henderson contracted Covid days after attending the European Championship final at Wembley in July 2021 and was laid low for two months. Solskjaer scrapped the succession plan.

With Lammens, Darlow and Heaton, each has a defined role of one, two and three. De Gea, Henderson and Romero all had a shout at claiming No.1 status.

Craig Mawson has been promoted to lead goalkeeping coach under Michael Carrick, having been at United for six-and-a-half years. Lammens is yet to make an outright mistake with his hands; his only blemish is a daft pass that allowed Liverpool to equalise in May.



Onana and Bayindir committed enough howlers for their own bloopers DVD, if they were still produced. De Gea’s final season was marred by clangers that convinced Erik ten Hag United needed a new No.1.

Former goalkeeping coach Richard Hartis, brought back to the club by Solskjaer and discarded amid Ineos’s coaching staff overhaul in 2024, oversaw a rocky five-year period for those between the sticks.

In an era of set-piece coaches, Hartis was the one Solskjaer used to send into the technical area to choreograph United’s defensive shape. United shipped 14 goals from dead balls in the 2020-21 season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Onana’s steadiest spell was after Hartis was replaced by Jelle ten Rouwelaar. Only he lasted four months.

It got much worse after Hartis and Ten Rouwelaar were discarded. Bayindir and Onana both conceded straight from corners. One week apart.

Sports.title: Newcastle plot transfer splurge for Jaissle after pulling off coup to get £75m Bruno Guimaraes fee from Arsenal
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE believe they have pulled off a coup by securing £75million for 28-year-old Bruno Guimaraes.

And the dosh Arsenal are coughing up for the Brazilian midfielder will give the green light for the club to bring in several new recruits for new boss Matthias Jaissle.



Club captain Guimaraes was in tears following an emotional goodbye at the club’s La Manga training camp on Tuesday before jetting off for his Gunners medical.

While Toon were gutted to lose their talisman, following on from the recent sales of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, they insist they have secured a “good deal”.



CEO David Hopkinson said: “It was not the fee that I think Arsenal had hoped to pay and of course we would have liked an even higher number.

“But I think you’re dealing with sophisticated actors on both sides and that’s what negotiation looks like.



“It’s a fee that satisfies us. If you want to put a merchandising spin on it, it’s the highest fee for a player in that position at that age.

“Is that a good deal for Newcastle? I believe it is. But Arsenal is getting a very special player and special person so this works from a financial perspective for both sides.”

Sporting director Ross Wilson has already brought in five exciting new young guns for Jaissle as he leads the rebuild of the squad following Eddie Howe’s departure.

And while he remains excited over the future, he admitted Guimaraes’ exit was not part of “the plan” this summer.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He said: “We didn’t want to sell Bruno. It wasn’t in the plan to sell Bruno. None of us – or ownership – wanted to sell Bruno.

“He’s our captain, he was very, very important to us and the debate over his price – it’s a world record fee for a player of his age.

The actual world record, however, is the £88.5million Real Madrid paid for Eden Hazard in 2019, with add-ons taking the deal towards £130million.

Wilson continued: “What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on.



“That doesn’t mean he can go but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number.

“But there’s no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer – it wasn’t.

“But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen. It might have been in our plan to sign one player but we didn’t get him so we move on to another.

“We can only be honest about that.

“We’d love Bruno Guimares to be in our squad this summer but I’m sure there are other clubs that have lost players that wish they were in their squads this season.



“It’s the world we live in, we had to adapt, we had to react.

“Having such an important player leave is disappointing but having a really important player who doesn’t want to play here anymore – for himself, he’s honest about that – it was the only decision we could make.”

Both Saudi PIF officials and co-owner Jamie Reuben were in southern Spain on Thursday as new manager Jaissle met the media for the face time.

With PIF officials present, and director Jamie Reuben, who jetted into southern Spain, there is great optimism that the transfer window can end on a high.

During a summit at the Hotel Grand Hyatt La Manga Club, chiefs were updated on how the club’s SCR situation is now positive.



More importantly, the Guimaraes cash gives them headroom to add to a depleted and young squad.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Wilson added: “We want to strengthen the squad. Of course we want to add more. The support of the guys is there as well.

“Matthias wants to assess what we have as well, which is obvious, he’s been doing that for some time now so he’s got a view on that already and we’re aligned on what we want to do.”

Sports.title: Man City set transfer price for Rodri with Barcelona way off valuation – after he picked them over Real Madrid move
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY have already rejected a bid from Barcelona for Rodri and will demand more than £60million if he insists on leaving.

The Catalan giants want to sign the former Ballon d’Or winner, 30, who prefers them over a move to rivals Real Madrid.



City have already laughed off a very low bid, with reports in Spain suggesting it was in the region of £38m.

The two clubs are not currently in negotiations and it will take a much bigger fee to tempt the Prem club to part with their World Cup winner – even though he only has 10 months remaining on his contract.



City’s stance has always been that if a player is clear that he wants to leave then they will not stand in his way.

Rodri’s agent told a Spanish television station that the midfielder had decided he wants a switch to the Nou Camp – despite previous interest from Real Madrid.

He was quoted as saying: “Out of respect for Madrid – as they have been class – Rodri has informed them his decision is to join Barca.”

But the club’s hierarchy – many of whom are here in Seoul for the second leg of their pre-season tour – have not been informed of that as things stand.

Rodri is due back at the City Football Academy early next week to begin his preparations for the season.

However he underwent a minor back operation after the World Cup so that could put his return to training back a few days.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

City are pushing on with their move for Lille’s £85m-rated youngster Ayyoub Bouaddi regardless of what happens with Rodri.

Sources at the Etihad have indicated that progress has been made over the Morocco World Cup star, 18, in recent days.

However if Rodri goes, then City are likely to look for a replacement – even though they have new boy Elliot Anderson and Nico Gonzalez already in that position.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer’s girlfriend stuns in blue athleisure tank top as Chelsea star’s sister gives rave review
Sports.content:
COLE PALMER’s girlfriend Olivia Holder was showered with compliments on her latest Instagram post.

Palmer’s sister, Hallie, was among those spreading the love as Holder posed outside a swanky doorway in London.



She wore a blue athleisure two-piece, carried a small black handbag, had on a pair of under-eye patches and sipped away on an iced matcha.

Holder captioned the post: “Cool girls wear @garageclothing.”



It was liked well over a thousand times, and over a hundred people flooded the comments.

Palmer’s sister, Hallie, wrote: “Gorgggggg [heart emoji].”



Another follower added: “Oh I’m obsessed with this.”

A third commented: “Ultimate cool girl.”

Another gushed: “Speechless.”

A fifth said: “Such a babe.”



And a sixth pined: “Obsessed with you.”



Model and influencer Holder was first spotted with Palmer at Winter Wonderland last December.

She posed for snaps on a yacht in Ibiza earlier this summer, where Palmer went on holiday after missing out on England‘s World Cup squad.

And she regularly attends matches at Stamford Bridge, where Palmer and his Chelsea team-mates will host Brighton in their first home game of the season on August 30.

Aston Villa stars 'think they know what's happening next' with Arsenal target Ezri Konsa

Arsenal are targeting Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa in a £60m deal - and his team-mates think they know where he'll end up before the transfer window closes

Sports.title: Rodri's agent drops transfer bombshell as Man City star decides future
Sports.content:
Rodri's agent drops transfer bombshell as Man City star decides future

Real Madrid were long considered the favourites to sign Rodri before Barcelona entered the running, with the midfielder having entered the final 12 months of his contract at Manchester City

View 2 Images Rodri has decided his next club (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Rodri's agent has announced that the Manchester City star wants to join Barcelona over arch rivals Real Madrid. Rodri, 30, agreed personal terms with Barca on Thursday in a sudden and dramatic twist.

‌



The Spaniard had been in talks with Real for weeks after suggesting back in March that he was keen on a move to the Bernabeu. But Barcelona have hijacked the move after Rodri spoke to their manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director Deco and was convinced to join the La Liga champions.

‌



Although City haven't given up hope of tying Rodri down to a new contract after he entered the final year of his current deal, Etihad chiefs are well aware of his desire to return to Spain. In a late-night interview with Cadena SER, Rodri's agent, Pablo Barquero, revealed all.

‌



"Out of respect for Madrid, as they have been class, Rodri informed them that his decision is to join Barca," Barquero told the Spanish radio station.

Barcelona are in the market for a midfielder after Frenkie de Jong was ruled out for several months. Rodri is seen as a plug and play option, having gotten over his injury troubles and helped Spain win the World Cup last month.

‌



The 30-year-old also picked up the Golden Ball at the tournament, playing an integral role for Luis de la Fuente's side. His departure from City would follow that of manager Pep Guardiola, defender John Stones and midfielder Bernardo Silva in a summer of change at the Etihad.

New boss Enzo Maresca remains desperate to keep him, though, and stated earlier this week: "It's very important (to have him). Any manager in the world wants Rodri because he's a top player; so it's important for me, the club and for everyone."

But Maresca's hopes could soon be dashed. Barcelona have room in their wage budget following the departure of Robert Lewandowski and appear to have enough funds to tempt City to the negotiating table, having bid around £100m for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez in June.

Rodri has spent seven years with City, winning four Premier League titles, one Champions League and two FA Cups. The former ex-Villarreal man received the Ballon d'Or in 2024, having won that year's European Championship with Spain.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has not yet followed transfer instructions previously laid out by Paul Scholes

View 4 Images Manchester United boss Michael Carrick was told by a former team-mate to sell some players (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick has not sanctioned any major sales so far this summer at Manchester United. This is despite United hero Paul Scholes recommending eight stars be sold.

‌



Carrick is currently taking charge of his first pre-season and there are just a few weeks until the Premier League returns. With only three first-team signings made so far in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow, more additions are expected.

‌



However, there has yet to be a major exit from the club, aside from Casemiro's departure. In April, Scholes was asked for a series of United stars who were surplus to requirements and of the eight players he listed, only one appears set to leave as things stand.

Scholes and Carrick spent seven seasons together in United's midfield during their playing days. However, whilst the pundit's suggestion to move on Zirkzee may materialise, the other seven stars Scholes mentioned could all remain part of United's squad next term, with Carrick's response clear.

The 51-year-old stressed the importance of United revamping their defence. Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast, Scholes said of Leny Yoro: "I think he's struggled, me. Sports.title: Man City reject Barcelona offer for Rodri
Sports.content:
Manchester City have knocked back an initial offer from Barcelona for Rodri that is considered far too low.

Talks over a deal have therefore halted for now.

It remains to be seen whether Barcelona return with a higher offer but their interest in signing him remains.

Sources in Spain believe Rodri would prefer a move to Barcelona over Real Madrid.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Transfer Show, the panel discuss which Spanish giant is favourite to sign Manchester City midfielder Rodri

City do not want to sell Spain's World Cup-winning captain and instead want to agree a new contract with him.

If Rodri asks to leave, however, then they would not stand in his way.

Chelsea's Fernandez would be 'dream' signing for Maresca

Image: Enzo Fernandez could be a target for Man City if Rodri leaves

As City assess their options for a replacement, Sky in Italy have reported that Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez would be boss Enzo Maresca's "dream" signing.

Sky Sports News reported earlier this summer that Fernandez was not an option they were looking to sign, however, as they have been looking to keep hold of Rodri.

The fluidity of the situation, therefore, means it remains to be seen whether circumstances change with regards to Fernandez, as City may look to bring in two players if Rodri joins Barcelona.

Carra: Don't sell Rodri for £40-50m!

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher:

"£40-50m? If you're Manchester City, what's the point in selling them? You might as well just keep them for the extra year.

"He's as good as anybody in that position in the Premier League, probably the best. Seeing what he was like in the World Cup, it was like he was back to his best.

"I thought the second half of the season him and Bernardo Silva were fantastic and almost took Manchester City to the title.

"So, if I was the manager of Manchester City, I'd be keeping Rodri at that price. It'd have to be something really special to want me to lose arguably the best midfield player in world football.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher urges Manchester City to keep midfielder Rodri for the final season of his contract rather than sell him in this transfer window

"I think it'd be really tough for them to win the Premier League without Rodri, even though they've got a lot of midfielders. He's the best, even though they've brought Elliot Anderson, who is one who I'm sure will learn off Rodri.

"And for me, I'd see those two as a pair. I see Elliot Anderson as almost the replacement for Bernardo Silva, who's gone to Real Madrid. So, I think that'd be a big hole. It'd be really difficult to fill.

"When Liverpool won the title under Arne Slot, Rodri got an injury in that season very early on, which helped Liverpool and was to the detriment of Manchester City. So if I was Manchester City, I'd be keeping him and letting him go on a free.

"City paid £60m for him. If they're getting £40m back now, what can they do with that type of money? Not a lot, really. So, I'd rather keep him."

Image: Real Madrid has also shown an interest in Rodri

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:

Massive. Despite his age, and recent injury record, Rodri remains the most complete central midfielder to have operated in the Premier League over the past five years. "The best midfielder in the world by far," maintains Pep Guardiola.

Under Guardiola, City's in-play strategy revolved entirely around him, always impressing with his use of the ball and ability to receive in tight situations. He set the tempo for his team and controlled games as a result, doing the same for triumphant Spain this summer.

There is no current player who can condition a game like Rodri, and it is no coincidence City failed to retain their Premier League crown in the two seasons he was injury-plagued.

So, how is he replaced?

In short, he isn't.

But in Anderson City have got a surrogate of sorts. The England international might not yet be the dictator Rodri is but he can evolve to become something close. As a box-to-box midfielder, the 23-year-old is putting up numbers that at least mean he is comparable.

"It did definitely open a lot of eyes, my last fight [against Smith], because of the fashion I did it in, it was a really dominant fight in my favour," McKenna told Sky Sports.

"To fight a former world champion in Liam Smith was a massive name to have on my record. A lot of people were predicting me to lose. So that was another bonus, once I beat him in the fashion I did, it opened a lot of eyes and really got my name out there.

"Going into that fight I was the underdog and not many people gave me a chance. But I knew that was my time to really show the world how good of a boxer I am. Not many people expected me to have that style but I've been saying it for years, of how good of a boxer I am.

"Now's another chance to really shine again."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McKenna and Oliha refused to back down as they faced off ahead of their IBF middleweight title fight

McKenna is determined to build from here. "Once I become world champion I'm going to take over the division," he said.

"I want to clean up the division. The 160lb division is there to be cleaned up. So I want to become undisputed and then become a multiple-weight world champion.

"I want the biggest and best fights, I want to take on guys with undefeated records, or guys who are world champions and prove to myself I'm the best in the world. If I can't get the champions at 160lb, I'll take them on at 168lb, it doesn't matter to me. I'll take care of business on Saturday first."

On the undercard Callum Walsh fights Tyler Denny in a dangerous test. Walsh, who has spent much of his previous career at super-welter, was exactly on the 160lb limit. Denny was 159.7lb.

Light-heavyweight talent Joe Ward hopes to announce himself to the professional sport against hard-punching, unbeaten contender Artjom Kasparian.

Both made weight, Ward scaled 174.08lb and Kasparian was 174.2lb.

"It's going to be unbelievable," Walsh told Sky Sports. "It's going to be a great card the whole way through.

"The buzz is going to be high. Quick fights, good fights back to back and keep the buzz going and by the time I come out it's going to be unbelievable in there.

"We can continue to show that Ireland does produce some of the best fighters in the world."

Sports.title: Van Barneveld fine and suspension revealed in Darts Regulation Authority case list
Sports.content:
Five-time world champion Raymond van Barneveld has been fined and suspended by the Darts Regulation Authority for inappropriate behaviour and offensive language.

The DRA, which is the independent body responsible for regulating the sport, particularly in events run under the umbrella of the PDC, WDF, Modus and ADC, has published an updated case list for the first time since 2022, listing all backdated hearings from January 2023 to June 2026, relating to various incidents that had occurred in both televised and non-televised competition.

Former world champions Rob Cross, Gary Anderson, Luke Humphries and Van Barneveld all feature in the case list, along with Cameron Menzies and Dom Taylor.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Raymond van Barneveld talks us through his greatest game as he beat Phil Taylor in the final of the 2007 World Championship

Van Barneveld, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest-ever players, features in two separate incidents.

The first involves 'Inappropriate behaviour and using offensive language' at Players Championship 2 event in Wigan last year, resulting in a three-month suspension [suspended for 12 months] and £3,000 fine.

The second relates to 'failing to report damage caused to hotel room' following a Players Championship event in Germany, which resulted in a formal warning.

'Barney' is a five-time world champion having won the BDO tournament at Lakeside in 1998, 1999, 2003 and 2005 before making the move to the PDC the following year.

The doyen of Dutch darts made his mark by winning the 2007 PDC World Championship with a legendary final against Phil 'The Power' Taylor.

Sky Sports have contacted the DRA regarding Van Barneveld's fines.

Menzies handed four-month suspension

Image: Cameron Menzies repeatedly punched the underside of the drinks table on stage in frustration following his defeat to Charlie Manby at the World Championship

Menzies' sanction for his outburst at the World Championship in December has been revealed, with the Scot handed a four-month suspension, which ended last month, and receiving a £2,500 fine after he repeatedly punched the underside of the drinks' table on stage in frustration following his defeat to Charlie Manby.

The incident drew blood on his knuckles, which he then wiped on his face before walking off the stage.

Shortly after the incident, Menzies issued a statement apologising for his actions.

"First of all, I would like to apologise for what happened," said Menzies. "I am sorry that I reacted in the manner that I did.

"It's not an excuse, but I have had a lot of things on my mind recently and I suppose it all just became too much at the end.

"It has not been an easy time for me with my uncle Gary passing away recently. I saw him four days before he died and he gave a look which told he much he thought of me. He treated me like a son.

"Had I won the game against Charlie, my second match would have been on the day of Gary's funeral and that has not been lost on me in recent days.

"Let me say again, that's no excuse for what I did on the stage. It was the wrong thing to do and I don't want it to take anything away from Charlie. He played well and deserved his win.

"This is not how I would like people to view me. Yes I can get emotional at times, but not like that and that wasn't right."

Taylor's failed drugs test

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dom Taylor impressed on his Ally Pally debut in a first round win over Oskar Lukasiak at the World Championship with three 100+ checkouts

Taylor's failed drugs test at the World Championship resulted in a six-month suspension until June 18, as well as a £1,275 fine in costs and the forfeiture of his £25,000 in prize money.

Taylor tested positive for cocaine and cannabis with the offence being his second which incurred a mandatory six-month ban under DRA rules.

"Accordingly, and taking into account all of the available evidence, the committee were satisfied that Mr Taylor's ingestion of both cocaine and cannabis occurred out of competition and was not following the commencement of the World Championship on 11th December 2025," the DRA statement read.

"Following on from this finding, the committee has determined that as this is Mr Taylor's second offence, then under these rules, he must serve a six month ban in line with 10.9 (a) and 10.9 (b) of UKAD Anti-Doping Rules 2021".

Taylor also lost his Tour Card as a result of the offence.

He had previously served a one-month ban in 2025 after failing a drugs test at the Players Championship Finals in November 2024. The ban was reduced from an initial two years after he agreed to undergo a UKAD-approved three-month substance abuse treatment programme.

Prakash Jiwa and Andy Jenkins both received hefty bans and were each made to pay costs of over £17,000 after being found guilty of match-fixing in the Modus Super Series from 2022-2023.

Sports.title: Massey-Ellis retires from officiating to take up new role with FA
Sports.content:
Assistant referee Sian Massey-Ellis has retired from officiating and will take up a new role with the Football Association.

Massey-Ellis will become the FA's Senior Manager - Women Referees from September, where she will support and develop female officials across the country and help provide a pathway into the elite game.

The 40-year-old became only the second female assistant referee to officiate in the Premier League when she made her top-flight debut in 2010 and has since worked on more than 150 Premier League matches.

Her career also included five Women's FA Cup finals, while she became the first female assistant referee appointed to the Community Shield. In 2021, Massey-Ellis became the first woman involved in a men's FA Cup final when she served as an assistant VAR, before also working as an AVAR at the 2025 Carabao Cup final.

On the international stage, Massey-Ellis officiated at four Women's European Championships and two Women's World Cups, as well as the 2018 Women's Champions League final. In 2019, she became the first English woman to officiate a men's European fixture when she worked as an assistant referee in the Europa League.

To the young girl who simply loved refereeing, we did it. Thank you, football.

Massey-Ellis, who received an MBE for services to football, said: "Although I am stepping away from the touchline, I am not stepping away from football.

"If my journey has helped change perceptions, open doors or inspire even one young person to believe they belong in the game, then I will consider that one of my greatest achievements.

"As I prepare for one final walk onto the pitch, I leave with nothing but gratitude. It has been the greatest honour to serve the game I love and represent English officiating."

Chief Refereeing Officer Howard Webb described Massey-Ellis as a "powerhouse" whose impact on female officiating "will be felt for years to come".

"Sian has done us proud time and time again - domestically and on the international stage, breaking multiple barriers and setting the standard for those coming through in her footsteps," Webb added.

Sports.title: The Hundred permutations: Who needs what to qualify?
Sports.content:
We are into crunch time in the 2026 edition of The Hundred, with knockout spots up for grabs in the men's and women's competitions. But who will claim them, and who needs what?

The men's and women's sides that finish first in their respective tables after the eight group games secure direct qualification to the finals at Lord's on Sunday August 16.

The teams coming second and third will meet in the eliminator at The Kia Oval on Friday August 14, with the winners of those matches then also making the final.

Here is the state of play as the league phase enters its final stages...

How points are scored in The Hundred? Win = four points

Tie/no result = two points

Defeat = no points

Men's competition

The Hundred - Men's standings Team Played Wins Losses No result/Tie Points Net run-rate Rockets 6 5 1 0 20 +0.893 MI London 6 4 2 0 16 +0.448 Brave 6 4 2 0 16 -0.537 Super Giants 6 3 3 0 12 +0.495 SunRisers 5 3 2 0 12 +0.348 Brave 6 2 4 0 8 +0.022 Spirit (E) 6 1 5 0 4 −0.458 Phoenix 5 1 4 0 4 -1.298

Barring the already-eliminated London Spirit, it is still wide open in the men's competition.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tom Curran appeared to clash with a few former England team-mates after hitting the match-winning runs for MI London that eliminated London Spirit

Trent Rockets moved one step closer towards qualification for the latter stages as they surged four points clear at the top of the table on 20 points with a fifth victory in six on Wednesday night.

Birmingham Phoenix are up against it, level with Spirit at the bottom of the table on four points but having played a game less.

They are still capable of getting to 16 points and giving themselves a chance of reaching the eliminator with three closing wins - the tally MI London and Welsh Fire in second and third, respectively, have accrued after six games.

It means, though, that Phoenix simply MUST win on Friday against SunRisers Leeds, or their tournament too will be ended early.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch as SunRisers Leeds hit the record highest total in The Hundred against London Spirit

SunRisers Leeds and Manchester Super Giants look to be the biggest threats to the top three, locked together on 12 points, albeit Super Giants have played a game more.

Things are looking pretty bleak, meanwhile, for Southern Brave, on eight points after six games. They will likely have to win out and have other results go their way to be in with a sniff of qualification.

What is net run-rate? This is used to separate teams on the same number of points during a league format, in the way that goal difference does in football.

Net run-rate in The Hundred is the average runs scored by a team over 100 balls in each game minus the average runs scored against them over 100 balls in each game.

Women's competition

The top two in the women's competition are all but confirmed, with table-toppers Trent Rockets joined on 20 points by Southern Brave after six games.

Only Manchester Super Giants, in third on 14 points, are capable of overhauling either team's tally, while Welsh Fire and SunRisers Leeds are able to match that 20-point total by winning out.

Fire are currently fourth on 12 points and SunRisers fifth on eight, but having played a game less.

They face off on Sunday, meaning they will take points off each other in some way or form, so the Monday meeting between Rockets and Brave will likely be a battle for top spot, the winner progressing straight through to the final and avoiding the eliminator.

MI London kept their tournament alive when finally registering their first win on Thursday night against capital-city rivals London Spirit, a result that sees the teams level on six points after six games.

It means both must now win their remaining two matches, and have other results go their way, to even be in with a sniff of qualification for the eliminator.

Birmingham Phoenix are in a similarly bleak position stuck on six points, albeit with three games remaining, allowing them a tiny bit more room to manoeuvre over the closing stages.

Sports.title: Gallagher ready to show what he can do under De Zerbi at Spurs
Sports.content:
Timing in sport often defines a career and for Conor Gallagher and Tottenham, it probably could not have been worse.

He arrived at Spurs last January from Atletico Madrid for £35m and within weeks boss Thomas Frank had been replaced by Igor Tudor, who by Gallagher's own admission "wasn't having me" as a player as the club battled relegation.

They were tough times at Spurs and Gallagher could not see a way out of the slump.

However, the arrival of Roberto De Zerbi as head coach began to change everything. Tottenham avoided relegation to the Championship and Gallagher played his part, although in an emotional interview on the final day he admitted he had not been able to show fans what he was really about.

Gallagher believes now is the time to really start his Spurs story.

"It's time to kick on to try and show the fans what I can do," he told Sky Sports. "I want to be at my best to help the club go to where we should be.

"Every footballer has things going on and hard, tough times. It's just life. Everyone has problems and I'm just really happy that we came out of it and I ended the season well.

"Hopefully this is only the start of my Spurs career."

Gallagher's praise for De Zerbi

Image: Gallagher struggled before Roberto De Zerbi's arrival at Spurs

It feels a very different Gallagher sitting in the sunshine a few weeks out from the start of a new season.

Much of that is down to De Zerbi, who joined Spurs in March.

Gallagher said: "With me, it was just a confidence thing mainly and slightly a physical thing, which you get from just playing more games. I wasn't really used to that at that time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player De Zerbi admitted he is not sure whether Richarlison or Cristian Romero will remain Tottenham players come the start of the season

"The manager gave me a bit of my confidence back and I started playing more consistent minutes on the pitch.

"A lot of credit to the manager but for him, it's only the start also."

De Zerbi's demanding reputation and intensity are clear to see but Gallagher admits he was still a little daunted during their first meeting.

He added: "He was a bit scary, especially the first time meeting him, but after a while it's not like that.

Image: De Zerbi (R) and Gallagher attend a press conference in pre-season

"He's actually a really nice man but you know you can't mess around. You've got to do the right things and train right and give 100 per cent.

"As a coach, he's one of those coaches that you want to do well for. He shows a lot of belief in his players. He instils that confidence in the players. He makes you want to do your best for him and work as hard as you can.

"He always said, 'if you listen to me and stick with me and believe me, then we'll be fine'. And that was when we were in the situation we were last season.

"So he had full belief in himself and he kind of needs everyone on board with him for it to work. And everyone is and does just by the way he is."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp backs his former club to have a 'strong season' after behaving like a 'big club' in the transfer window

That belief is reflected in the way De Zerbi talks about Gallagher.

In Sydney during pre-season, the Spurs boss said, when Gallagher is at his best, it is like Tottenham have an extra player - a remarkable turnaround from a player who a few months ago was struggling for minutes.

Gallagher smiles. "It's nice. I always try and give my best whenever I'm on the pitch. I feel like it should be my prime kind of years. I've kind of been at a load of teams already and had amazing experiences and loved every club I played for at that time.

"So now I just want to have a bigger role and try and lead by example, on and off the pitch."

'De Zerbi wants to dominate everything'

Image: Gallagher and Spurs' new signing Sandro Tonali in pre-season action

Tottenham have backed De Zerbi heavily this summer, getting much of their business done early.

Almost £200m has been spent on new players - all with Premier League experience - and the early arrivals have given Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson a chance to create some chemistry in the squad.

For De Zerbi, building relationships is as important as building a team, and Gallagher says he loves a bit of team bonding.

He said: "We've got a really good group of people and footballers. The gaffer loves it - a team dinner and a few drinks and a bonding night out."

It is all part of what De Zerbi's vision for the club is and, perhaps, I suggest to Gallagher, we got a glimpse of it in one of their pre-season games with Chelsea - one of Spurs' biggest rivals and the midfielder's former club - which was pretty fiery.

Gallagher's tackle committed on Dario Essugo - too committed thought some - prompts him to hold his head in his hands and laugh.

"That tackle was not as bad as what it looked, to be fair," he said. "I had no intention of hurting anyone."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pre-season friendly highlights between Chelsea and Tottenham. Credit: SpursPlay

He added: "De Zerbi wants to dominate everything. He wants to have the ball and control games.

"He wants us to obviously win every game, like any manager would. But he believes we can dominate any team we play against if we play the right way and with the right personality."

Where that can take Tottenham this season will be fascinating after two 17th-placed finishes.

What will also be interesting is to see what Gallagher does next. "It feels perfect here," he finishes.

Perhaps now really is his time at Spurs.
