Sports.title: I could have been Arsenal Invincible but rejected transfer out of love for Tottenham
Sports.content:
I could have been Arsenal Invincible but rejected transfer out of love for Tottenham

In another universe, Darren Ambrose can count himself as a part of Premier League history.

With Ipswich Town falling into administration in early 2003, the club needed an immediate injection of funds and Ambrose was deemed as the man to provide it.

3 Ambrose had quite the career choice to make when he left Ipswich Credit: talkSPORT

Ambrose, who was an England Under-21 international at the time, had interest from some of the Premier League's heavy hitters, including Arsenal.

However, it was Newcastle who landed Ambrose in March 2003, with the deal allowed to fall outside of the traditional January transfer window due to the Tractor Boys' perilous financial situation.

Although Ambrose claimed it was the pulling power of Sir Bobby Robson, who was in charge of the Magpies at the time, the midfielder conceded his love for Tottenham had a small part to play in his choice of where to go next.

Ambrose's sliding doors moment

"I had an opportunity to go to Arsenal. Or, I had an opportunity to talk to Arsenal before I went to Newcastle," Ambrose revealed on the Sports Bar.

"I was highly thought-of as a kid, so I had options.

"When I spoke to Newcastle, Sir Bobby Robson. I had a message off Arsenal saying, 'Come and speak to us.'

"The Spurs side of me was probably a little bit involved in that (decision). But Darren Bent played for Tottenham and is a huge Arsenal fan, we know that.

"It (club rivalries) doesn't really come into contention as a player. It was more Sir Bobby Robson in that situation."

Ambrose made just one appearance for the Magpies in what was left of the 2002/03 campaign, before featuring 37 times across all competitions in the next term.

Gunner make history

However, had Ambrose ended up at Arsenal, he would have been a member of their Invincibles squad.

3 The Gunners won 26 and drew 12 of their 38 games in the 03/04 Premier League season Credit: Getty

The Gunners' 2003/04 season is enshrined in history as they became the first Premier League club to remain unbeaten across all 38 fixtures.

No other club has managed to repeat the feat, underlining just how incredible Arsenal's achievement was.

Unfortunately for Ambrose, he struggled to hold down a regular spot in Newcastle's starting line-up and moved to Charlton in July 2005.

Ambrose spent four seasons at The Valley before joining Crystal Palace in the summer of 2009.

Lightning strikes twice?

The midfielder then had a serious case of deja vu when, at the end of his time with the Eagles in July 2012, he was once again faced with the prospect of going against his heart.

This time, it was Palace's bitter rivals Brighton.

3 Ambrose made over 120 appearances for Palace but would've been public enemy No.1 had he joined Brighton

"There was a chance (to join Brighton) before Birmingham," Ambrose said.

"I said no, I went to Birmingham and ended my career. It went downhill from there!"

Ambrose's stint with the Blues was beset by injuries as he made just 10 appearances before joining Greek side Apolon Smyrnis on loan.

A return to Ipswich followed before Ambrose moved to Colchester United in August 2015, which proved to be the final stop of his professional career.

Sports.title: How many teams will qualify for the Championship play-offs this season with new format?
Sports.content:
How many teams will qualify for the Championship play-offs this season with new format?

EFL football is back and there is already focus on the promotion race.

The English second-tier is considered as one of the toughest leagues in the sport and boasts the reward of Premier League riches for three clubs.

3 Hull were last season's Championship play-off winners Credit: Getty

Whilst there are heated races for champion and runners-up status, the play-offs deliver drama and excitement in abundance.

Finishing third to sixth has offered teams the opportunity to battle for promotion to the top flight.

However, the 2026/27 season will bring an expanded play-off format, adding further unpredictability to the Championship.

The English Football League (EFL) announced the new Championship-specific plans in March, and you can read how it will all work below.

How many teams qualify for the play-offs?

The number of qualified teams for this season's play-offs and beyond will increase from four to SIX.

First and second will remain as the only two automatic spots for the Championship teams.

Normally, the teams that finish from third to sixth are automatically into the play-off semi-finals.

However, from this season onwards, this is only the case for third and fourth.

Teams that finish fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth will compete in the new eliminator matches.

Fifth will face eighth whilst sixth meet seventh in one-off fixtures to decide who competes in the semi-finals with third and fourth.

3 There will be six teams competing for play-off glory this season Credit: AFP

The semi-final ties are played over two legs so, when adding the final, there will be a total of seven play-off matches.

And of course, whoever wins the showpiece at Wembley Stadium will join first and second in the 2027/28 Premier League campaign.

Championship on talkSPORT talkSPORT will bring you unmatched live and exclusive coverage of the Championship's opening weekend. Just look at what we've got in store! FRIDAY 14th AUGUST Wolves v Blackburn - 8pm (talkSPORT) SATURDAY 15th AUGUST Bolton v Preston - 12.30pm (talkSPORT)

Around the Grounds with Adrian Durham - 2.30pm (talkSPORT)

Middlesbrough v Lincoln - 3pm (talkSPORT 2)

Sheffield United v Birmingham - 5.30pm (talkSPORT 2) SUNDAY 16th AUGUST Watford v Southampton - 1.30pm (talkSPORT 2)

Burnley v West Ham - 4pm (talkSPORT 2) MONDAY 17th AUGUST Cardiff v Wrexham - 8pm (talkSPORT 2)

Who is in the running for promotion?

West Ham United, Burnley and Wolves will all be favourites to earn an instant return to the Premier League as the three relegated sides.

Middlesbrough will also be hopeful of earning promotion to avenge their play-off final defeat to Hull City in May.

Boro actually lost their semi-final against Southampton, but reached the final after the Saints were kicked out for spying on opponents.

Southampton will have their own wrongs to right as they look to seal a Premier League return.

3 Middlesbrough will be eyeing another run to the play-off final Credit: Getty

Thanks to their American owners, Birmingham City and Wrexham are other clubs who will look to reach the play-offs at the very least.

That would leave one final spot, with Norwich City, Sheffield United and Millwall among the sides set to be right in the mix.

How would the new format have looked last season?

Coventry City were crowned as Championship winners whilst Ipswich Town finished as runners-up, meaning automatic promotion.

Millwall and Southampton were the respective third and fourth-placed teams, so they would be in the play-off semi-finals.

Middlesbrough and Hull would have been joined by Wrexham and Derby in the eliminators.

Middlesbrough v Derby and Hull v Wrexham would have been the two fixtures.

Sports.title: Chris Smalling searching for new club aged 36 as title winner reveals widespread interest
Sports.content:
Chris Smalling searching for new club aged 36 as title winner reveals widespread interest

Chris Smalling will only join a new club if it's 'the right kind of project' as he plots what could be the final act of his playing career.

Smalling is a free agent and back in the UK having departed Saudi club Al-Fayha, where he made 67 appearances.

3 Smalling is eyeing up the next stop in his playing career Credit: AFP

Speaking exclusively on talkSPORT Breakfast, the 36-year-old revealed clubs from a variety of leagues have made their pitch to sign him.

However, he is in no immediate rush to put pen to paper.

"At the minute, there's conversations ongoing," Smalling said.

"I've had some offers, so I feel like I'm in a good position.

"But at my stage in my career, it's now about being patient, making sure it's the right kind of project that fits everything in terms of my role in the team and what I can bring on and off the pitch.

"I'm in a nice position and just kind of seeing where that lies over the next couple of weeks."

All the Small things

Whoever lands Smalling will get one of the most experienced centre-backs available.

The 36-year-old has over 580 appearances to his name at club level, the bulk of which were made representing Manchester United.

Smalling was on the Red Devils' books for nine years, where he won two Premier League titles, the FA Cup, a League Cup and the Europa League.

Plenty has happened at Old Trafford since Smalling departed in August 2019, with the club now managed by one of his former teammates, Michael Carrick.

3 Smalling made over 300 appearances in total for the Red Devils Credit: Getty - Contributor

The midfielder initially returned to his old stomping ground as interim boss until the end of the 2025/26 campaign following Ruben Amorim's sacking.

However, Carrick turned around United's fortunes completely and guided them to a third-place finish, securing a return to Champions League football.

The remarkable run of results prompted United to hand Carrick the managerial reins on a two-year deal and he has already made his stamp on the squad, with Youri Tielemans joining from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos from Chelsea for a combined £85million.

Mic drop

Given the positive atmosphere surrounding the club since Carrick's return, Smalling believes there is 'no one better steering that ship' than his former teammate.

"I'm so happy to see Carra just thriving," Smalling said.

"Having played with him, you know what kind of character he is. He's composed and intelligent and he's bringing that into one of the biggest jobs in world football.

3 Carrick has lost only twice since returning to United as manager Credit: Getty

"I think the run they had at the end of last season, they were number one in points taken.

"For him to have a full pre-season and bring in whoever he likes in terms of players and have that belief, there's no-one better steering that ship."

Sports.title: Rangers boss given sack warning and branded ‘Russell Martin in disguise’ during furious rant
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes could suffer a similar fate to Russell Martin at Rangers and be dismissed as manager before Halloween.

That is the concern of one fan after their 2-1 defeat against Jagiellonia Bialystok, which put their Europa League qualification in jeopardy.

4 Rangers are yet to win under McInnes this season Credit: Getty

Rangers led during their third qualifying round first leg in Poland on Thursday night, but now find themselves with a mountain to climb in the reverse fixture next week to reach the play-off.

McInnes, who guided Hearts to second in the Scottish Premiership last season, remains without a win from two matches since joining at the beginning of June.

Speaking afterwards, he drew parallels between this Rangers side and that of the previous campaign by seemingly calling them out, saying: "We stopped doing what was working for us.

"We make two mistakes for the two goals. I'm not going to watch us all season lose the ball on the edge of their box and it ends up in a chance for the opposition.

"We need to be far more concentrated, far more focused, far more aggressive, far more talkative and organised to stop these types of things happening.

"We've seen a lot tonight of what I thought Rangers were last season. I thought they gave up too many chances, and gave teams too much encouragement."

Fan fury

However, Rangers fan Mal called The Sports Bar on talkSPORT to warn McInnes that he could be heading down the same road as former boss Martin, who was sacked just four months after taking the job.

"McInnes, is he Russell Martin in disguise?" he asked. "How dare Russell Martin, at the start of last year, call out a few players in the first few games?

"I was the one to give the exclusive to talkSPORT, and to the BBC, calling him out before Halloween. Not an OBE, not a CBE, but an OBH - out before Halloween.

"Surely it's too early for me to call out McInnes right now? Because I'm telling you, for him to call out the whole Rangers team in that interview, saying that Rangers played like the same team as last season... how dare he?

4 McInnes has been touted to follow in the ill-fated footsteps of Martin Credit: Getty

"All the signings that we've had, he's had the opportunity to work with the players and to obviously play some sort of attacking football, and some sort of coherence with the players.

"And then calls out the whole team to say, 'Rangers look like the same team as last season'. Who does he think he is? Seriously, this is not going to last.

"If we get beaten on Sunday against Hibs (Hibernian), I'm telling you right now, he's not going to last. I don't want to be giving him an OBH, the same as Russell Martin."

Rangers were held to a 1-1 draw by Dundee United in their first league match last Friday in a performance that left Mal far from impressed.

"It was basic football," he said. "They can't even read a pass to another player without another player intercepting it from the other team.

"We're talking basic football skills here, and I am embarrassed to say it's not going to go well this year."

4 McInnes has been tipped to be in danger of the sack before Halloween Credit: Getty

Mal added: "It's absolutely disgusting to start thinking about an OBH for the manager, it's terrible...

"You're the manager. You sort it out and develop that team. I mean, does he know who the starting XI is right now? No chance, absolutely no chance."

Darren Ambrose then claimed that the Rangers squad will stop playing for McInnes if he continues to call them out publicly, and feared it won't be long until this happens.

"That went against the manager last year, Russell Martin, to start calling out individual players," Mal explained.

"Then obviously there was a lot behind the scenes with (Nicolas) Raskin (dropped by Martin). The supporters supported Raskin and what he was trying to do.

"Other managers have had their challenges with certain players, but you don't call out the whole team and if Rangers don't get European football after the money that they've spent, I'm sorry, it's going to be a long season."

What happened to Martin at Rangers?

Within weeks of his appointment as head coach in June 2025, Martin found himself on the wrong side of Rangers fans after they drew 1-1 with Motherwell in their league opener last season.

He then delivered a scathing post-match assessment, in which he said they were lucky to get a point and called for some of the players to 'drop their ego'.

4 Martin had a dismal spell at Rangers last season Credit: Getty

Rangers failed to win their opening two league matches for the first time since 1989, and Martin later earned his first Scottish Premiership victory at the sixth time of asking.

Alongside a poor European campaign, where they were thrashed 9-1 on aggregate by Club Brugge in the Champions League qualifiers, the 1-1 draw at Falkirk on October 5 spelled the end of Martin's tenure.

He needed police protection when leaving the stadium as angry Rangers fans waited by the team coach to protest against him.

Rangers announced his dismissal later in the day and eventually finished third in the Scottish Premiership.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero strikes personal terms as Tottenham prepare for £8million transfer hit
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero has agreed personal terms to join Atletico Madrid, talkSPORT understands.

The Tottenham captain has long been tipped for a summer exit from north London, having previously held talks with Inter Milan over a move.

5 Cristian Romero's time at Spurs looks to be up Credit: Getty

More recently, Romero was linked with a shock switch to Spurs' bitter rivals Arsenal, but any chance of this now looks to have ended.

The Argentine defender is now set to join up with compatriot Diego Simeone at Atletico, in a move which will bring to an end his five-year stay at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

So long, farewell?

Romero joined Spurs on loan from Italian outfit Atalanta in August 2021, which was later made permanent for £43million.

Now, Tottenham are prepared to take a loss on the centre-back, with the club ready to sell for £35m.

Spurs have already signed centre-backs Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer, with Micky van de Ven in positive talks over a new five-year deal.

This left Romero free to leave the club, despite penning a contract extension through to 2029 last August.

His seemingly imminent exit comes after he drew criticism from fans for his conduct and ill-discipline last season.

Romero was sent off twice in 23 league appearances, as well as receiving ten yellow cards as Spurs narrowly avoided relegation.

The 2022 World Cup winner also became embroiled in a storm in May when it was reported that he was to miss Tottenham's crucial final game of the season in favour of a return to his homeland to watch formative club Belgrano.

With Spurs at risk of relegation and Romero getting wind of fan disgruntlement, he later changed his mind and instead was on hand to support his teammates in their quest for survival.

5 Romero now looks set to join Diego Simeone and his Argentine contingent at Atletico Madrid

5 The Argentine seeing red became a frustratingly familiar sight for Spurs fans in recent seasons Credit: Getty

'Get rid of him'

As Romero closes in on a move away from north London, talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara had no qualms about Tottenham losing their captain.

Discussing the defender's links with Arsenal on Friday morning, the Sport Bar host and former Spurs player insisted the club would be better off without him, and claimed their new arrivals are better options.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, O'Hara said: “Get rid of him. I've heard there’s Arsenal chat about him - get rid of him.

“He was a liability for us last season. We’ve finished 17th in the last two seasons - he was the captain. He didn't want to be there on the last day. It was only because he got told that he had to come back that he ended up coming back.

“So get rid of him. We've got better players now. He's a liability.

“Van de Ven - make him captain. He's a player that you want in your side. You got Senesi, Van Hecke. Romero isn't even going to play.”

5 Jan Paul van Hecke looks set to fill Romero's boots after his £52million arrival from Brighton Credit: Getty

5 Romero helped Argentina through to a second consecutive World Cup final this summer, but his best form has often eluded him at Spurs Credit: Getty

After two disappointing league campaigns, Tottenham have set about kickstarting a new era under Roberto De Zerbi this summer.

Spurs have splashed the cash in a bid to rebuild, spending £237m in total which includes twice breaking their club transfer record - first to sign Mateus Fernandes and then Sandro Tonali from West Ham and Newcastle.

And O'Hara insisted there is no place for Romero in De Zerbi's new-look team, even after playing a central role in Argentina's run to the World Cup final.

Continuing to blast him, he added: “I'm happy to see the back of him.

"We need a new era under De Zerbi and it looks like he's putting a right good team together. We'll see what happens, but it looks like we've got a right good team and the players seem to like him.

“But Romero isn’t part of it. Get rid of him, get as much as we can."

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Vinicius Jr alternatives: Dream target revealed as Premier League winger discussed
Sports.content:
Arsenal are interested in signing Julian Alvarez, Iliman Ndiaye or Bradley Barcola after missing out on Vinicius Junior, talkSPORT understands.

After a high-profile contract saga, the Gunners' hopes of signing Vinicius Jr have now officially ended as Real Madrid confirmed the Brazilian superstar had signed a new six-year deal with the club.

6 Vinicius Jr has now agreed to extend his eight-year stay at Real Madrid Credit: Getty

The 26-year-old was heavily linked with a summer departure to the Emirates, amid reports of a stand-off over a new contract.

Before signing his latest deal, Vinicius had only a year left on his Los Blancos contract.

talkSPORT reported last week that Arsenal were weighing up an approach for the winger, though they were believed to have always viewed him as an option rather than their top target.

And any hopes of a blockbuster move ended on Thursday night, when Vinicius finally put pen to paper on a new long-term contract at the Santiago Bernabeu.

6 This is how all three players matched up last season

Back to the drawing board

After seeing their dreams of signing Vinicius go up in smoke, Arsenal will now begin their search for alternative attacking targets.

Mikel Arteta has been keen to strengthen at left-wing this summer, already signing Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge after Leandro Trossard left to join Besiktas.

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs provided the latest on their next move on Transfer Insiders, and he revealed that Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez is high up on the Gunners' list.

Arsenal have previously been linked with the Argentina forward, who has publicly informed Atletico that he wants to be sold, with Barcelona his preferred destination despite reaching a standoff with their LaLiga rivals after a failed £86million bid.

Jacobs told talkSPORT: “Arsenal are now still going to add some form of either left-sided or versatile attacker.

“Not all the profiles are identical to Vinicius Junior, but Julian Alvarez is one possibility if Atleti decide to sell.

6 Julian Alvarez has a £432m release clause in his Atletico Madrid contract Credit: Getty

6 Mikel Arteta and Arsenal were handed a reality check in their pursuit of Vinicius Jr Credit: Getty

"We know they'd prefer to keep. Barcelona would love Julian Alvarez as well but Atleti may prefer, if they realise the player wants to leave, to sell outside of La Liga. So he's a dream target."

Do or Ndiaye?

Aside from Alvarez, Jacobs then suggested Arsenal could look to Premier League rivals Everton, with Iliman Ndiaye another option.

talkSPORT understands the Senegal international is not a high priority for the Gunners, although he would appear open to a move away, having turned down a new contract offer at the Toffees earlier this summer.

Ndiaye has impressed since moving to Merseyside in 2024, and also has interest from Manchester United and Al Hilal, with the Saudi outfit currently pushing for his signature.

Jacobs continued: “Iliman Ndiaye has been discussed as well and there'll be other options too. Some will say Bradley Barcola."

Barcola update

Moving on to another of this summer's biggest transfer stories, Jacobs insisted Paris Saint-Germain forward Barcola remains an option for Arsenal.

6 Ndiaye scored six goals and provided three assists in 32 league appearances for Everton last term Credit: Getty

6 Bradley Barcola's future remains up in the air Credit: Getty

talkSPORT has previously revealed the France forward would like to join Liverpool - who are readying a €100million (around £85m) offer, plus add-ons for the star - with Arsenal also known admirers.

But with the Reds' figure falling significantly short of PSG's starting valuation of €170m (around £145m), Jacobs insisted they could still land Barcola's signature by outbidding their league rivals.

Jacobs added: “If Arsenal want Bradley Barcola their tactic has to be to gazump Liverpool, because the player wants Liverpool.

"But PSG want €170million - so Arsenal would have to overpay and hope that Liverpool back off. But he's a possibility too.

“So Arsenal are still going to be busy between now and the end of the window.”

Sports.title: Dele Alli can still make English football return as Championship transfer mooted
Sports.content:
Former Salford boss Karl Robinson believes Dele Alli is 'still a talent' but cannot afford to waste another opportunity.

Alli has not appeared in a competitive fixture since March last year, although that ended in despair.

3 Alli joined Como on a six-month deal with the option of an extra 12 months, but it didn't go to plan Credit: Getty

Making his comeback for Como after nearly 750 days in the cold, Alli came on in the 81st minute but was sent off less than 10 minutes later.

It proved to be his only appearance for Cesc Fabregas' side.

But Alli is now attempting to get his career back on track once again, with reports claiming he is training at Championship side West Ham United.

And Robinson, who bumped into Alli in Marbella whilst the latter was put through his paces during a pre-season camp, believes the 37-time England international still has plenty to give.

However, Robinson was quick to warn that given Alli's time away from football, he cannot be expected to return to the levels he's previously shown straight away.

The 'tell-tale sign' whether Alli is ready to return

"I had about an hour just chatting to him, just bumped into him really," Robinson told Alan Brazil and Ray Parlour on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"We spoke just about football in general, about how well he feels and how he wants to get himself back playing and how he seeks an opportunity.

"I think the problem you have in the modern world is social media governs an awful lot of our perception of them as a human being, first and foremost. We forget the fact he was and still is a talent.

"I think being away from football for so long, he was saying before about a pre-season, being away from a training ground for six weeks, it can be difficult to come back in and hit the ground running.

"Somebody who's not played competitive football for probably over 12 months, that's going to be the tell-tale sign. When he goes back over that white line with an actual match shirt, to see where he's actually at."

3 Robinson believes Alli can still succeed, but needs to have the right attitude Credit: Getty

Even though Alli may still have magic in his feet, Robinson acknowledged the attacking midfielder is very much in last chance saloon territory.

Robinson: It's all down to Alli now

He believes West Ham are fully aware of Alli's enduring talent and it is not too late for the ex-Tottenham man to revive his career in the Championship.

"Now, he's had multiple chances to get himself back playing, so you can't blame everybody else," Robinson continued.

"You've got to look at yourself, first and foremost.

"And at the end of the day, if he is given this opportunity and he goes in to West Ham and hits the ground running, they know they're going to have such a talented footballer. But that's down to him. It's not down to anybody else now.

"I think it's about him just putting his boots back on and doing something that he loves."

3 Alli made nearly 270 appearances for Spurs, scoring 67 goals Credit: AFP

Should Alli be offered a deal at West Ham, it would mark the first time he has appeared in the Championship following the Hammers' relegation from the top flight.

He began his career with MK Dons in League One before joining Tottenham in February 2015.

Alli spent six-and-a-half years in north London before he joined Everton.

But since he moved to the Toffees, Alli has played a total of 29 competitive fixtures in four-and-a-half years.

The Hammers begin their 2026/27 season on Saturday with a Carabao Cup first round fixture against Portsmouth, with talkSPORT providing live coverage from 1pm.

Sports.title: Ivan Toney left shocked as England striker charged with assault after incident at Soho nightclub
Sports.content:
Ivan Toney left shocked as England striker charged with assault after incident at Soho nightclub

England striker Ivan Toney has been charged with assault following an incident in London last December.

A statement from the Met Police read: "Ivan Toney, 30, of Northampton, was charged on Thursday, 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.

2 Toney will appear in court in September Credit: Getty

"He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday, 24 September.

"The charge relates to an assault, which reportedly took place on 6 December 2025 at a nightclub on Wardour Street, W1."

Following the Met Police's statement, a spokesperson on behalf of Ivan Toney said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."

What is alleged to have happened at the Soho nightclub?

Toney is alleged to have headbutted a person at a venue in Soho.

According to reports, the incident was sparked by a fan who grabbed the England international for a photo, only to be pushed away.

After Toney repeatedly requested the man to get off of him, he allegedly dished out a headbutt.

Five officers were reportedly dispatched to the venue to deal with the situation.

The man who was headbutted by Toney got taken to a local hospital in an ambulance.

However, his injuries were not believed to be life-changing or life-threatening.

Toney was arrested at the scene on suspicion of two counts of assault and one count of affray.

2 The incident did not prevent Toney from playing games for club side Al-Ahli Credit: Getty

The 30-year-old was charged by police weeks after he participated in the World Cup for England.

Toney featured just twice for the Three Lions as they finished the tournament with a bronze medal.

He came off the bench in the dying stages of England's semi-final loss to Argentina as Thomas Tuchel's side desperately searched for a late equaliser.

Toney was then handed a starting berth for the third-place play-off against France, which ended in a 6-4 victory for the Three Lions.

The 30-year-old was drafted in to the England squad for the World Cup after he scored an impressive 42 goals in 49 games for Al-Ahli during the 2025/26 season.

Toney's eye-catching campaign at club level was bookended by Al-Ahli winning the AFC Champions League Elite for a second consecutive season.

Sports.title: Roy Keane and Micah Richards dress up as traditional Victorian gentlemen, perform pigskin keepy-uppies and enjoy a day out at the terraces as they turn back the clock for Sky Bet's new 'Game's Back' advert
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roy Keane and Micah Richards have embraced football's roots by dressing as Victorian gentlemen for Sky Bet's latest 'Game's Back' campaign.

Revisiting football's earliest days ahead of the new Premier League season, the popular Sky Sports punditry duo donned period costumes as they took in the action from the terraces and showed off their keepy-uppy skills with a traditional pigskin ball.

Sky Bet's new advert, which officially launched on August 7, plays on the familiar 'game's gone' phrase often used by supporters looking back nostalgically at how the sport has changed over the years, from players refusing to celebrate against former clubs to the introduction of VAR.

The advert begins with Keane and Richard sitting on the sofa watching modern-day football, before the Manchester United legend complains that the 'game's gone' over a five-minute VAR decision.

The punditry duo then take a trip through different eras of football to discover that supporters were always questioning how the game was evolving.

Transported first to 1965, the pair complained about the introduction of the substitutions law before heading further back in time to 1891 to learn how fans moaned when nets were first attached to goalposts.

Popular punditry duo Roy Keane and Micah Richards have embraced football's roots by dressing as Victorian gentlemen for Sky Bet's latest 'Game's Back' campaign

Richards and Keane also showed off their keepy-uppy skills with a traditional pigskin ball

In one light-hearted moment, Richards shushes his famously fiery punditry partner while the pair watch on from the stands, poking fun at Keane's well-known habit of questioning changes in the modern game.

Sky Bet also shared behind-the-scenes footage of Keane and Richards shooting the advert, which showed off the duo's chemistry.

Keane said: 'One thing about football history is that people have always questioned changes to the game, but it's funny looking back at some of the things we'd never want to lose now.

'We had good fun bringing those moments to life.'

Richards added: 'Football fans love a debate and that's never going to change'.

'Game's Gone is a phrase that has engrained itself in football culture and beyond,' said Harry Phillips, Sky Bet Marketing Director.

'Yet even though we all love to moan about the game, it's never been more universally popular and when push comes to shove, it's the incredible moments of football culture, both on and off the pitch that keeps us coming back.

Sky Bet's new campaign plays on the familiar 'the game's gone' phrase often used by supporters looking back nostalgically at how the sport has changed over the years

'We believe football always has and always will create moments no fan can resist. And at Sky Bet, we champion those iconic moments of football and fandom by giving our customers more ways to get in on the action.'

The new Premier League season kicks off with champions Arsenal hosting newly-promoted Coventry City on Friday, August 21.

Sports.title: Top football executive linked with replacing Gianni Infantino reports FIFA president to Ethics Committee - following failed plan to sell the World Cup, overturning of Florian Balogun's suspension and award of Peace Prize to President Trump
Sports.content:
Norwegian FA president Lise Klaveness will report Gianni Infantino to FIFA's Ethics Committee as European football intensifies pressure on the FIFA president.

UEFA have already pledged to boycott FIFA tournaments so long as Infantino remains FIFA president.

And the head of the Norwegian FA, Klaveness - who has been mooted as a potential successor to Infantino - endorsed that position after their monthly board meeting. Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter is among those advocating for Klaveness to succeed Infantino.

The 45-year-old former lawyer will also submit a complaint to the FIFA Ethics Committee, which has the power to impose bans from football.

The complaint will not only challenge the proposed sale of a £3.1billion stake in the World Cup to private investors, but also the decision to award an ad hoc FIFA Peace Prize to President Donald Trump and the suspension of Florian Balogun's red card at the World Cup following alleged political pressure from Trump.

‘The board believes that we do not have confidence in Gianni Infantino. We did not have that in the last election and we do not have it now,’ Klaveness said.

‘There is no going back for Gianni Infantino. The international football community is very divided, and we must unite now.

Lise Klaveness has long been an opponent of Gianni Infantino

Klaveness spoke to reporters on Friday to explain the decisions taken at the Norwegian FA's monthly board meeting

Europe have upped the pressure on Infantino, with UEFA vowing to boycott FIFA competitions so long as he remains in post

‘We will ask the FIFA president to resign now. There is no doubt about it: there is a deep crisis in international football cooperation.

‘Irreversible transgressions have occurred,’ she added on the decision to complain to the ethics committee.

‘We have reached a situation where extraordinary measures are needed to create lasting change.’

UEFA are leading the charge to dethrone Infantino as FIFA president. However, the Swiss football administrator appears to retain support from Africa, South America and Asia - which is enough to fend off any leadership challenge.

Meanwhile, Mexico have broken ranks from CONCACAF's opposition to Infantino, reaffirming their confidence in the FIFA leadership.

UEFA's current refusal to play in FIFA competitions will cause the governing body significant commercial problems, potentially prompting Infantino to reconsider his position at the top of world football.

But the FIFA president has shown no sign of relenting thus far after being supported by the governing body's hierarchy on Wednesday.

Sports.title: Man City reject £40m bid from Barcelona for Rodri as Catalans look to pip bitter rivals Real Madrid to land Spain captain in bitter blow to Jose Mourinho's title hopes
Sports.content:
Man City reject £40m bid from Barcelona for Rodri as Catalans look to pip bitter rivals Real Madrid to land Spain captain in bitter blow to Jose Mourinho's title hopes

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City will demand upwards of £60million if Barcelona are to complete a sensational move for Rodri this summer.

Spain’s World Cup-winning captain has agreed terms with the Catalans ahead of the new season and is seeking a fresh challenge.

Barca instigated talks between the clubs and are understood to have had a derisory bid of nearly £40m rejected.

City have a history of allowing unhappy players to leave should the club’s valuation be met - and are standing firm in talks.

Rodri had been in negotiations with Real Madrid but communicated to them earlier in the week that Barca represented his preferred destination and has agreed personal terms.

While they are working on a transfer worth more than £80m for Lille teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi, City sources indicated that they are ready to land an experienced replacement for Rodri were he to depart.

Barcelona have begun talks with Manchester City over a move for Spain's World Cup winning captain Rodri

Man City are set to demand upwards of £60m if Barcelona are to seal the sensational move

The 2024 Ballon d’Or winner had remained coy over his future while away on international duty but is believed to have been open to a return to Spain once Pep Guardiola’s reign came to an end.

Guardiola had suggested last season that Rodri would not return to his best until the World Cup, as he battled various injury problems after the devastating ACL injury sustained two years ago.

Rodri underwent back surgery, revealed by Daily Mail Sport, immediately after lifting the World Cup.

City have kept an offer of a new contract on the table for the 30-year-old, whose deal expires next summer, and he is scheduled to link up with Enzo Maresca’s squad next week.

Sports.title: Aston Villa transfer briefing: Players fear losing Ezri Konsa, the latest on Nicolas Jackson move and UEFA stumbling block, Matteo Ruggeri deal close and wingers on radar after Johan Manzambi injury blow
Sports.content:
Aston Villa transfer briefing: Players fear losing Ezri Konsa, the latest on Nicolas Jackson move and UEFA stumbling block, Matteo Ruggeri deal close and wingers on radar after Johan Manzambi injury blow

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Aston Villa supporters could be forgiven for feeling angry and confused. Barely two months after one of the greatest nights in their history, they have lost two of their most important players and more are expected to follow.

Under Unai Emery, the club have finished seventh, fourth, sixth and fourth in the Premier League. They have qualified for the Champions League twice, won the Europa League and will have a chance to add the UEFA Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain in Salzburg on Wednesday.

Yet because of UEFA’s maddening financial rules that appear designed to help revenue-generating monsters like Chelsea and Manchester United and punish ambitious rivals like Villa, Emery finds himself without Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers heading into the new season, after they joined United and Chelsea respectively for a combined £152million.

Left back Lucas Digne is expected to join PSG and centre back Ezri Konsa – another pillar of Emery’s best teams – is a target for Arsenal, with Liverpool also monitoring the situation.

There are positives, however. Pound for pound, Emery is perhaps the best coach in the league and he is still at Villa. Champions League football will boost the balance sheet and plans to take the capacity of Villa Park to 50,000 are moving ahead. That should also deliver improved revenue and a bigger transfer warchest.

Yet football is always about the here and now and Daily Mail Sport looks at where Villa stand...

Under Unai Emery, Aston Villa have qualified for the Champions League twice, won the Europa League and will have a chance to add the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg on Wednesday

It's been a tough transfer window for Villa fans, with Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans (pictured) leaving the club for a combined £152million

Could there be more outgoings?

FIRST SIX FIXTURES Weds PSG (n, Super Cup) Aug 23 Brighton (a, PL) Aug 31 Arsenal (h, PL) Sep 5 Hull (a, PL) Sep 12 N Forest (h, PL) Sep 19 Tottenham (a, PL)

The big one to watch after Digne is Konsa. At 28, the England defender is probably at the peak of his market value and heading into the summer he was one of three principal targets for Arsenal, along with Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior.

Guimaraes is due to sign for £75million this week and while Vinicius is set to stay at Real Madrid, Arsenal have not given up hope of landing Konsa, who is needed while they handle injuries to William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Ben White.

The champions will have to do better than the original offer, though, which was believed to be little more than half of Villa’s £60million valuation. That did not go down well with co-owner Nassef Sawiris, but it is thought the Villa squad are becoming increasingly concerned about the possibility of Konsa departing.

There continues to be interest in Ollie Watkins, particularly from clubs in the Turkish top flight and the Saudi Pro League, though with so many experienced players already out of the door, it would be brave to let Watkins follow them. Though he turns 31 in December, Watkins has been Villa’s top scorer in every season since he joined the club in 2020, and is their leading all-time Premier League marksman.

It is a different matter with Tammy Abraham – another curious Villa transfer. Emery and his lieutenants pushed hard to sign Abraham for £18.2million from Besiktas in January yet it is thought that after only four starts Villa are prepared to let him go again, ideally on a permanent basis.

Earlier in the window, Villa were open to offers for Ross Barkley but with Tielemans leaving and Amadou Onana recovering from ACL damage, the former England man will not be placed on the market unless Villa can strengthen in midfield.

Arsenal are pushing to make Ezri Konsa (centre) the next big exit at Villa this summer

Tammy Abraham's £18.2million January move has not panned out and he could leave this summer

And what about incomings?

This is where it becomes tricky. Villa’s £54million club-record signing Johan Manzambi is not fit due to the knee injury he sustained playing for Switzerland at the World Cup.

Joao Gomes has made a promising start after joining for £38million from Wolves but more strength is needed in midfield, with Joao Palhinha still a target, though Bayern Munich would prefer to sell the Portugal international permanently.

Digne’s impending departure means another left back is needed, and Matteo Ruggeri could join from Atletico Madrid. The clubs have all but agreed terms on a deal worth about £15million for the Italian.

Alejandro Garnacho has joined on loan from Chelsea while Marseille winger Igor Paixao is another on Emery’s radar. Plenty of wingers have been observed this summer – from Ibrahim Mbaye to Harvey Barnes and Crysencio Summerville (who has since joined Al Hilal for £68million) – but Villa’s strong relationship with Chelsea helped get the Garnacho move over the line. Keep an eye on that for later in the window.

Then there is the striker. Ever since Emery joined the club, it feels like Villa have been looking for a forward to complement Watkins and ultimately succeed him. Jhon Duran had the talent to do so, but not the temperament. Donyell Malen did reasonably well when he played and his departure to Roma last January felt more of a financial move than a football one, given the constant pressure from UEFA rules. Quite simply, Abraham Part 2 simply has not worked.

Could Nicolas Jackson be the next one? At the moment, Villa are playing down interest in the Senegal forward. But Emery has always admired him since their days together at Villarreal and as highlighted, Villa and Chelsea have a good relationship.

But there's a hitch. UEFA rules state that permanent transfers between the same clubs within a 45-day period will be deemed ‘swaps’, which affects how profits can be recorded on balance sheets and stops any financial chicanery between teams.

The final day of the window is 41 days after Chelsea announced they had signed Rogers. Would that stop Villa signing Jackson? In such a frantic window, nothing can be ruled out – especially as players often sign for clubs some days before the official announcement.

Club-record signing Johan Manzambi is still recovering from the injury he suffered playing for Switzerland at the World Cup

Villa have all-but agreed a £15million deal with Atletico Madrid for Italian left back Matteo Ruggeri (left)

Emery's admiration for Nicolas Jackson dates back to their days together at Villarreal

How are Villa shaping up for the season?

Given the departure of Rogers, Villa need the Manzambi transfer to work and as things stand, the 20-year-old is unlikely to be fit for their Premier League opener at Brighton on August 23, and the early part of the season. Supporters are understandably alarmed at this summer's exodus while the squad are keen to see more high-level players join.

There is also a feeling, though, that Villa needed a refresh. The majority of last season’s squad had been at Villa throughout Emery’s four-year tenure and Villa knew they would have to sell this summer. Perhaps Emery would have preferred not to lose both Tielemans and Digne, who were key figures in the dressing room, but he will rarely stand in the way of a player who wishes to leave.

Roberto Olabe replaced Monchi as Villa’s transfer chief last September and this is his first summer window. Softly spoken and methodical, he is a much calmer figure than his predecessor and is a good counterbalance to the more instinctive Emery and director of football Damian Vidagany.

Villa started last season dreadfully, failing to score in any competition until September 16 and waiting until September 25 for their first win. It did not stop Emery’s men recording one of their best seasons in modern times, turning that first win into a run of 12 in 13 league matches as they roared back to finish fourth.

So a slow start is no reason to panic – but with so many changes to their team, Villa fans will struggle to stay calm if August goes awry.

Sports.title: Inside the new-look Birmingham City: How Blues' recruitment has been supercharged, their transfer wishlist, the coaching talents taking centre stage and why Chris Davies is shaking things up at rebranded HQ
Sports.content:
Inside the new-look Birmingham City: How Blues' recruitment has been supercharged, their transfer wishlist, the coaching talents taking centre stage and why Chris Davies is shaking things up at rebranded HQ

Unlock more of the best of our football coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

For the first time in many years, there is a welcome air of calm around Birmingham City on the eve of a new campaign.

Life has rarely been dull for Blues supporters in recent seasons. They have watched their club wobble on the edge of oblivion. They have witnessed Jude Bellingham, Wayne Rooney and Tom Brady at close quarters and marvelled at US owners’ Knighthead’s £2-3billion investment plans, including a 62,000-seat stadium.

Blues’ American owners have developed a rivalry with their counterparts at Wrexham that brought David Beckham to St Andrew’s when the teams met in September 2024.

They bought Jay Stansfield for £15million in League One and showcased a six-part Amazon Prime documentary a year ago.

This summer has allowed Blues finally to pause for breath. Although there will be more signings, so far they have spent less than £5million. The training ground looks different, so too the style of play. The approach to recruitment feels more measured.

Ahead of Saturday’s Carabao Cup tie at Swansea, Daily Mail Sport visited Blues’ base in rural Warwickshire to see how they are shaping up.

After a rollercoaster few seasons at St Andrew's, Birmingham City look set for a year of stability and solid progression

But ambitions remain high under the stewardship of Tom Wagner (left) and Tom Brady

What are the goals?

Promotion to the top flight remains the focus – but perhaps with a little more realism attached. When boss Chris Davies pointed out a year ago how few teams were able to bounce straight from League One to the Premier League in consecutive seasons, it did not fit the script.

When Birmingham won promotion from the third tier, there was a two-year plan to reach the summit – and ideally, it would happen instantly.

Though nobody will say it publicly, Daily Mail Sport understands that senior figures at Blues realise that it might not be quite that easy. There is an acceptance that promotion might take longer than the initial two-year forecast, though the expanded six-team play-offs should play into the hands of clubs like Blues.

Last season Davies stuck to his high-possession game and though it yielded excellent home form, Birmingham struggled on the road, winning only five times in the league and losing 13. Expect a more flexible style this term with Blues playing a more direct game, especially away from St Andrew’s.

This switch dates back to New Year’s Day, when Birmingham lost 3-0 at Watford and Davies saw a lack of strength – in body and mind. Like the Premier League, the Championship’s athletic demands have grown dramatically and, in some fixtures, Blues felt they were being physically outmatched.

In came Jhon Solis, August Priske, Carlos Vicente and Ibrahim Osman in January. The first three are expected to be key figures this term after having six months to adapt while Blues remain key to re-sign Osman from Brighton.

Blues have added set-piece coach Scott Fry, whose input helped Lincoln score 30 set-piece goals in League One in 2024-25. After a spell at Rangers, he was snapped up by Blues and in the recent friendly against Barcelona, Fry took centre stage in the technical area at every restart.

Blues are keen to re-sign Ibrahim Osman after taking him on loan from Brighton last season

‘It seems to be calmer than it was last year,’ says Davies. ‘That’s not to say we lack ambition, but I think that calmness bodes well.

‘We know what we’re walking into – the players do, I do. We’ve got that continuity and it’s the best way to approach it.

‘There was a lot there last year, because of winning League One the previous season and I felt we deserved to finish higher than 10th – but it was a creditable finish. We went through the ups and downs and emerged stronger, so I’m hopeful and excited.’

What could happen before the window closes?

Davies feels Blues are well set at the back and in goal but the club are keen to improve the squad in midfield and attacking positions.

Following Craig Gardner’s departure as director of football in June, Blues are a little more methodical in their approach to recruitment and will rely heavily on data. Joe Carnall and Micky Moore are running the department as Blues consider a long-term replacement for Gardner. Keep an eye on the experienced Mike Rigg, currently working as technical director in the Blues academy and another who follows data closely.

Here, though, Davies sounds a note of caution. He has watched with interest as Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck have joined Chelsea this summer, while James Milner retired at the end of last season aged 40.

‘Football has gone "data, data, data" but it doesn’t measure character, personality type or leadership skills,’ said Davies. ‘There’s a very human side to it.

‘I worked with Jordan Henderson at Liverpool – he’s 36 now but he’s gone to a massive club like Chelsea and went to the World Cup. That’s because of his personality and leadership skills.

‘I am happy with what we have here,' says boss Chris Davies. 'We don’t have a team of mercenaries here for the money'

‘You have your ups and downs in the Championship. Someone could be outstanding on the data and you think, "Wow, he’s too good for this level". But what is he like when you lose three games in a week, or he’s not starting? Will he help the team?’

‘I am happy with what we have here. We don’t have a team of mercenaries here for the money. These players want to win games for this club. I’d rather have a worse player on paper but I know he’s committed, than someone who’s a better player but you’re not quite sure (about his character).’

How might the season go?

At heart, Davies is a coach. He has never been one of those managers to watch from the sidelines and leave sessions to others.

Before becoming Blues boss, Davies was right-hand man to Brendan Rodgers and Ange Postecoglou and loves to be – as the modern football buzz phrase has it – on the grass.

In recent times, though, Davies’ assistant Ben Petty is thought to have taken a more prominent role in sessions, allowing Davies to take a wider view of life at the Elite Performance and Innovation Centre (EPIC), Blues’ base near the picturesque town of Henley-in-Arden.

Visting EPIC ahead of the Swansea fixture, the change was noticeable. Bare walls told the story of an imminent rebrand and there were fewer motivational quotations emblazoned on various surfaces.

NFL superstar Brady remains an influence behind the scenes and the logo of his performance and fitness company, TBRx, was still visible, although not as prominent as 12 months ago. Yet TBRx staff will continue to manage players’ recovery, which means reporting to EPIC the day after every game. No Sundays off for Blues players.

Much is made of the rivalry between Birmingham’s Americans and those at Wrexham – Hollywood superstar Ryan Reynolds and fellow actor Rob McElhenney. Blues leaned into that last season but this term, it may be a little different. It will be intriguing to take the temperature when the teams meet in north Wales on August 28.

Birmingham have a natural leader in defender Christoph Klarer but Davies is keen to share the responsibility around his dressing room

Davies is also keen for his players to take greater responsibility. In Christoph Klarer, they have a natural leader as skipper but he cannot do it alone. So during pre-season, Davies asked players to split into small groups to discuss certain topics – sometimes tactical, others technical or mental – and report their findings to the squad.

‘If it’s just me explaining things to them, it’s like you’re preaching all the time,’ Davies argued. ‘When the players speak, nuggets come from it that I find really useful. We did it during pre-season in Portugal. They have to have a voice.’

As well as Klarer, Blues have a natural leader at the top of the club. Chairman Tom Wagner has been absent from St Andrew’s since suffering a stroke in February. In an update last week, Knighthead wrote that they ‘expect to see (Wagner) at a match in the near future.’ That would be hugely welcome news across the club and fanbase.

Sports.title: South Korea FA 'provided "sexual entertainment" for foreign referees at massage parlours ahead of international matches including World Cup qualifier'
Sports.content:
South Korea FA 'provided "sexual entertainment" for foreign referees at massage parlours ahead of international matches including World Cup qualifier'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

South Korea's football federation provided sexual entertainment to foreign referees before and after international matches, a government audit report revealed.

The report said the Korea Football Association (KFA) used business credit cards to pay for sexual entertainment for visiting referees at massage parlours in Seoul and other cities that hosted international matches between March 2011 and March 2012.

Those matches included qualifying games for the 2012 London Olympics and the 2014 FIFA World Cup.

Around twelve referees and match coordinators received the favours provided by the KFA across seven matches, according to the report compiled in 2016.

The officials came from Japan, the United Arab Emirates, Iran, Bahrain and Uzbekistan.

South Korea's news outlet Yonhap News Agency reported South Korea remained undefeated in the seven matches with five wins and two draws.

The report emerged this week as part of an investigation into the KFA's appointment of former coach Hong Myung-bo in 2024.

In two Olympic qualifying matches, South Korea beat Oman 2-0 on September 21, 2011. The nation then drew against Qatar, with no goals scored, on March 14, 2012.

The report said the Korea Football Association (KFA) used business credit cards to pay for sexual entertainment for visiting referees at massage parlours in Seoul and other cities that hosted international matches (Pictured: KFA HQ)

But South Korea had already secured an Olympic spot before the game.

On February 29, 2012, South Korea beat Kuwait 2-0 to progress to the next phase of the World Cup qualification.

South Korea had been the favourites in all three matches.

The KFA could also escape FIFA sanctions. The organisation's Code of Ethics bars most cases from being pursued after five years, with only bribery and corruption allegations carrying a 10-year limitation period.

There is no time limit for cases involving sexual abuse, harassment or exploitation. But paying for sexual entertainment may not be covered by those provisions.

Cho Chung-yun, who was KFA president at the time, was referred to police by South Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism following a 2016 audit that alleged he had misused federation funds.

The ministry also found that current and former KFA staff had used business credit cards at massage parlours and other inappropriate establishments.

The ministry said on Friday it had investigated claims referees had been provided sexual entertainment, but it struggled to verify all the facts.

Those KFA employees accused of improper business credit card use were not convicted and did not receive disciplinary repercussions from the football association.

South Korea's defender Lee Gi-hyuk reacted in dismay after his team lost a FIFA World Cup match to South Africa this year

Former KFA officials told local news outlet JTBC that the referees asked to visit the adult establishments and that it was 'common practice at the time' to accommodate their wishes.

While one noted the practice extends past South Korea and is more common in other countries.

A current KFA official has since said strict internal guidelines have been implemented.

The report, compiled by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, emerged mere hours after police raided the KFA HQ in Cheonan and the KFA House in Seoul.

The raids came as part of an investigation into the KFA's appointment of the former coach Myung-bo in 2024.

His appointment faced criticism after the KFA abandoned a months-long search involving foreign applicants and appointed him after a brief meeting.

Hong returned as national team coach after a brief time in the position from 2013 to 2014.

The investigation was sparked after South Korea's disappointing performance in the FIFA World Cup campaign, which ended in a group-stage exit.

During the raids, police seized documents believed to show whether Hong's hiring process included improper meddling and obstruction by KFA leaders, including by its former chief Chung Mong-gyu.

Both Hong and Chung stepped down after South Korea's exit from the tournament this year.

The pair also testified in parliament last month and were scrutinised over the reasons behind the disappointing performance and the operations within the KFA.

Sports.title: England footballer Ivan Toney charged with assault after 'headbutting fan who wanted selfie' in Soho nightclub
Sports.content:
England footballer Ivan Toney charged with assault after 'headbutting fan who wanted selfie' in Soho nightclub

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged after allegedly headbutting a fan who was trying to get a selfie at a Soho nightclub.

The 30-year-old striker was charged with assault causing actual bodily harm last Thursday after an incident at 100 Wardour Street in London on December 6 last year.

Toney, who is originally from Northampton but currently plays for Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on September 24.

Reports at the time alleged that the former Brentford player, who moved to Al-Ahli for £40million two years ago, had been grabbed by a fan who had wanted a selfie.

A witness said: 'He [Toney] walked past a table of a group of lads. One of them recognised him and said, 'Oh, it's Ivan Toney' and tried to put his hands around his neck to get a photo with him. And then Toney has said, 'Get off me, get off me'.'

The witness said Toney wore a 'real nice watch' and may have been concerned he was being mugged. Toney was reportedly arrested after an alleged headbutt.

His spokesperson said: 'Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.'

A Metropolitan Police statement said today: 'A man has been charged with assault following a Met investigation. Ivan Toney, 30, of Northampton, was charged on Thursday, July 31 with assault causing actual bodily harm.

England's Ivan Toney ahead of kick off against France at the World Cup in Miami on July 18

The alleged incident took place at 100 Wardour Street in London's Soho (file photograph)

'He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday, September 24. The charge relates to an assault, which reportedly took place on December 6, 2025 at a nightclub on Wardour Street, W1.'

Toney has been on unconditional bail since being arrested by the Met last year, but was granted a US visa and allowed to travel to the World Cup in June.

He played twice - coming on as a substite in the final minutes of England's semi-final defeat to Argentina, then starting the third-place play off victory against France.

Toney began his career at hometown club Northampton Town in 2012, scoring 11 goals across 53 appearances before signing for Newcastle United three years later.

He only played twice for Newcastle between 2015 and 2018 but had loan spells in that period at Barnsley, Shrewsbury Town, Scunthorpe United and Wigan Athletic.

Toney then joined Peterborough United for about £350,000 in 2018, where he scored 40 goals in 76 appearances, before a big-money move to Brentford in 2020.

This was for an initial fee of £5million which later rose to £10million. He scored 67 times across 128 appearances for Brentford before leaving for Saudi Arabia in 2024.

Toney signed with Al-Ahli until 2028 and has so far scored 55 goals across 62 appearances, winning the AFC Champions League Elite title in his first season.

He has played ten times for England, with his debut coming at Wembley against Ukraine in March 2023 and his only goal being against Belgium in March 2024.

100 Wardour Street opened in 2016 but shut in January. It is on the site of the former Marquee Club, which hosted early gigs from The Rolling Stones and David Bowie.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
