Sports.title: Why Honda only realised the scale of its F1 problems in January
Sports.content:
Heading into Formula 1's major technical overhaul, expectations at Aston Martin were high. With a state-of-the-art factory in Silverstone, legendary designer Adrian Newey and a works partnership with Honda, all the ingredients for success appeared to be in place.

That may still prove to be the case in the longer term, but the start of the new era has proved far more challenging than anticipated. Mike Krack recently admitted that Aston Martin had barely been racing before the summer break, simply because the gap to newcomer Cadillac amounted to around one second.

That changed when the AMR26 received its first major upgrade package in Hungary, although the chassis is naturally only part of the story. Honda has also encountered numerous problems since officially returning to F1, ranging from vibrations that troubled the drivers during the opening weeks of the season to a significant deficit in outright performance.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with Autosport, trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explained that the full extent of those problems only became clear in January.

“So, probably at the end of last year, our position was not so bad,” he said. “Still, performance and drivability were in the development stage, but it looked okay.

"But in January, we realised that in some of the areas we found some, not issues, but we realised that performance was always up, down, up, down. So we found some performance, but then we also found some reliability issues."

Shintaro Orihara, Honda Photo by: EYE4images / NurPhoto via Getty Images

Because reliability is always a top priority, Honda had to take a step back on several performance gains to ensure reliability at that performance level. Naturally, that slowed down its overall development.

"In January, we realised that our performance and reliability would not be competitive,” Orihara added. “When we started running in Barcelona, we realised that our performance was definitely poor compared to the other manufacturers. And also, we found some issues on the battery side."

Those battery-related issues made the development process more complex. They cost valuable track time during winter testing, something that was especially painful given Aston Martin and Honda's need to gather data to recover from their deficit.

"So we realised that we were not in good position, maybe at beginning of this year. Last year, at end of last year, we already saw that we were not competitive, but we didn't expect it so bad," Orihara admitted.

What has been Honda's biggest challenge?

Part of the explanation is that Honda's current F1 project is very different from its successful years with Red Bull, something that ties in with the company's philosophy of transferring F1 knowledge to other parts of the company.

Another part of the explanation is, according to Honda, the complexity of the current regulations. Orihara stressed that there has not been one single stumbling block ahead of 2026, but rather the combination of all the changes introduced at the same time.

Honda Power Unit Launch

"It's difficult to say which component of the power unit is most challenging because in this regulation, everything has changed a lot,” said Orihara. “For example, MGU-K power changed from, let's say, [120] to 350 kilowatts. That is a significant change.

"But also on the internal combustion engine side, we have changed the fuel flow rate. So in this regulation, everything has been changed so much. So, a challenging point for Honda is just the combination of a lot of changes happening at the same time."

That means Honda is lacking outright power from its internal combustion engine, something the long-awaited Zandvoort upgrade is specifically designed to address. It is intended to be the first step towards reducing the brand's still significant performance deficit.

On the electrical side of the power unit, the emphasis is on efficiency. However, Orihara explained that the changes there have also had a major impact on drivability – one of the areas that has been a recurring topic for Honda and Aston Martin in the opening months of the season.

"Removing the MGU-H has also been quite challenging on the power unit side,” he said.

“Probably that is the most exciting point for power unit manufacturers. I have always been mentioning drivability. That is, maybe not mainly, but the majority of that is coming from removing the MGU-H.

"So that is a challenging point for us as a power unit supplier, to keep the boost pressure at a target. Again, it's difficult to pick one component that has been most challenging for us, but it has been the combination of all changes at the same time."

Although Honda knows that returning to the competitive level it is targeting will take time - a lot of time - it hopes to make a first step at Zandvoort. That upgrade is focused purely on improving the internal combustion engine and was already tested during a filming day at the Hungaroring.

Sports.title: Why McLaren has been coy about introducing its rotating F1 rear wing
Sports.content:
McLaren will race its version of the so-called 'Macarena' rear-wing concept – but not until an unspecified point in the future, according to team principal Andrea Stella.

It's understood that the reason for not rushing to race the new rear wing is not linked to Red Bull's well-documented issues with its similar design. Instead, McLaren is being cautiously pragmatic, since the rotating rear wing adds to the complexities of managing car behaviour as it moves in and out of Straight Line Mode (SLM).

McLaren planned to test its new wing in Austria but made a late decision to abandon the evaluation. It then waited until Hungary to run it for the first time in FP1 on Oscar Piastri's car, driven by Leonardo Fornaroli, before parking it for the remainder of the event.

Max Verstappen crashed at the Red Bull Ring and Silverstone, prompting his Red Bull team to temporarily shelve its pivoting rear wing based on suspicions that a delay in airflow reattachment when the wing returned to cornering mode made Verstappen's car unstable.

"I have to say it's been a complicated project," Stella told media including Autosport.

"Which was no surprise because when we saw Ferrari introducing the wing in Bahrain test and testing it in China in the first lap, [Lewis] Hamilton spun. And then it took a few more events to actually being in condition to race it.

"We knew it was going to be a complex project, so I have to say that our engineering department has delivered this project in a way that looks well-behaved – like the wing in terms of mechanical actuation, times of the actuation, because there's some limitations by the regulations, not only for aerodynamic reasons.

Ferrari was the first team to run its rotating rear wing, which operates differently to the McLaren and Red Bull examples Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"And then the overall behaviour from an aerodynamic point of view, reattachment – so the time it takes for the car to regain the load, not only the load on the wing, the load on the entire car as driven from the wing.

"All this I have to say has been pretty consistent with expectation, so it's been a positive sign off of this concept and we look forward now to introducing this concept at some future events."

These concepts are a classic example of thinking-outside-the-box creative engineering that is possible for the first time this season because the regulations are relatively open. F1 first adopted the principle of legally shedding drag in a straight line with the Drag Reduction System (DRS) in 2011, which permitted the upper rear wing plane to flatten in prescribed areas of the track.

The speed and actuation procedure for this was clearly defined, along with the dimensions of the wing planes themselves. But under the new ruleset introduced this season, in which front and rear wing flaps can open in specified Straight Line Mode zones, the speed of transition from one state to the other is defined (within 0.4s), but not the means by which it moves between open and closed.

McLaren's pivoting rear wing is closer to Red Bull's than Ferrari's, in that it uses a central actuator to manage the rotation rather than having a mechanism built into the endplates. Also like Red Bull's, it pivots forwards rather than backwards.

The means of actuation gives it an element of air braking as it closes. The trade-off between the two concepts is that Red Bull and McLaren accept a degree of aerodynamic blockage from the actuator and its shroud in exchange for having a wider space between the upper and lower planes when SLM is active.

Ferrari's also has to take a longer path between open and closed because of the angle of rotation.

Verstappen shunted in qualifying in Austria, and a delay in airflow reattachment to the rear wing was cited as one possible contributory factor Photo by: Getty Images

One of the less predictable effects of the new regulations has been the shift in tyre loading during the transition between SLM being on and off. This is because the airflow doesn't reattach to the wing planes instantly, but takes fractions of a second to re-establish its path.

Teams knew ahead of the season that this would be a significant performance factor, but were unable to measure it accurately with simulation tools such as the wind tunnel and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD).

The true extent of the shifts in loadings, and their effect on car behaviour, could only be measured at the track.

This also applies to the theoretical benefits of the rotating rear wings. The airflow around the rear of an F1 car is tremendously busy because of the interaction between the car's aerodynamic surfaces and the turbulent wake of the rear wheels.

Simulating this with great accuracy is very difficult in the wind tunnel, where model size is capped at 60% scale and the wind is generally blowing in one direction. Historically it is difficult to access a car's aerodynamic performance when it's in a state of yaw (i.e. turning), or facing different wind directions. The different deflection properties of the model tyres, as well as their smaller size, also has a tendency to skew results.

Hence McLaren has done a lot of FP1 running with large aero rakes fitted behind the rear wheels to validate substantial bodywork changes such as the latest-spec floor, introduced in Hungary, as well as its pivoting wing. Practical measurements trackside are the real proof (or otherwise) of any theoretical gains.

"There was a question about comparison with Red Bull, but I don't think the wind tunnel is a major factor in terms of determining the aerodynamic behaviour in reattachment," Stella said.

"I think you can use some other tools for that, and then the most important tool, especially when you have this sort of complicated project, even from an aerodynamic point of view, remains what you observe at the track. So it was important for us to acquire data here trackside, because you would have never relied on a wind tunnel only for such a delicate project."

Sports.title: Why the FIA couldn't intervene sooner over F1's 2026 rules
Sports.content:
With the first Formula 1 season under the new technical regulations approaching its halfway point, the summer break provides a good opportunity to take stock. The 2026 rules, with their much greater emphasis on electric power, have sparked considerable debate both in and outside the paddock.

F1 insists that fan ratings – for example in its own Formula 1 Fan Voice programme – have been largely positive, but drivers have been far more critical.

Max Verstappen described the power unit regulations as "Formula E on steroids" during winter testing in Bahrain, while Oscar Piastri spoke at Spa-Francorchamps about the "self-learning elements" of the power units and "qualifying grids being decided by computers behaving or misbehaving".

Asked by Autosport whether the criticism from drivers over the past few months had been stronger than the FIA expected, Tombazis responded: "I think drivers are, by definition, quite demanding clients. I don't think we expected them to have a sugarcoat or to not speak their minds. So to say that it's been more than expected, no, I wouldn't say so."

The complaints from drivers about energy management, super clipping and algorithms were also in line with what the FIA had anticipated, according to its single-seater director.

"We did anticipate a lot of these things that they have complained about in the two years before the launch of the season. We did try to make some adjustments, but we failed with the governance that was in place," Tombazis said. "So I think it was realistically only to be expected."

Energy-starved circuits such as Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps have highlighted the shortcomings of the 2026 regulations Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

FIA tried to listen to F1 drivers' criticism in build-up to 2026

If it had been up to Tombazis, the changes to the regulations that have now been agreed for 2027 and 2028 – to gradually move to a 60-40 split – would ideally have been introduced much earlier.

"I think it's a bit of a shame that we had to wait until we discussed things in May and get to a package for 2027 and for 2028. I think we could have ideally done that a couple of years before and then there wouldn't have been all of this discussion," Tombazis said.

Several drivers warned about potential problems with the new engine regulations before 2026. Verstappen was the first to do so publicly during the 2023 Austrian Grand Prix, when Autosport asked him about his initial simulator runs with the new engine formula.

That has perhaps created the impression that drivers were not listened to in the years leading up to 2026, but Tombazis insists the reality is different. According to him, the initial feedback was taken seriously, but the governance framework meant the regulations could not be significantly revised.

"When OEMs decide to participate as PU manufacturers, they sign a governance agreement that is binding towards all parties, so the FIA, FOM and the PU manufacturers. It's similar to what the Concorde Agreement does for the team side of things," Tombazis explained.

"And there was a separate governance agreement signed in 2022 in order to basically outline the requirements for the PU manufacturers during the years of 2023, 2024 and 2025. That is before the championship started because there's such things like financial regulations for the first time."

The FIA states that governance, even with new manufacturers such as Audi, has made intervention impossible Photo by: Pirelli

Among other things, that agreement stipulated that new entrants would not be allowed to spend unlimited amounts of money to develop their 2026 power units.

"If a PU manufacturer who was not participating in Formula 1, let's say Audi, they still had to be bound by regulations and not come to us and say, well, we're not participating, hence we can spend five times the money. That would be unfair," he said.

"So that's why there was a governance agreement that on the one hand forced them to be bound by the regulations, including the financial and operational rules and all of that."

At the same time, that document made it much harder for the FIA to reopen the regulations in the years leading up to 2026 without securing a supermajority.

"On the other hand it put limitations as to how much we could change things unilaterally as the FIA. And therefore any change had to be approved by a significant number of the PU manufacturers," Tombazis explained.

"So for the sort of changes we did [in May], we needed at least four of them to agree. And quite simply, four of them did not agree during the years when we discussed some adjustments."

Tombazis had hoped that the changes for the coming years could have been implemented sooner Photo by: Lars Baron / Getty Images

Challenges known since 2022, but races still entertaining

Part of the reason for that was that the reality of the automotive industry looked very different at the time, with manufacturers placing a much greater emphasis on electrification.

"Overall, it was always a challenging target to have a close to 50-50 power split between the two units," Tombazis said.

"But that was a very important position for the OEMs participating, and frankly having to decide whether they want to be in Formula 1 or not. Don't forget that if we didn't have them in, we would have just two power units in Formula 1, which I think would have been a bit of an issue. So that requirement to have a much stronger electrical part did create these difficulties."

Tombazis explained that the FIA had already become aware of these challenges in 2022, a year before Verstappen publicly voiced his concerns, but by then it was simply too late to fundamentally alter the regulations.

"As simulations came in back in 2022 or so, we knew there were these issues, but we were a bit too far down the line there to change things and some people had committed too much resource," he said. "So that left us slightly on the back foot at the start of the season, discussing that."

Tombazis concluded by stressing that, despite all of this, the races themselves have still provided good entertainment during the first half of the season.

Tombazis feels despite the problems with the F1 regulations, the racing has been exciting Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"Now with that said, I think most races have been pretty exciting, I would say. There's been quite a lot of fighting," he said.

"I would even say that currently we still have, I don't know if I would go quite as far as to call it domination, but we do have a clear advantage for one manufacturer. And in the past when we've had that at the early start of the regulations, races have been very processional.

"Now I think, even despite the fact that Mercedes have been doing most of the winning, I think the races have nonetheless been quite exciting with quite a lot of changes and so on."

Sports.title: Verstappen's mindset going into the F1 summer break: "Of course I can easily stop, but I love racing"
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen says he is "feeling good" about his place in Formula 1 as he detailed his mindset about Red Bull and the regulations heading into the summer break.

Verstappen and Red Bull have not had an easy ride this year with a RB22 chassis that has fallen short of expectations and has been tricky to set up and drive. At the same time Red Bull-Ford Powertrains delivered above expectations with its first-ever power unit, although its place atop the pecking order of the convoluted ADUO upgrade system means Red Bull isn't allowed to improve its engine.

As Red Bull heads into the summer break winless and fourth in the standings, which could see Verstappen trigger get-out clauses from his 2028 deal, the other concern has been the Dutchman's bitter discontent with the 2026 power unit regulations, which has been another element to take into account as he weighs up his future.

Despite the usual mid-season speculation around Verstappen's future, little appears to have moved in recent weeks, and with few credible alternatives the expectation is that the four-time world champion will simply stay put at Red Bull for another year.

As he heads into the summer break, Verstappen has offered the latest insight into his thinking, suggesting he can easily walk away tomorrow if he wanted to, but that he's still keen to keep racing on. In that regard Verstappen is still in a different place than 45-year-old veteran Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso, who said his enjoyment of the regulations will play a big role in deciding his future.

"Of course, Fernando is 45, so it's probably a bit easier for him to say: 'I quit,'" Verstappen said. "But as a real racer, it's tough, especially when you're not enjoying the regulations and you're not competitive at the moment. Fernando, of course, doesn't deserve to be in P21.

Lando Norris, McLaren, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Zak Mauger / LAT Images via Getty Images

"I'm of course 28 years old, so it's a little bit different. I mean, of course I can easily stop, it's not a problem, but I love racing, and I'm just trying to deal with what we have, even though what we have at the moment is not what I like."

The two sticking points for Verstappen are still the same, with some hope that both Red Bull's own performance and F1's controversial regulations, which will be tweaked further for 2027, can be improved enough for an extended stay in the series to be desirable. But speaking on the eve of the Hungarian Grand Prix weekend, Verstappen insisted his focus was squarely on the former.

A confusing Budapest weekend in which Verstappen and team-mate Isack Hadjar both struggled for confidence in an unpredictable car, but Verstappen still had strong race pace to finish second, perfectly encapsulated Red Bull's 2026 campaign.

"I am feeling good from my side, but I'm saying that there is nothing to say because there is nothing going on," Verstappen explained. "I'm just focused on trying to get the most out of the car and that's already complicated enough to deal with.

"This team is like a second family to me. I'm just trying to understand our car a bit better, and get back to winning ways. We've been close one weekend, I hope of course a little bit more often than just one weekend, but like I said before, it's definitely on an upward trend, so that's good to see."

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Not Impressed By Moses Itauma Hype
Sports.content:
“I think I’m the best opponent he’s faced. I think he’s never been until now in the ring with someone like me, with that kind of experience and endurance, toughness, power. So let’s see how good he is,” Hrgovic told DAZN Boxing. “Everyone says he’s a future superstar, future Lennox Lewis.”

“You believe it as well, though,” Itauma said.

“Let’s see,” Hrgovic said. “We’ll see. I don’t know. For right now, I’m not impressed. I must see something more than this to believe he’s the real deal. So, let’s see.”

Hrgovic believes he can force Itauma into situations previous opponents have been unable to create. The young heavyweight has spent his rapid climb through the division overwhelming opposition before being pushed into prolonged, difficult fights.

Hrgovic has already experienced those kinds of battles, including his grueling fight with Zhilei Zhang and stoppage loss to Daniel Dubois. His durability gives Itauma something different to solve if the fight extends beyond the early rounds.

Itauma has looked considerably faster than Hrgovic and carries dangerous power, but the Croatian represents a significant jump from the opposition the prospect has faced so far.

The Lennox Lewis comparisons are especially premature. Itauma does not need to resemble a future Hall of Famer on August 29. He does need to show that his talent remains effective against a durable heavyweight capable of absorbing punishment and firing back.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois-Fabio Wardley Rematch Could Land October 17
Sports.content:
Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round of their May 9 fight in Manchester following an exhausting battle in which both heavyweights had difficult moments. Wardley dropped Dubois twice early, putting himself in position to take control before Dubois worked his way back into the fight.

Dubois gradually took over as the rounds passed, landing the cleaner, heavier punches while Wardley absorbed increasing damage. The punishment accumulated before Dubois forced the stoppage in the 11th.

Wardley exercised his contractual right to an immediate rematch rather than taking an interim fight. An October 17 return would leave him with little time to recover physically before beginning another training camp for the same opponent.

That decision recently drew criticism from former two-division champion Paulie Malignaggi, who questioned the wisdom of going directly back into another fight with Dubois. Malignaggi believes Wardley has the punching power to change a fight instantly but sees a considerable skill advantage for Dubois.

The possible October date makes Malignaggi’s concern more relevant. Wardley would have to recover physically, make tactical adjustments and prepare for another demanding heavyweight fight just over five months after the first one.

A quick return also gives Dubois an opportunity to repeat his first result before Wardley has much time to make major changes. Wardley has already shown that he can hurt Dubois. Five months may not be enough to correct the technical weaknesses Dubois exploited as their first fight progressed.

Sports.title: Héctor Camacho Overwhelms Rafael Limón for First World Title
Sports.content:
The belt became available after the WBC stripped Bobby Chacon when a defense against No. 1 contender Camacho failed to materialize. Limón, 29, had recently held the championship before losing a brutal 15-round decision to Chacon in their celebrated fourth fight eight months earlier.

This was Camacho’s first opportunity to win a world title. Limón also represented something new for the young Puerto Rican: an opponent who had previously worn a world championship belt.

The difference in speed became apparent almost immediately. Limón tried to reach Camacho with wide punches, while the younger fighter attacked from different angles, with his straight left finding the target repeatedly. A clean left floored Limón late in the third round. More punishment followed during the fourth as Camacho had him in serious trouble.

Limón’s situation deteriorated further in the fifth. Body shots put him on the canvas in the center of the ring. He regained his feet, but Camacho quickly resumed his assault. A subsequent barrage knocked Limón through the ropes near his corner.

Limón climbed back into position once more. Referee Richard Steele decided he had absorbed enough punishment and stopped the contest at 2:52 of the fifth round. Camacho was the new WBC junior lightweight champion.

All three judges had Camacho comfortably in front through four completed rounds. Dimas Hernandez scored it 40-34, while Moises Sister and Hector Chaumont each had it 40-35.

The celebration afterward illustrated Camacho’s popularity as much as the fight itself. Spectators and members of his entourage poured around the ring as Puerto Rico celebrated its newest world champion.

The performance showed a version of Camacho that later generations of boxing fans rarely saw. Before age and years in the ring changed his style, Camacho possessed extraordinary speed, reflexes and offensive ability. Limón was a hardened former two-time champion who had survived wars with Bobby Chacon, yet the 21-year-old Camacho overwhelmed him with a combination of speed and aggression that Limón simply could not handle.

Camacho made one defense of the title, knocking out Rafael Solis in five rounds, before moving up in weight. Two years after defeating Limón, he captured the WBC lightweight championship. His flamboyant personality, exceptional speed and success across multiple divisions eventually established “Macho” among boxing’s most recognizable stars.

Sports.title: Dwight Braxton Dominates Saad Muhammad In Philadelphia Rematch
Sports.content:
This time, Braxton was even more dominant. Braxton, 29, gave away considerable height and reach to the 28-year-old Saad Muhammad, but the physical disadvantages meant little once the action began. The 5-foot-5 titleholder worked his way inside behind his jab, forcing the taller challenger onto his back foot.

Saad Muhammad had replaced longtime trainer Sam Solomon with Steve Traitz following the first loss, but the change did little to alter the outcome.

Braxton bloodied Saad Muhammad’s nose in the second round and dropped him in the third. There would be none of the remarkable recoveries that had defined Saad Muhammad’s prime years. Braxton kept attacking with compact hooks, right hands, and heavy body shots.

By the end of five rounds, judges Tony Castellano, Tony Perez, and Dick Young had Braxton comfortably in front by scores of 50-43, 50-42, and 50-41.

The finish came quickly in the sixth. Braxton drove Saad Muhammad toward the ropes with a left-right combination and continued firing as the challenger struggled to defend himself. Referee Carlos Padilla intervened at 1:23, giving Braxton his second consecutive stoppage over his rival.

The performance established Braxton, who would become known as Dwight Muhammad Qawi, as the premier 175-pound fighter alongside Michael Spinks. He later defeated Eddie Davis before losing a light heavyweight unification contest to Spinks in 1983.

The night ended Saad Muhammad’s time at the top of the division. His championship years had featured extraordinary rallies and grueling wars, but those battles took their toll. He continued fighting long after the Braxton losses and was eventually inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame.

There was no miraculous Matthew Saad Muhammad comeback this night. Braxton’s inside control, compact punching, and relentless pressure produced an emphatic conclusion to a rivalry he had already taken command of seven months earlier.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Is Running Out Of Fighters To Reject
Sports.content:
The back-and-forth with WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney illustrates the problem. Shakur wants a 144-pound catchweight, a condition Bill Haney rejected by insisting Devin should not drop below the 147-pound welterweight limit.

Shakur can take the fight at 147, pursue a mandatory position or move on to another opponent. Instead, another potentially lucrative fight has stalled because he wants terms the champion has little reason to accept.

That is almost the opposite of the old-school mentality. Fighters who scored career-defining wins often returned to work quickly, signing another fight and capitalizing on their success while the public was still talking about them.

Seven months is enough time to negotiate a deal, complete a training camp and fight again. Shakur has instead acted like an employee who had the best day of his career at the office and responded by taking an extended vacation.

Shakur spent years trying to reach this position. The question now is how many months of his prime he’s willing to sacrifice by ruling out opponents and demanding terms that keep fights from getting made.

Sports.title: Murat Gassiev Vs Jarrell Miller Talks Underway For WBA Belt
Sports.content:
“There’s a little bit of confusion with the WBA. I mean, Gassiev’s the champion. He’s got to fight Jarrell Miller, our guy, which we’re negotiating at the moment,” Hearn told iFL TV.

The fight offers Miller a shot at a heavyweight belt late in his career. A scheduled 2019 title bout against Anthony Joshua was canceled after Miller failed multiple drug tests before the event.

Miller rebuilt his career and remains a difficult opponent due to his size, constant pressure, and high work rate. A fight against Gassiev puts him near the top of the division without requiring a long series of elimination bouts.

Gassiev’s heavyweight run has moved slowly since leaving the cruiserweight division. The former unified cruiserweight champion possesses considerable punching power, though health issues and long layoffs have prevented him from establishing the same position at heavyweight that he held at 200 pounds.

Hearn is already considering potential opponents if Miller wins.

“Hopefully Jarrell Miller can beat Gassiev. We can do Miller against Kabayel. There’s loads of fights to be made,” Hearn said.

Miller first needs the Gassiev fight finalized. At 38, an opportunity to challenge a WBA champion gives the recently signed Matchroom heavyweight another chance to capture a world title.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Sees No Reason To Delay Fury-Joshua
Sports.content:
“There is still plenty of time,” the Queensberry promoter told a media roundtable. “The fighters will just need to get into training some time in September, so that is what will happen in early September.”

Fury is spending time with his family on the Isle of Man after completing two training camps following his lengthy absence from the ring. He plans to begin serious preparations once the fight date is set.

“I believe the fight will go on in November,” Warren said.

Questions about Joshua’s readiness increased after Prenga dropped him with one of the first clean punches he landed. Pushing the bout into 2027 offers little benefit, particularly with Joshua having already fought twice this year.

“He has got plenty of time to get ready,” Warren said. “So what does he do if he doesn’t fight? He will carry on training, training and training, and he will be getting older as will Tyson, so what is the point? Get on with it.”

Warren believes Joshua’s vulnerability gives Fury a major advantage, pointing directly to the Prenga knockdown when explaining the danger facing the former champion against a more accomplished heavyweight.

“Looking at the Prenga fight, if that had been Tyson in there, that would have been all over.”

The location remains unresolved. Madison Square Garden has been linked to the event, although Joshua and Eddie Hearn have pushed to keep the fight in Britain. Turki Alalshikh will announce the official date and location.

Sports.title: Cassius Clay Dominates Brian London In Three-Round Title Defense
Sports.content:
London gave away advantages in height, reach, and speed, leaving him with few answers after the opening bell. Using a sharp jab, quick footwork, and rapid-fire combinations, the champion controlled the action and repeatedly beat London to the punch. The challenger generated almost no offense. Many accounts credited him with only a single solid left jab in the opening round that briefly caught Clay’s attention.

The finish came at 1:40 of the third round. Clay trapped London in a neutral corner, unleashing a blistering combination described by observers as roughly a dozen punches within a few seconds. A left-right combination sent London to the canvas, where referee Harry Gibbs completed the count.

Clay weighed 209½ pounds, while London came in at 201½ pounds. The champion received a guaranteed purse of approximately $252,000 plus a share of the television revenue. London earned about $112,000 for the brief outing.

Earls Court fell well short of full capacity. Many fight fans dismissed the matchup as a mismatch, and Clay quickly justified those expectations by displaying the hand speed, reflexes, and accuracy that defined his prime.

Clay’s knockout of London set up a meeting with Karl Mildenberger later that year. The event became the final bout under Clay’s agreement with the Louisville Sponsoring Group before Herbert Muhammad assumed management duties.

London remained remarkably candid about the experience throughout his life. He openly admitted Clay held every advantage, describing himself as smaller, slower, and lacking the champion’s athleticism. He frequently joked about accepting a rematch only if Clay entered the ring wearing heavy weights around his ankles. While certain British critics questioned London’s effort, his honesty about facing one of boxing’s greatest champions became an enduring part of the event’s history.

Ghana News.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign defence pact
Ghana News.content:
Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have signed a joint defence agreement, against the backdrop of war between the US and Iran.

Pakistan's foreign ministry said an attack on any of the three states "shall be regarded as an attack against them all".

The pact was announced at a meeting between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif in the Saudi city of Mecca.

The three countries have been looking to strengthen security ties as the conflict in the region has drawn in Saudi Arabia and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan announced a joint defence pact last year.

Ghana News.title: Vice President bids farewell to outgoing Brazilian Ambassador, reaffirms Ghana-Brazil partnership
Ghana News.content:
Vice President Prof. Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has received the outgoing Ambassador of the Federative Republic of Brazil to Ghana, Mariana Gonçalves Madeira, and commended her for her contributions toward strengthening relations between the two countries.

During a farewell meeting, the Vice President, on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama, the Government and people of Ghana, expressed appreciation to Ambassador Madeira for her service and efforts in deepening Ghana-Brazil cooperation during her tenure.

Ambassador Madeira reflected on the progress Ghana has made and praised the efforts of President Mahama’s administration to strengthen the country’s economy.

She described Ghana as a key partner for Brazil and expressed confidence in the potential for both nations to expand their collaboration in areas of mutual interest.

The discussions focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation in sectors including agriculture and agribusiness, energy, security and defence, trade, and social development.

Prof. Opoku-Agyemang highlighted opportunities for increased collaboration in the energy sector, particularly through partnerships involving Brazil’s state-owned oil company, Petrobras, as Ghana seeks to expand its energy capacity and attract strategic investments.

She noted that the relationship between Ghana and Brazil goes beyond modern diplomatic ties, with deep historical and cultural connections shaped by the movement of people across the Atlantic.

The Vice President also acknowledged Brazil’s support for Ghana on international initiatives, including efforts related to the United Nations resolution on the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade, as well as cooperation under the Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty and programmes focused on women and social development.

Prof. Opoku-Agyemang commended Ambassador Madeira for broadening the scope of diplomatic engagement during her tenure through collaborations with institutions including the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, the Ga Traditional Council, and initiatives aimed at promoting food security and social welfare.

She wished the outgoing ambassador well in her future diplomatic endeavours and expressed Ghana’s commitment to working with her successor to maintain the momentum in Ghana-Brazil relations.

The meeting, she said, reaffirmed the shared commitment of both countries to building partnerships that deliver tangible benefits to their citizens.

Ghana News.title: Losing the next generation? Ghana cannot afford to ignore youth substance abuse
Ghana News.content:
Every nation looks to its youth as the architects of tomorrow. They are expected to become the doctors who save lives, the teachers who inspire minds, the engineers who build infrastructure, the entrepreneurs who create jobs, and the leaders who shape national destiny. Yet, in Ghana today, a growing number of young people are falling into the grip of substance abuse, threatening not only their individual futures but also the country's social and economic progress.

This is no longer an isolated social problem or a challenge for law enforcement agencies alone. It is a national emergency that demands urgent, coordinated, and sustained action.

Recent concerns raised by the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), alongside warnings from the World Health Organization (WHO) and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), should serve as a wake-up call to every Ghanaian. These institutions have consistently highlighted the increasing misuse of drugs among young people and the devastating health, social, and economic consequences that follow.

The warning by NACOC Director-General Brigadier General Maxwell Obuba Mantey that Ghana risks losing its future generation should not be dismissed as mere rhetoric. It reflects a painful reality already unfolding in many communities across the country. The growing availability and misuse of substances such as marijuana, tramadol, shisha, and synthetic drugs continue to destroy lives. Behind every statistic is a young person whose education has been interrupted, whose health has deteriorated, whose family has been devastated, and whose dreams are gradually fading.

The roots of substance abuse are both complex and interconnected. Peer pressure, unemployment, poverty, family instability, mental health challenges, academic stress, curiosity, and the influence of social media all contribute to the problem. For many young people, drugs are not taken simply for pleasure; they become an escape from emotional pain, hopelessness, anxiety, and difficult life circumstances. Sadly, what often begins as experimentation can quickly develop into dependence, addiction, and irreversible physical and psychological damage.

While NACOC deserves commendation for intensifying public education and community awareness campaigns, awareness alone cannot win this battle. Ghana must significantly invest in prevention, early intervention, mental health services, counselling, and rehabilitation programmes that are both affordable and accessible. Schools must strengthen their guidance and counselling units to identify and support vulnerable students before they fall into addiction. Parents must remain actively involved in the lives of their children, while religious bodies, traditional authorities, civil society organisations, and community leaders must work together to create environments that discourage substance abuse and promote healthy lifestyles.

Equally important, the fight against substance abuse should not be driven solely by punishment. Addiction is a public health challenge that requires compassion as much as accountability. Young people battling substance dependence need treatment, counselling, rehabilitation, and opportunities for reintegration—not merely imprisonment or social rejection. Criminalising addiction without addressing its underlying causes will only deepen the crisis and leave many lives beyond recovery.

Government must also acknowledge that tackling youth unemployment is central to reducing substance abuse. A young person with meaningful employment, quality education, vocational skills, and opportunities for personal growth is far less likely to seek comfort in harmful substances. Expanding youth employment programmes, recreational facilities, entrepreneurship support, and skills training should therefore be viewed as part of Ghana's broader drug prevention strategy.

History has shown that Ghana has overcome major national challenges through unity and collective responsibility. The growing menace of youth substance abuse requires that same spirit of national commitment. Families, educators, healthcare professionals, policymakers, law enforcement agencies, traditional leaders, religious institutions, civil society organisations, and young people themselves must work together to reverse this dangerous trend before it becomes irreversible.

The next generation remains Ghana's greatest national resource. If we fail to protect our young people from the growing threat of substance abuse today, the consequences will extend far beyond individual lives. We risk weakening our workforce, increasing crime, overburdening our healthcare system, and slowing the nation's development.

The cost of inaction will be measured not only in statistics but in shattered dreams, broken families, and unrealised potential. Ghana cannot afford to lose another generation to addiction. The time to act is now—not after another promising life has been destroyed by substance abuse.

Ghana News.title: Nalerigu SHS ends Bunkpurugu’s reign to return to NSMQ after three years
Ghana News.content:
Nalerigu Senior High School has secured the North East Region’s only ticket to the National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) National Championship after defeating reigning regional champions Bunkpurugu Senior High School in a thrilling tie-breaker contest.

The two schools finished the competition level on 33 points each, forcing a tense speed race to determine the winner, with Nalerigu SHS holding their composure to claim qualification.

The victory marks Nalerigu SHS’s return to the national stage after a three-year absence and their second appearance in the prestigious science and mathematics competition.

Bunkpurugu SHS started strongly, taking control of the opening rounds and appearing set to retain their regional title. However, Nalerigu SHS mounted a spirited comeback in the later rounds to draw level and force the decisive tie-breaker.

In the final standings, Nalerigu SHS emerged winners after the tie-breaker, while Bunkpurugu SHS finished as runners-up.

Walewale Senior High School placed third with 25 points, while debutants STEM Senior High School finished fourth with 17 points.

For STEM SHS, the regional qualifier marked their first attempt at securing a place in the national competition. Despite a promising debut performance, the school could not complete a historic qualification.

Nalerigu SHS’s victory adds another chapter to the growing list of schools securing places at the 2026 NSMQ National Championship as regional qualifiers continue across the country.

The result also brings an end to Bunkpurugu SHS’s reign as North East Regional champions and sets the stage for Nalerigu SHS to represent the region at the national contest.

Ghana News.title: Standard Chartered declares GH¢673m dividend at 56th Annual General Meeting
Ghana News.content:
Standard Chartered Bank Ghana PLC has held its 56th Annual General Meeting (AGM) to present its Annual Report and Financial Statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 to its shareholders.

The Bank declared a dividend of GH¢4.989 per ordinary share, amounting to a total payout of GH¢672.35 million, and preference share dividend of GH¢1.13 million, resulting in a total payout of GH¢673.48 million after shareholders approved the final dividend at the Bank's 56th Annual General Meeting (AGM) held in Accra.

The Bank also reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Ghana's economic development as it marks 130 years of continuous operation. This commitment was reinforced during the Board’s engagement with shareholders, where the Bank’s impact and contribution to Ghana’s progress, from trade and infrastructure to wealth creation and cross-border banking solutions were highlighted.

Addressing shareholders, Mr Ebenezer Twum Asante, Chairman of Standard Chartered Bank Ghana PLC, highlighted the bank’s commitment to delivering shareholder value.

He said, "as we reflect on the year under review, our focus remains on positioning the Bank to deliver sustainable value for our shareholders. Looking ahead, Ghana's improving macroeconomic outlook provides grounds for optimism, even as global uncertainties remain. We remain confident in the strength of our franchise, the resilience of our people and the relevance of our strategy. We will continue to support our clients, deepen our contribution to Ghana's economic development and deliver long-term value for our shareholders."

Mr Xorse Godzi, Chief Executive of Standard Chartered Bank Ghana PLC, commenting on the Bank's priorities, said “Our focus is on supporting our clients’ ambitions while positioning the Bank for sustainable growth."

"As a super-connector bank, we leverage our international network, deep local expertise and differentiated capabilities to provide cross-border banking solutions that connect Ghanaian businesses and institutions to global markets, capital and innovation. We will continue to deepen client relationships, strengthen our digital capabilities and deliver solutions that help our clients navigate change with confidence.”

“As we commemorate 130 years in Ghana, our priorities remain anchored in disciplined execution, innovation and long-term value creation, while contributing to the country’s continued economic development,” he added.

Since its establishment in 1896, the Bank has been a trusted partner in the country’s economic evolution, enabling trade and investment, supporting enterprise growth, advancing innovation and connecting Ghana to global opportunities through the strength of its international network.

The Bank contributes to sustainable economic growth through our core banking business, responsible business practices, community investment and the development of talent. Given our heritage and legacy, we also provide thought leadership on key industry topics, helping to shape and strengthen the banking and financial services.

Ghana News.title: GenCED condemns Afenyo-Markin’s treatment of Nana Yaa Jantuah during NPP petition presentation
Ghana News.content:
The Gender Centre for Empowering Development (GenCED) has criticised Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin’s conduct during the presentation of the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) petition at the Jubilee House, describing his treatment of Presidential Staffer Nana Yaa Akyenpim Jantuah as unfortunate.

The gender advocacy organisation said the incident raises concerns about how women in public leadership and administrative positions are treated, particularly when carrying out official responsibilities.

In a statement issued on Friday, August 7, and signed by its Executive Director, Esther Tawiah, GenCED said political differences should not affect the dignity and respect accorded public officials.

“Regardless of political differences or disagreements, all public officials deserve to be treated with dignity and respect while carrying out their official responsibilities,” the group stated.

The controversy followed the NPP’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration on Thursday, August 6, when Nana Yaa Jantuah was assigned by the Presidency to receive the party’s petition on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama.

Mr Afenyo-Markin, who led the NPP delegation, questioned the decision, arguing that the level of leadership present at the demonstration required a more senior representative from the Presidency to receive the document.

He argued that the choice of Ms Jantuah did not reflect the seriousness of the issues raised by the opposition party.

GenCED, however, said actions or comments that diminish a woman performing an official duty risk reinforcing stereotypes that continue to affect women’s participation in leadership.

The group warned that such conduct could undermine efforts to promote greater inclusion and equality in governance, particularly at a time Ghana is advancing measures to improve women’s representation in public life.

“Political leaders have a responsibility to model respectful engagement and contribute to building a political culture that values inclusion, equality, and institutional respect,” GenCED said.

Nana Yaa Jantuah later expressed disappointment over the comments attributed to the Minority Leader, saying she felt disrespected because she was acting as a representative of the President and not in her personal capacity.

“I’m so mortified that you could stand there and look in the face of a woman and tell that woman she is nobody. I just cannot comprehend what happened,” she said in an interview on Asempa FM’s Ekosiisen.

She maintained that the focus should have been on the concerns contained in the NPP’s petition rather than questioning the person designated to receive it.

The NPP has since defended Mr Afenyo-Markin’s position, arguing that the issue was about the status of the delegation and the level of representation provided by the Presidency.

The Minority Leader later shared a video of a similar objection raised by former Minority Leader Dr Cassiel Ato Forson during an opposition demonstration, appearing to draw comparisons between the two incidents.

GenCED urged all political actors to reflect on the incident and promote respectful engagement regardless of political affiliation or gender.

“Respect for women in leadership is not a partisan matter; it is a democratic imperative,” the group added.

Ghana News.title: James Agalga tipped to replace Mahama Ayariga as NDC Majority Leader
Ghana News.content:
Builsa North Member of Parliament James Agalga is the leading contender to become the next Majority Leader of Parliament following Mahama Ayariga’s appointment to President John Dramani Mahama’s cabinet, sources within the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Caucus have told MyJoyOnline.

Mr Ayariga, who served as Majority Leader, has been reassigned as Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs in President Mahama’s first cabinet reshuffle announced on Friday, August 7, 2026.

Sources indicate that the NDC Caucus has settled on the former Deputy Minister for Interior over South Dayi MP Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor, who had also been tipped for the position.

The decision is yet to be formally announced by the NDC parliamentary leadership.

The Builsa North MP served as Deputy Minister for Interior during President Mahama’s previous administration and holds a Master’s degree in Conflict, Peace and Security from the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre.

He currently serves as Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Defence and Interior Committee, a role that has placed him at the centre of debates on national security and governance issues.

Party strategists are said to believe his experience in executive administration and parliamentary work will help him manage government business in the House.

The possible selection of Mr Agalga also maintains continuity in the NDC’s parliamentary leadership structure, as both he and Mr Ayariga are from the Upper East Region.

Sources suggest regional representation and parliamentary dynamics were among the factors considered during discussions over the replacement.

Mr Dafeamekpor, who has served as Majority Chief Whip since January 2025, was widely regarded as a strong contender for the position due to his experience coordinating parliamentary strategy and managing legislative business.

However, sources say the party ultimately favoured Mr Agalga’s approach and experience, particularly as the NDC prepares to manage an increasingly competitive parliamentary environment ahead of election 2028 in two and a half years.

The choice comes at a time when the Majority side will continue to engage with an assertive Minority led by Alexander Afenyo-Markin.

If confirmed, Mr Agalga’s immediate responsibility will be coordinating government legislative priorities, maintaining cohesion within the Majority side and steering parliamentary business ahead of the 2028 general election.

Ghana News.title: NSMQ 2026: The battle for academic supremacy begins as 157 schools prepare for national glory
Ghana News.content:
The countdown has begun. Across classrooms, libraries and science laboratories, students are sharpening their minds, revising formulas, testing their knowledge and preparing for one of Ghana’s most anticipated academic battles, the National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) 2026.

The prestigious competition is set to return with another season of intense intellectual rivalry as some of the country’s brightest young minds compete for national recognition, school pride and the coveted NSMQ trophy.

For participating schools, the journey is not just about answering questions correctly. It is about legacy, reputation and the opportunity to etch their names into the history books of Ghana’s academic excellence.

The organisers have announced that they are targeting 157 schools to compete at the national championship stage, with 27 schools already securing qualification for the ultimate contest.

In the coming weeks, the nation will witness fierce battles in science, mathematics, technology and general knowledge as schools fight for the bragging rights of being crowned champions.

The race officially begins on Thursday, August 13, 2026, with the launch and balloting ceremony, where schools will discover their pairings and begin mapping out their path to glory.

The preliminary stage is scheduled for Thursday, August 20 to Monday, August 24, 2026, before the competition enters the knockout phase.

The one-eighth stage will run from Wednesday, August 26 to Friday, August 28, followed by the quarter-finals from Sunday, August 30 to Tuesday, September 1.

The intensity will rise further as the remaining schools battle for a place in the semi-finals on Thursday, September 3.

Only three schools will survive the long academic marathon to compete for the ultimate prize at the grand finale on Thursday, September 10, 2026.

With past champions setting high standards and new contenders eager to announce themselves on the national stage, the 2026 edition promises another thrilling display of brilliance, strategy and academic excellence.

The question remains: Which school will rise above the rest and lift the NSMQ trophy?

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
