World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Iraqi Drilling Company completes well rehabilitation at West Qurna 1 oil field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) has successfully completed the rehabilitation of oil well WQ1-132 at the West Qurna 1 oil field, marking another step in Iraq’s efforts to enhance oil production efficiency and support the long-term development of its energy sector.

The project was carried out as part of the company’s operational program to improve well performance and maintain sustainable crude oil production.

According to a statement issued by the Iraqi Drilling Company, the rehabilitation work was completed in line with directives from Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi and under the supervision of the company’s Director General, Mohammed Hantoosh Asad Al-Azirjawi.

Technical and engineering teams carried out the operation using the company’s specialized expertise and equipment.

The company said the rehabilitation project forms part of its broader strategy to improve the efficiency of existing oil wells while supporting sustainable production across Iraq’s major oil fields.

Restoration work on producing wells helps maximize output, extend operational life, and improve field performance without the need for entirely new drilling operations.

The Iraqi Drilling Company emphasized that the successful completion of the project reflects the capabilities of its engineering and technical staff, who continue to execute specialized rehabilitation operations according to approved operational plans.

The company noted that relying on local expertise strengthens operational efficiency while supporting the continued development of Iraq’s oil infrastructure.

West Qurna 1 is one of Iraq’s largest producing oil fields and plays a significant role in the country’s crude oil output.

Ongoing rehabilitation and maintenance projects are designed to ensure production stability, improve operational reliability, and meet the technical requirements of field development programs.

The completion of well WQ1-132 is expected to contribute to maintaining efficient production operations within the field as Iraq continues investing in the modernization of its energy sector.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Kurdistan president discuss Erbil-Baghdad cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and the president of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Nechirvan Barzani, discussed on Wednesday the country’s political, economic, and security situation.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two leaders indicated that it is important to boost cooperation between the federal government and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) to enhance stability, address challenges, and serve the interests of the Iraqi people, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi affirmed the government’s commitment to resolving outstanding issues in line with the constitution, preserving Iraq’s unity, and strengthening national partnership.

Barzani stated that it is important to continue dialogue between national parties. He added that the KRG supports the federal government’s efforts to enhance stability and promote national development.

The discussions focused on approaches to secure the success of the government’s national agenda.

This high-level meeting comes after al-Zaidi’s trips to Turkey and Iran, where he met top officials, and Barzani’s visit to Damascus, where he met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

World.title: Iraq wins legal case in Jordan for Samarra Pharmaceutical Company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice has announced a legal victory before the Jordanian judiciary after securing a final court ruling in favor of the State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra, a subsidiary of the Ministry of Industry and Minerals.

The ruling requires a Jordanian company to pay financial compensation following a dispute over the supply of medical materials that failed to meet agreed specifications.

According to a statement from the Ministry of Justice, the ministry’s Legal Department successfully represented the Iraqi pharmaceutical company throughout all stages of the legal proceedings before Jordanian courts.

The case involved a supply contract under which the Jordanian company was expected to provide metal covers for medical supplies. However, the supplier allegedly delivered products that did not comply with the contractual specifications.

Director of the Legal Department, Haitham Mohi Radi, said the final judgment issued by the Jordanian Court of Cassation, and upheld by both the Court of Appeal and the Court of First Instance, ordered the Jordanian company to pay financial amounts to the Samarra-based pharmaceutical company.

The ruling concludes a lengthy legal process aimed at protecting the contractual rights of the Iraqi state-owned enterprise.

The Ministry of Justice described the outcome as an important achievement in safeguarding Iraq’s financial interests abroad.

Officials said the successful litigation reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to defend state institutions before international courts and judicial authorities while protecting public funds from contractual violations.

The ministry added that the case demonstrates the expertise and professionalism of Iraq’s legal teams in handling international commercial disputes.

By successfully pursuing the claim through multiple judicial levels in Jordan, the Legal Department reinforced Iraq’s commitment to enforcing contractual rights and ensuring accountability in cross-border commercial agreements.

The decision is expected to strengthen confidence in the government’s ability to defend the interests of Iraqi public institutions through legal channels.

World.title: Ammar Al-Hakim and Iranian Science Minister discuss academic cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s National State Forces Alliance, Ammar Al-Hakim, met with Iranian Minister of Science, Research and Technology Hossein Simaei Sarraf in Baghdad to discuss expanding academic cooperation between Iraq and Iran through university partnerships, knowledge exchange, and joint educational initiatives.

The meeting focused on strengthening higher education ties while emphasizing the role of universities in addressing labor market needs and societal challenges.

According to a statement released by Al-Hakim’s office, the two sides reviewed opportunities to deepen cooperation between Iraqi and Iranian universities by promoting twinning agreements, expanding academic collaboration, and exchanging expertise.

The discussions highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional relationships to support scientific research and educational development in both countries.

During the meeting, Al-Hakim stressed that university graduates should possess skills that match the demands of today’s job market.

He also urged academic institutions to prioritize scientific research that offers practical solutions to national challenges and contributes to sustainable development.

Al-Hakim emphasized the importance of equipping university students with strong scientific knowledge to prepare them for future professional opportunities.

The Iraqi political leader underscored the role of research institutions in supporting innovation and policymaking.

He noted that universities should focus on producing research capable of addressing economic, social, and developmental issues while enhancing academic excellence.

The discussion reflected a shared interest in strengthening educational cooperation as part of broader bilateral relations.

The meeting also touched on the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, with Al-Hakim praising the hospitality shown by Iraqis toward visitors traveling to commemorate Imam Hussein.

He said the event demonstrates positive values of solidarity and cooperation, while calling for stronger ties between societies based on shared humanitarian and religious principles.

The visit concluded with discussions on enhancing educational cooperation alongside broader people-to-people engagement between Iraq and Iran.

World.title: Iraq’s State Administration Coalition warns armed groups after September 30
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Administration Coalition has reaffirmed its support for restricting all weapons to state control, warning that any armed activity outside the authority of the government after September 30, 2026, will be treated under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

The position was announced following the coalition’s 37th regular meeting, hosted by Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi, with the participation of Iraq’s senior political and constitutional leaders.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the meeting brought together the President of the Republic, the Speaker of Parliament, the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the Kurdistan Region, and leaders of the State Administration Coalition.

Participants reviewed Iraq’s political, security, economic, and public service developments, as well as regional events and their impact on the country.

The coalition reiterated its backing for the government’s efforts to ensure that all weapons remain under state authority, in line with the government program approved by the Iraqi Parliament.

The coalition stressed that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries or for actions that could draw Iraq into regional conflicts.

It warned that individuals or groups engaging in such activities would be committing crimes that threaten national security.

According to the statement, after September 30, 2026, any armed activity conducted outside the state’s legal framework will be dealt with under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

Officials also cited constitutional provisions prohibiting the formation of armed organizations outside the official security forces.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi briefed coalition members on government efforts to strengthen security, improve public services, implement the ministerial program, and address Iraq’s financial and economic challenges.

The coalition emphasized the need to:

Maintain national security and stability.

Protect essential public services.

Diversify Iraq’s oil export routes.

Increase non-oil revenues.

Combat corruption, smuggling, and financial waste.

The meeting highlighted the government’s commitment to protecting citizens’ interests while strengthening economic resilience.

On regional affairs, coalition leaders expressed support for diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions across the Middle East.

The meeting reaffirmed Iraq’s rejection of resolving disputes through military force and emphasized Baghdad’s willingness to play a constructive role in promoting dialogue between regional parties.

Participants also discussed border security, counterterrorism cooperation, combating drug trafficking and organized crime, and strengthening relations with neighboring and international partners based on mutual respect and national sovereignty.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the State Administration Coalition called for accelerating the completion of the government formation process and submitting the government’s official program to the Council of Representatives for discussion and approval.

The coalition said completing these constitutional steps remains essential for advancing Iraq’s political stability and governance agenda.

World.title: Astrobase unveils 800kN rocket engine, eyes reusability
World.content:
BENGALURU: Space start-up Astrobase Space Technologies Friday unveiled what it described as Indiaâs first privately built â800kN Full-Flow Staged Combustion (FFSC) liquid oxygen-methane rocket engine, named âEverestââ, as it seeks to develop reusable launch systems and expand domestic launch infrastructure.

The Bengaluru-based company said the engine is designed for medium-lift launch vehicles and forms part of its long-term plan to build an integrated launch ecosystem covering propulsion, manufacturing, testing and launch operations. The next major milestone for the programme will be a full-engine hot-fire test, followed by vehicle integration and orbital launch development.

According to the company: âEverest uses the full-flow staged combustion cycle, one of the most complex rocket engine architectures, and is powered by liquid oxygen and methane.

The engine has been designed for reusability and offers 800 kN of thrust, a specific impulse of around 340 seconds and a throttle range of 50% to 110%.â

The company said it plans to manufacture up to 50 engines annually once its facilities are fully operational, with the capability to hot-fire about one engine every week. It aims to test around 20 engines before attempting its first orbital mission.

Its first phase of expansion is intended to support about 100 tonnes of annual launch capacity, with a longer-term goal of exceeding 1,000 tonnes through a higher launch cadence.





It also said it was âworking towards a launch-on-demand capability that could enable a dedicated mission within 15 days of an urgent national requirement. These targets are yet to be demonstratedâ.

Astrobase co-founder Neeraj Khandelwal said the engine was intended to establish an industrial capability rather than serve only as a technology demonstrator, adding that India would require indigenous high-thrust propulsion systems as satellite launches increase globally.

World.title: Former Nestle CMD Suresh Narayanan says India Inc needs to shed the ‘elite’ tag

Former Nestle CMD Suresh Narayanan in his new book, 'Courage Under Fire', writes that in a crisis people follow those they trust.

For over four decades,

Suresh Narayanan

has navigated boardrooms, brand battles and one of

India Inc

's defining crises. In â

Courage Under Fire

â (

Penguin Random House India

), the former NestlÃ© India chairman and managing director looks beyond business strategy to explore what truly shapes

leadership

.

In an exclusive chat with Lopamudra Ghatak, he argues that clarity matters more than charisma, challenges India's obsession with pedigree thatâs causing companies to overlook leadership potential, and reflects candidly on the lessons of the

Maggi

crisis. He also explains why

Gen Z

's approach to work-life balance deserves respect rather than ridicule, and recalls how a woman boss taught him that empathy is one of the key traits to being a good leader.

Congratulations on your book. How did the idea to write 'Courage Under Fire' come to you?

In 'Courage Under Fire' you write that "great leadership is not about position; itâs about responsibility, authenticity, and the ability to inspire trust, when it matters". In an increasingly trust-deficit and information-surplus world, how does a leader earn trust? And how does an organisation make trust a part of its DNA?

leadership. You mention in the book about visiting Tier-2 and Tier3- colleges, and how students there are often more grateful, hungry and eager to learn. Do you think they make better leaders?

After a 40-year career in corporate India, I wanted to leave behind a few lessons that had served me well. They're not prescriptions, but perspectives shaped by the crises and difficult moments I have experienced.'Courage Under Fire' is more of a personal journey through those defining moments - that focuses on people, purpose, partnerships, values, behaviour and outcomes. I thought it would be of some use to a younger generation entering the workforce.I think you've hit the nail on the head! Trust is the most valuable currency - for an individual as much as for an organisation. It emerges when three streams converge at one point in time.The first is purpose. Every organisation, and every individual, needs a clear sense of purpose, something that guides decisions and actions.The second is values. What do you want to be known for? What principles define how you conduct yourself, especially in adverse situations?Purpose and values, in turn, lead to the third element: authenticity. Unfortunately, in today's digital world, authenticity often gives way to performance.We spend too much time embellishing, instead of being genuine.Correct. Leadership isn't about saying what you'll do, it's about doing what you say. That's the dilemma many leaders face. Do they wear a(mask) that projects one image while concealing another?In order to establish trust among people, there has to be a convergence between purpose, values and authenticity, and that leads to outcomes. Over time, those actions create credibility, and credibility becomes trust.Trust is built when purpose, values and authenticity consistently translate into action. Over time, those actions create credibility, and credibility becomes trust.I've also come to see vulnerability as a strength, not a weakness. When people know you're human, that you have strengths as well as limitations, they know what to expect from you. Predictability in values and behaviour is reassuring. What people fear most is unpredictability.Ultimately, trust isn't about being the most liked person in the room. In a crisis, organisations don't rely on the most loved people; they rely on the most trusted ones. If I'm liked but not trusted, I won't be asked to lead when it matters. Trust, more than popularity, is what carries an organisation through difficult times.Leadership, for long, has suffered from some myths. The first is the myth of charisma - that great leaders must have magnetic personalities. The second is that complex communication (by leadership) is somehow superior. The third is executive presence: the belief that a leader must be a larger-than-life figure at any gathering and dominate every room they enter. And the fourth is the idea that leaders should only display their strengths while hiding every flaw, angularities.I don't subscribe to any of those myths. Leadership can absolutely be taught because, at its core, leadership is an act of being human.You don't have to be charismatic; you have to be clear. You don't have to be complex; you have to be transparent in your communication. You don't need the loudest voice or the most commanding presence. Some of history's greatest political and business leaders inspired people far beyond the reach of their voices.But leadership doesn't develop in isolation. It blooms through the right mentors, timely nudges and experiences. Looking back, I benefited from teachers, parents, colleagues, relatives and even competitors who pushed me to exceed my own expectations. Those influences gradually built confidence, not just the confidence to lead others, but the confidence to manage myself first.One thing we need to do as a society is demystify elitism. We place far too much value on where someone studied, where they work, the company they built or the organisation they belong to â as though those labels alone define success and achievement.Exactly, the tag culture. I believe those days should be behind us. Look at ISRO. They might have their own travails but the fact is that most of the talent that comes there are not from the premier institutions in the country and yet they do premier and outstanding work and make us proud as a nation.The same is true of organisations that consciously recruit from Tier-2 cities and smaller towns. I often find students there to be remarkably humble, eager and determined. They are trying to prove themselves against a system that has long suggested only the elite succeed.As leaders, we have to move away from that entitlement mindset and create space for talent to flourish. India has extraordinary talent. Some young people may not be the most articulate when speaking in English but they are capable of hard work and possess grit, discipline and can deliver on their promise each and every time.That's what the country needsânot people who merely preach from the pulpit, but people who consistently deliver.I think as a country now we are mature enough to realise that we cannot be a developing country or hope to become a wealthy country one day on the crutches of elitism. I think elitism is a crutch that we have to get out of as quickly as possible.I think the kind of companies that I worked in - Unilever, Colgate-Palmolive and Nestle - they always prided themselves in a middle-class culture. Their leaders weren't chosen because they came from privileged backgrounds; they rose through competence, commitment, energy and hard workI use the term middle class in a positive sense because it symbolises humility, integrity, transparency, trust and a strong work ethic. This is what middle-class India is, and these are the values we strive to teach our children. When those values enter an organisation, they become a source of strength.I do think the growing recognition of talent from Tier-2 institutions and smaller towns is slowly weakening elitism. But there's still work to be done. Our education system and employers must create more opportunities for capable graduates from less celebrated institutions.Too many people still believe admission to a top college guarantees success. Life doesn't work that way. Success is usually about moving two steps forward, one step back, and repeating that journey with resilience and consistency.There are two principles that have guided me throughout my career.The first is simple: a crisis never arrives with a calling card. You have to remain alert at all times. Don't be caught sleeping at the wheel. Anticipate risks before they balloon into crises.The second is to manage yourself before you manage others. That's often overlooked. When a crisis hits, we immediately focus on facts, meetings and firefighting. But we spend far less time asking:In a crisis, everyone's anxiety levels are elevated. The leader's role is to remain calm, anchored in the organisation's purpose and values, and provide stability.That's often the difference between a crisis handled well and one handled badly. The outcome rarely depends only on strategy. More often, it depends on leadershipâhow clearly you communicate, how consistently you act and how much confidence you inspire.The first lesson, that a crisis doesn't come with a calling card, certainly applies in this case. In hindsight, we could have done better in terms of sensing the environment and knowing that something was brewing in parts of the country. If we had been able to address it more comprehensively, maybe we would have been able to manage the outcome a lot better.Secondly, one of the important issues in managing a crisis is to have a single point of contact communicating to the environment. One criticism we faced was that we were slow in communicating. Looking back, I believe we could have responded faster.I don't know whether the dial has shifted enough in India to say that with confidence. But I do believe people follow leaders who are authentic, humane and emotionally present â not those who remain distant and issue instructions from above.Professor George Kohlrieser at IMD Business School describes a leader as a "secure base." I find that idea deeply meaningful. Just as we turn to a parent in moments of uncertainty, employees should feel they have someone they can approach with their fears, concerns and aspirations, someone who will provide anchorage in a crisis.Vulnerability, to me, is a source of strength. It acknowledges that you're still learning and growing. That's not weakness, it's humanity.We've long been told that men don't cry. But they do. Suppressing emotion doesn't make you stronger; it makes it harder to empathise. And empathy is one of the most powerful qualities a leader can possess.Wan Ling, who headed Nestle Asia-Oceania-Africa, was one of the toughest leaders I worked with. She could be incredibly demanding, yet deeply compassionate.What struck me most was that every conversation with her began with family. With many of my male bosses, business came first and family last. With her it was always, âHow is your family doing?â. Only then would we move on to tackle the toughest business crisis moments.One of her greatest strengths was her ability to read a room. She sensed what people were feeling before anyone uttered a word. Just as importantly, she had the ability to step back, consider various perspectives and avoid rushing into decisions. That balance of empathy and judgement made her an exceptional leader.I see it as a positive shift. The old belief that success demanded 80-hour work weeks came at a huge personal cost. You may have earned more, but you often missed out on family, friendships and life's important moments. There's little value in reaching 80 and regretting that you never spent enough time with your parents or your children. So I welcome this change.These youngsters are not work-shy. They simply want work to coexist with life, and I think that's a healthy aspiration. I only wish my generation had the courage to tell our bosses at seven in the evening that we were leaving to meet family or friends. Instead, we stayed back until the boss switched off the lights, as though commitment was measured by the last person to leave the office.That said, balance has to be calibrated. Every generation has something to learn from the other.What also strikes me about young professionals is that they're driven by experiences. They move from one challenge to another in search of learning and fulfillment. I would encourage them to embrace the challenge itself rather than becoming overly anxious about the outcome. Careers are rarely linear. If you focus on learning, growth and doing meaningful work, the outcomes usually take care of themselves.

World.title: 'News, Spice Rani, He Ram': Names on police merit list triggers row in Chhattisgarh
World.content:
The unusual names prompted the opposition Congress to question the credibility of the selection process. (Representative image)

What really happened

What the board said

Several candidates clarify

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: What began as a routine police recruitment result in Chhattisgarh quickly turned into an internet sensation after candidates with names such as 'News', 'Space Rani', 'He Ram', 'Bhakt Prahlad' and 'Tufail' appeared on the list of successful applicants, sparking disbelief, political allegations and eventually, a defence from the candidates themselves.The unusual names, which surfaced in the results of the Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission's (CGPSC) preliminary examination for police recruitment, prompted the opposition Congress to question the credibility of the selection process.The commission, however, dismissed the allegations, insisting that the names were genuine and matched the details submitted by candidates during registration.The controversy erupted after the results of the preliminary examination for 341 posts of subedar, sub-inspector and platoon commander were declared on August 4. A total of 7,301 candidates qualified for the mains examination.According to the CGPSC, the candidates had appeared for document verification, physical tests and the preliminary examination under the same names, which were also printed on their admit cards.Former chief minister Bhupesh Baghel mocked the list after sharing it on X."The Public Relations Department should spend Rs 1 crore daily on s to display this achievement at public intersections so that, in the coming days, 'Radio' and 'Space Raja' might also succeed in some examination."State Congress communication wing chief Sushil Anand Shukla accused the BJP government of failing to deliver transparent recruitment despite promising PSC examinations on the lines of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).He alleged that the names reflected the alleged "negligence" of the CGPSC and the state government and claimed that several recruitment and promotion examinations held over the past two-and-a-half years had come under suspicion.Rejecting the allegations, the CGPSC described the claims circulating on social media as "misleading and baseless" and said they unfairly ridiculed candidates over their names."The names of the candidates displayed in the examination result are the same as those entered by them in their online application forms, which they finally submitted. The candidates appeared for document and physical tests as well as the preliminary examination under these names, and their names were also displayed accordingly on their admit cards," it stated.The commission urged candidates and the public not to believe misinformation and rely only on information published on its official website.As the debate gathered pace online, several candidates clarified that the names attracting attention were the same as those recorded in their official documents."My name is News Kumar Pradhan. My surname was not added to my Class 10 marksheet. My marksheets of Classes 10 and 12 and Aadhaar card carry the name News, without the surname. People think that the name is incorrect," said News Kumar Pradhan, who qualified in the preliminary examination. He added that he is from Bhatanpali village in Raigarh district.Tufail, a 29-year-old candidate from Nayapara in Raipur district, said his name appeared the same in all official records."After the result was released, rumours are being spread about names such as Spacerani, News and Tufail without any information or facts. These are the names of students who have prepared for the examination for years," he said.He appealed against spreading rumours and said such claims were hurting the morale of candidates from ordinary families.Another successful candidate, He Ram, said there was nothing unusual about the way his name was recorded."My name is He Ram, and I have qualified the PSC preliminary examination. Some people are raising objections over my name. My surname is Kashyap, but it is not mentioned in any of my documents. Hence, I entered only my name while filling the form," he told PTI.Bhakt Prahlad also clarified that his name was correctly recorded in all official documents."My surname is not mentioned. Please do not spread confusion regarding my name," he said.

World.title: Monsoon Session: Congress issues whip to MPs ahead of FCRA Bill discussion in Parliament
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday issued a whip to its MPs, directing them to be present in both the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha as the government is set to take up the contentious FCRA Amendment Bill for discussion.

Congress has asked its parliamentarians to remain present in their respective Houses on August 10, 11 and 12.

"Very important issues will be taken up for discussion in the Rajya Sabha on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, i.e. August 10, 11 and 12, 2026," Congress chief whip in the Rajya Sabha said in the whip.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"All Members of Congress Party in the Rajya Sabha are requested to kindly remain present in the House from 11.00 am onwards till the adjournment of the House on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, i.e.

August 10, 11 and 12, 2026, without fail and support the party stand. This may be treated as most important," the whip, issued by Chief Whip Jairam Ramesh, said.

An identical whip was issued to Congress members in the Lok Sabha.

Congress has also conveyed to all INDIA bloc allies to ensure that their MPs remain present on the three days, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.

The move comes as the government is set to take up the FCRA Amendment Bill and is also considering reintroducing the Constitution Amendment Bill on delimitation.

However, while listing the tentative government business for next week, minister of state for parliamentary affairs made no mention of either the FCRA Amendment Bill or the Constitution Amendment Bill on delimitation.

World.title: 'Avoid Lutyens web': PM Modi's advice to 45 NDA MPs at breakfast meet
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Friday met 45 National Democratic Alliance (NDA) MPs at a breakfast meeting amid the stormy Parliament monsoon session, advising the parliamentarians to "not carry the anxiety from inside the House to outside" and avoid the "web of Lutyens' Delhi".

In the meeting, which also included the rebel factions from the Uddhav Sena and Mamata Banerjee's

, PM Modi said: "No one should say anything trashy on TV. Maintain full dignity at all times. Engage actively in social media through Facebook, Instagram and X; interact with youth, inform government welfare work, encourage youth for sports activities."

Modi advised the MPs to follow the party line and calmly present their views on every issue and that there was "no need to speak angrily or shout (in House) in anger".

"Do not carry the anxiety from inside the House to outside. Because sometimes there is such an atmosphere in the House that it causes anxiety, you should not carry it with you. There is also no need to speak angrily or shout in anger. You all know the party line, and you should calmly present your views on every issue," said PM Modi as per the sources who informed news agency ANI.

NDA a 'collective identity'

Jagdish Basunia, a leader of the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), which was formed after breaking away from the TMC, described his meeting with Modi as a "great interaction," noting that the Prime Minister emphasised the collective identity of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) as a "family."





Speaking to ANI after the session, Basunia characterised the meeting as highly cordial and focused on the shared goal of national development.

"It was a great interaction with PM Modi over breakfast today, a very cordial meeting. PM told us we are all part of the NDA family. Let's work together for public welfare, the way NDA works," Basunia said.

World.title: Uttarakhand Forward 2.0 | Manoj Pant maps out development roadmap to 2047
World.content:
Uttarakhand Forward 2.0 is the second edition of The Times of India's flagship video series spotlighting the state's journey of growth, innovation and transformative governance.

Through exclusive conversations with policymakers, administrators, industry leaders, educationists and experts, the series explores the ideas, initiatives and vision shaping Uttarakhand's future across infrastructure, clean energy, education, tourism, sustainability and more. The campaign highlights the policies driving progress, the challenges and opportunities ahead, and the roadmap for the state's next phase of development.

In this episode of Uttarakhand 2.0, Richa Jain Kalra is in conversation with Dr Manoj Kumar Pant, Director, Department of Planning, Government of Uttarakhand, about the state's long-term vision. From migration and rural development to climate resilience, digital connectivity and infrastructure, the conversation explores how today's decisions will shape Uttarakhand's future for generations to come. As India moves towards the centenary of its independence in 2047, the discussion examines what it will take for Uttarakhand to emerge as a resilient, sustainable, and future-ready state over the next two decades.

World.title: Karnataka legislative council chairman Basavaraj Horatti resigns
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

leader Basavaraj Horatti on Friday tendered his resignation as Chairman of the

Legislative Council.

Asked about the reason behind his decision, Horatti said, "I was asked to resign, so I tendered my resignation."

"I don't know why they (the Congress government) asked me to resign," he added.

Horatti also admitted that he was under pressure to resign.

Horatti, who was previously with the Janata Dal (Secular), joined the BJP on May 18, 2022, a year before the Congress came to power in Karnataka.

He said the Congress government, led by D K Shivakumar, mounted pressure on him ahead of the Legislative Council session beginning on August 13.

World.title: Assam records world’s first-ever release of captive-bred slender-billed vultures
World.content:
Guwahati

Five slender-billed vultures bred in captivity at the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS)’s conservation facility in Assam were released into the wild on Friday, marking the first such release anywhere in the world.

The birds, along with five captive-bred white-rumped vultures, were transported from the Vulture Conservation Breeding Centre at Rani near Guwahati and released at the Jatayu Soft Release Centre in the Biswanath Division of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve.

BNHS deputy director Sachin Ranade said that captive-bred white-rumped vultures (Gyps bengalensis) had been released earlier. “This is the first such release of the captive-bred slender-billed vulture (Gyps tenuirostris) in the world,” he said.

He said the 10 scavengers were shifted from the Rani centre three months ago for acclimatisation at a vulture-release aviary in Biswanath’s Tewaripal area. They were released in the presence of Assam’s Environment and Forest Minister Jayanta Mallabaruah, senior Forest Department officials, and others.

The population of Gyps vultures in India has declined by 99% over the last 20 years due to the use of veterinary painkillers. Although the Centre banned four such drugs—diclofenac, aceclofenac, ketoprofen, and nimesulide—pesticide poisoning remains a threat to vultures in Assam. The BNHS has identified these dangers and has collaborated with the State’s Forest Department on the vulture breeding conservation programme since 2007.

“All the vultures have a numbered, blue ring around the leg and a tag on their backs. These vultures are expected to stay in the area and mix up with the vulture populations around,” Mr Ranade said.

More than 700 vultures, including Himalayan griffons, have died in Assam due to accidental secondary poisoning since 2018. These mass deaths usually happen when these birds feed on carcasses laced with toxic pesticides, often used illegally to target stray or feral dogs.

Wildlife officials said awareness drives are conducted periodically to prevent people from using banned medicines for livestock or from spraying pesticides on dead animals. “We tell people to let the vultures take care of carcasses, their natural food,” an official said.

World.title: Centre spent ₹69,860 crore on Telangana cotton procurement, says Kishan Reddy on National Handloom Day
World.content:
The Centre has spent over ₹69,860 crore on procuring cotton from Telangana farmers under the Minimum Support Price (MSP) mechanism, Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy said on the occasion of National Handloom Day on Friday.

The Minister said the upcoming PM MITRA Mega Textile Park in Warangal would integrate traditional textile practices with state-of-the-art machinery, creating new opportunities for the handloom and textile sectors in the State.

Highlighting the Centre’s efforts to strengthen the textile value chain, Mr. Kishan Reddy said the Modi Government was implementing the ‘Make in India’ initiative alongside the ‘5F’ vision: Farm to Fibre, Fibre to Fabric, Fabric to Fashion and Fashion to Foreign Markets. He said incentives worth about ₹9 lakh crore are being extended up to 2030 to promote growth in the sector.

According to the Minister, weavers are being supported through a range of initiatives, including the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme, PM MITRA Parks, the National Handloom Development Programme, the Raw Material Supply Scheme and the Weavers’ Mudra Scheme. These programmes provide assistance in the form of modern looms, raw materials, worksheds, design development, marketing support, credit facilities and social security measures.

Mr. Kishan Reddy said the government was also integrating technology with the handloom and textile sectors to improve productivity, quality and market access. Emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, automation and advanced analytics are being leveraged to make the sector more competitive, he added.

Describing the handloom and textile industry as a vital pillar of India’s economy, the Minister said it provides direct and indirect employment to nearly five crore people and generates substantial foreign exchange earnings for the country.

BJP chief

Meanwhile, Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao extended greetings to handloom weavers, artisans and their families on National Handloom Day. He said the observance revives the spirit of the Swadeshi movement and reflects India’s rich weaving heritage.

Referring to Telangana’s handloom tradition, Mr. Rao said regions such as Narayanpet, Kothakota, Gadwal, Pochampally and Sircilla have earned global recognition for their distinctive products. He appealed to the public to support weavers by purchasing and wearing handloom fabrics, thereby strengthening the livelihoods of handloom families.

Organisational meeting

A Telangana BJP organisational meeting was also held at the party’s national headquarters in New Delhi with national president Nitin Nabin. The meeting was attended by Mr. Ramchander Rao, Mr. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Rajya Sabha member K. Laxman, and Lok Sabha members Dharmapuri Arvind, Godam Nagesh, Konda Vishweshwar Reddy, and Raghunandan Rao. Telangana in-charge Abhay Patil and State General Secretary (Organisation) Chandrashekhar Tiwari also attended the meeting.

World.title: Basavaraj Horatti resigns as Karnataka Legislative Council Chairperson
World.content:
Karnataka Legislative Council Chairperson Basavaraj Horatti submitted his resignation from the post on August 7, making way for the Congress to have one of its own members to preside over the Upper House.

Congress has named its senior leader Saleem Ahmed as the candidate for the position. He is expected to be officially anointed Chairperson on August 14. Till such time, Mr. Horatti would continue as pro-tem Speaker.

There had been several rounds of talks with Mr. Horatti on the issue, with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar taking the lead in an effort to persuade him to resign of his own volition to avoid the embarrassment of a no-confidence motion. Congress now enjoys a majority in the 75-member Legislative Council.

While the monsoon session of the Karnataka legislature starts on August 13, Mr. Horatti had on August 6 told mediapersons that he would address the Council about the circumstances of his resignation before stepping down. However, after another round of talks with Mr. Shivakumar and other legislators, he submitted his resignation on August 7.

Speaking after a meeting with Mr. Horatti, the Chief Minister said that he would be designated pro-tem Speaker as per procedure and would preside over the session on August 13, and officially resign thereafter on August 14.

Mr. Horatti said he would appoint the Deputy Chairperson and submit his resignation to him. Currently, the post of Deputy Chairperson is vacant after M.K. Pranesh lost his position following a legal battle, over counting of votes, to A.V. Gayatri Shante Gowda of the Congress. The resignation submitted by Mr. Horatti has been accepted by the Council Secretary, in the absence of the Deputy Speaker. Incidentally, Ms. Shante Gowda was sworn in by Mr. Horatti on August 7.

The opposition BJP has taken exception to the manner in which Mr. Horatti is being ‘forced’ to step down. It has also taken exception to Mr. Horatti going to the Chief Minister’s residence for a meeting.

Mr. Horatti brushed aside the criticism and said, “I met the Chief Minister to thank him for co-operating for this long. I will conduct the House on August 13, appoint a Deputy Speaker and tender my resignation formally.”

Former minister Umashree is the Congress’ nominee for the post of Deputy Chairperson.

An eight-time MLC, Mr. Horatti has been a member of the Legislative Council for 46 years. He has two years remaining in his current term.

World.title: Centre sanctions 14 new day-care cancer centres for Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
The Union government has approved the establishment of 14 new day-care cancer centres in Andhra Pradesh as part of its nationwide initiative to expand access to cancer treatment facilities at the district level.

Replying to the question raised by Vijayawada MP Kesineni Chinni in the Lok Sabha, Union Health and Family Welfare Minister J.P. Nadda said the Centre proposed to establish day-care cancer centres across district hospitals over three years, in line with the announcement made in the 2025–26 Union Budget.

Mr. Nadda informed the House that 524 such centres were currently functioning across the country. He said the Centre had so far approved 313 new centres under the programme and would consider additional proposals submitted by States and Union Territories based on local requirements.

For Andhra Pradesh, the Centre sanctioned 14 new facilities during the 2025–26 Financial Year. The Union government allocated ₹2.40 crore for the establishment of each centre and ₹1.49 crore annually for operational expenses from the second year onwards. The Minister said that 23 day-care cancer centres were already functioning in the State.

The programme was being implemented under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD), with the State governments expected to identify requirements on the basis of gap analyses and submit proposals accordingly.

Mr. Chinni said the establishment of additional centres would significantly improve access to cancer treatment by enabling patients to receive care closer to their homes, thereby reducing the need to travel long distances for treatment.

He also said that efforts would continue to secure approval for additional centres in the areas where demand for cancer care services remains high.

World.title: Two arrested for youth’s murder near Kinathukadavu in Coimbatore
World.content:
The police on Friday arrested two persons, including a 16-year-old boy, for murdering a youth from their neighbourhood near Kinathukadavu in Coimbatore district early on Thursday.

Mathesh (22) and a 16-year-old boy from Sikkalampalayam near Kinathukadavu were arrested for the murder of S. Aswin (22) from the neighbouring Solavampalayam village. Mathesh allegedly suffered a fracture on his right arm when the police tried to apprehend him.

According to the police, the accused and the deceased knew each other. Aswin, a construction labourer, went to his friend Vishnu’s house at Sikkalampalayam on Wednesday night, consumed alcohol with him and slept over.

The two accused trespassed into house in the early hours of Thursday and assaulted Aswin, who was under the influence of alcohol, due to previous enmity. They recorded videos of the assault and took a selfie with the victim’s body, which were posted on Instagram.

The police launched a hunt for the two accused who escaped after the murder. The two were arrested on Friday. Mathesh was brought to Coimbatore Medical College Hospital for a medical examination of his fracture.

World.title: Two pedestrians killed after tipper lorry rams them in Ballari district
World.content:
Two pedestrians were killed on the spot after a speeding tipper lorry allegedly rammed them from behind near Venkatagiri village in Sandur taluk of Ballari district on Thursday (August 6) evening.

The deceased have been identified as Kumar, 34, and Manjunath, 38, both residents of Hampinakatte village in Hospet taluk. Both men succumbed to their injuries on the spot.

According to a press release issued by Ballari Superintendent of Police Suman D. Pennekar, the accident occurred near agricultural land belonging to Seethabai on Venkatagiri Road, within the limits of Sandur Police Station.

The tipper lorry was allegedly being driven in a rash and negligent manner when it hit the pedestrians.

A case has been registered at Sandur Police Station under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act. An investigation is under way.

The police have taken the lorry driver into custody and initiated further legal proceedings.

The Superintendent of Police warned owners of mineral transport vehicles to ensure that their vehicles and drivers possess all valid statutory documents. She said stringent legal action would be taken not only against vehicle owners and drivers operating without valid documentation, but also against mining companies that permit transportation of minerals without verifying the required documents.

World.title: SIR: Deadline for enumeration phase in Karnataka extended again; draft rolls to be published on August 24
World.content:
The enumeration phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which was scheduled to end on Saturday, has been extended till August 17, the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Karnataka, announced on Friday. This is the second extension granted for the exercise.

The draft electoral rolls, scheduled to be published on August 17, will now be released on August 24. The period for filing claims and objections will run from August 24 to September 23, while the final electoral rolls will be published on October 27.

The extension comes days after civil society groups urged the Election Commission to extend the exercise following the publication of the Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others (ASDDO) list, arguing that voters needed adequate time to check whether they had been wrongly classified and approach their Booth Level Officers (BLOs) for corrections.

Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president B.K. Hariprasad had also written to the Karnataka CEO on August 6, seeking a 15-day extension.

With the deadline now extended, voters whose names have been wrongly included in the ASDDO list have time till August 17 to get their details corrected.

As of 4 p.m. on Friday, only 182 enumeration forms were pending digitisation across the State — from Bengaluru South and Belagavi districts.

Meanwhile, the share of voters placed under the ASDDO category has declined from 20.02% on August 5 to 19.81%, indicating that many voters had been wrongly placed under this category.

World.title: TG leveraging emerging tech to improve governance, public service delivery
World.content:
From issuing blockchain-based certificates, rolling out high-speed digital connectivity to rural areas to plans for a digital legislature, a number of emerging technologies-based initiatives are on the cards in Telangana, IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu said on Friday.

The Minister, who was inaugurating an AI Transformation Conclave jointly organised by GOVconnect and Electronic Service Delivery (MeeSeva) here, cited the plans while pointing to how Telangana was leveraging emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Blockchain, Data Analytics and Quantum Computing to improve governance and public service delivery.

On the State’s digital governance initiatives, he said Telangana had introduced a Digital Cabinet, a real-time government dashboard integrating 20 departments; the country’s first AI-powered data exchange; WhatsApp-based citizen services; and the Mee Ticket platform. There are plans to introduce a Digital Assembly and a Digital Council as part of efforts to modernise governance through technology.

Mr. Sridhar Babu said the government was planning to roll out Blockchain-based certificates to enhance security and authenticity of citizens’ data. Efforts were also under way to extend high-speed digital connectivity to rural areas through T-Fiber while ensuring doorstep delivery of government services to senior citizens and persons with disabilities.

The government was implementing paperless administration across departments under the Digital Office Project. Governance must evolve with technological advancements to become more efficient, transparent and citizen-centric, he said.

Chief Economic Adviser to the Maharashtra Chief Minister’s Office and CEO of MITRA Praveen Pardeshi; Centre for Railway Information Systems Managing Director GVL Satya Kumar; National Internet Exchange of India CEO Devesh Tyagi; and Additional Secretary-Direct Benefit Transfer to the Government of India Saurabh K. Tiwari participated in the conclave, the Minister’s office said.

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) of Law and Justice and Minister of State of Parliamentary Affairs Arjun Ram Meghwal had recently informed Lok Sabha that 33 out of the 37 State/UT legislatures have signed MoUs – Telangana is one of them -- for implementation of the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA). Of them, 21 Legislative Houses have been transformed into digital Legislatures under the NeVA project.

The NeVA public portals are equipped with AI-driven multilingual translation tools developed by BHASHINI, enabling content translation into the 22 Scheduled Indian Languages and English. Several safeguards have been incorporated into NeVA software suite to provide the Legislatures with a robust, secure, and resilient digital environment for conducting legislative business.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign tripartite defence agreement in Makkah
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in Makkah that empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Türkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence” held at Al-Safa Palace.

The three countries announced the signing of the agreement in a joint statement published by the Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency.

The statement said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.”

It also “provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added.

The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”.

During the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted.

Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well, pictures showed.

Sealing the agreement in Makkah, the holiest site in Islam, adds symbolic heft to a pact that builds on longstanding bilateral military ties among the three countries.

The agreement ties together Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed Muslim country; Saudi Arabia, the home to Islam’s holiest sites and one of the world’s top oil exporters; and Turkiye, Nato’s second-largest military.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the agreement “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race; rather, it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” he wrote on X.

He noted that the deal “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states”.

The Saudi official further said the agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

Mansoor Ahmed, of the Australian National University’s Strategic and Defence Studies Centre, said Islamabad and Ankara bring strong defence industries to the table, while Riyadh could contribute with technological spending.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

The three countries, along with Egypt, have been closely involved in efforts to promote regional stability and contain the regional upheaval sparked by the US-Iran war.

The regional conflagration has rained missile fire onto Gulf oil exporters, with Iran targeting Gulf countries in retaliation for attacks carried out against it using US military bases in the region.

The deal also comes as a 2022 truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in Yemen has broken down.

After the two sides traded fire for the first time in years last month, Houthis declared a maritime blockade against the kingdom, threatening access to its ports, and has claimed to have attacked Saudi tankers in the Red Sea.

Pakistan had condemned the Houthis’ threats to Saudi Arabia and to trading with the kingdom via the Red Sea. It also warned that it had the right to self-defence if its “maritime interests” were targeted in “any hostile act”.

As the conflict expanded onto new fronts, Saudi Arabia last week unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, have voiced support for the coalition.

Saudi crown prince meets PM Shehbaz, Erdogan

Crown Prince Salman held separate meetings with PM Shehbaz and President Erdogan at the Al-Safa Palace earlier in the day.

DPM Dar, CDF Munir and Asif were also present in the meeting with PM Shehbaz, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

Meanwhile, Erdogan’s office confirmed on X that he also held a meeting with Crown Prince Salman.

PM Shehbaz arrived in Saudi Arabia on a three-day visit on Thursday, while the Turkish president undertook a one-day visit today, Anadolu Agency reported.

Erdogan landed at King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah, from where he departed for Makkah by road, the Turkish news outlet reported.

PM Shehbaz had landed in Jeddah on Thursday. CDF Munir later joined the Pakistani delegation, which also included Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Special Assistant to PM Tariq Fatemi.

On Friday morning, the delegation visited the Holy Kaaba and performed Umrah, the PMO said. PM Shehbaz is also expected to visit Masjid-i-Nabvi (PBUH) in Madina.

According to an earlier statement by the FO, discussions between the two sides were to “focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relations as well as exchange of views on regional and international developments of mutual interests”.

The FO had noted that although the visit was taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, it carries “significance beyond the immediate crises and short-term considerations”.

It said the visit will “further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest, and reinforce multilateral cooperation”.

“The visit marks Pakistan’s long-standing partnership with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia anchored in decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood,” the FO had emphasised.

Pakistan has provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Turkiye and Pakistan have exchanged warships and training aircraft.

In 2023, Riyadh agreed to buy Turkish drones in what Ankara called its largest defence export contract. In April this year, Saudi Arabia said it received a military force and fighter jets from Pakistan to boost the kingdom’s security.

Additional input from AFP and Reuters

World.title: Schedule for 3rd phase of AJK polls revised over law and order concerns
World.content:
The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Election Commission on Friday revised the schedule for the third phase of elections in the region, saying polling would only be held in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts on August 10 amid concerns over the law and order situation.

Elections are being held across AJK in three phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities. Polls in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively.

The third phase in Poonch division was set for August 10. Poonch Division comprises 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, the Election Commission said in a press release on Friday that the electoral process will go ahead as planned on August 10 in only the division’s Bagh and Haveli districts.

In its press release, the AJK Election Commission said polling will be held in the three constituencies of Bagh and one of Haveli on August 10 as per the previous schedule.

However, the electoral process in the constituencies of Poonch district and Sudhnoti’s Pallandri will not be held on August 10, it said. The Election Commission said it reviewed the “current situation” regarding the scheduled elections in Poonch.

It noted that according to a report it received from the AJK home secretary, there were “concerns over the law and order situation in some areas of Poonch district and Pallandri district”.

“Moreover, the Election Commission received requests from some political personalities and candidates hailing from these districts, in which it has been requested to postpone the elections in Poonch district and Pallandri district considering the current situation,” the press release read.

The electoral watchdog said it will announce the new polling dates and a revised election schedule for Poonch and Pallandri after reviewing the situation and “considering all relevant matters”.

The commission clarified that the decision to postpone some of the polls was taken “only in the context of the current law and order situation to ensure that elections are held in a free, fair, transparent and peaceful environment”.

The Election Commission’s decision comes in the wake of clashes that took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Poonch district’s Rawalakot on July 27, which reportedly resulted in several casualties.

Rawalakot has been gripped by unrest since early June, with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) staging sit-ins periodically.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

The government has accused militant elements “pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest.

Earlier this week, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal noted that the “law and order situation and the demands of the safety of voters play an important role in holding elections”.

Responding to a question, he had said that under the AJK constitution, the current Legislative Assembly ceases to exist after August 4.

“Even if elections cannot be held in two or a few more constituencies, one cannot say that the house is not complete or those who have returned cannot take oath or perform their functions,” he explained.

He said the new assembly would still take oath after the completion of the August 10 polls.

Election Commission addresses malpractice allegations

On Friday, the Election Commission also responded to allegations of electoral malpractices and rigging, noting that a candidate claimed the previous day that Forms-24 had not been provided to polling agents at some polling stations.

The allegation was made by PPP’s Raja Muhammad Shakeel Khan, which the Election Commission denied.

“The Election Commission has not received any complaint regarding any constituency or polling station till now. The relevant presiding officers provided Forms-24 to polling agents at polling stations in line with law and the electoral practice,” its press release said.

The Election Commission further said some candidates had also tried to create an impression that it allotted election symbols at a matter of its prerogative.

“This impression is baseless and contrary to the facts. The symbols are allotted in accordance with the legal process described under AJK Elections Rules, 2020 and Form-42,” it said, adding that the commission allotted symbols without any bias towards or against any candidate.

PML-N has already won: Rana Sana

Meanwhile, PML-N leader and Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah addressed a public gathering in AJK’s Haveli, where he said his party had already won the required number of seats in AJK and was set to form the government.

He said 23 seats were required for a simple majority in the assembly, while the PML-N had already won 24.

Sanaullah told the rally’s participants that the PML-N would focus on development in AJK, which he said had been witnessed in the past every time the party was in the government in the Centre and AJK at the same time.

World.title: Bilawal claims 'certain elements' within PML-N are sowing division among allies, undermining PM Shehbaz
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari claimed on Friday that certain elements within the ruling PML-N were undermining Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and sowing discord between him and his political allies.

The PPP and the PML-N have been engaged in a war of words since the latter emerged in the lead in Mirpur polls on July 27. The PML-N has also won the majority of the seats in the second phase , with the PPP accusing it of rigging and other violent tactics in both phases.

The PPP chief was addressing an election rally in Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s Poonch district, where the third phase of elections in the region is slated to be held.

“High-profile people are saying that the government has collapsed. I’m not saying that, nor am I casting doubt on the prime minister’s intentions. He’s a good man with good intentions. But what can he do when the people around him have bad intentions?” Bilawal asked.

In reference to remarks he made earlier this week, the party chief highlighted that the PPP did not start the “countdown” to the government’s collapse, but rather these elements within the ruling party.

“The PML-N’s fight is not with the PPP — it happens in elections, as it has before. The real fight is entirely different, because the PM, with his good intentions and actions, is undermined by a large part of the PML-N,” Bilawal alleged.

“A big part of the PML-N wants the PM to fight not only the opposition, but also his own allies.”

He then asked the audience: “Have there ever been elections held in six phases in Kashmir’s history? If Kashmir is one, then the election should have been held on a single day.”

Bilawal said the elections were being held in phases “so that there is calm and the elections are peaceful, free and fair”, before asking: “But in which phase were the elections free, fair or peaceful?”

“In truth, elections were carried out in phases so they could rig them. They knew that 10 seats were in their pocket from the start,” he alleged.

“With the 10 seats in their pocket, they robbed Mirpur, they robbed Muzaffarabad, and they’re looking at you, in Poonch. They are looking at Bagh. On August 10, they will find out that those in Poonch and Bagh hunt tigers.”

Elections are being held across AJK in three phases . Polls in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively.

The first phase of polling in Mirpur saw the PML-N secure nine of the 13 seats while the PPP won the remaining four.

In the second phase in Muzaffarabad, the PML-N bagged 15 more seats, while the PPP managed to add just six more to its tally.

The third phase in Poonch division was set for August 10. Poonch Division comprises 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, earlier today, the AJK Election Commission revised the schedule for the third phase of elections in the region, saying polling would only be held in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts on August 10 amid concerns over the law and order situation.

The electoral process in the constituencies of Poonch district and Sudhnoti’s Pallandri would not be held on August 10, the Election Commission said, adding that it reviewed the “current situation” regarding the scheduled elections in Poonch.

It noted that according to a report it received from the AJK home secretary, there were “concerns over the law and order situation in some areas of Poonch district and Pallandri district”.

The commission’s decision comes in the wake of clashes that took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Poonch district’s Rawalakot on July 27, which reportedly resulted in several casualties.

Rawalakot has been gripped by unrest since early June , with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) staging sit-ins periodically.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

World.title: JI protests cause traffic disruptions across Karachi
World.content:
Several major thoroughfares in Karachi were blocked or affected by traffic disruptions on Friday as Jamaat-i-Islami held protest sit-ins in the city as part of a nationwide demonstration against the petroleum levy.

A day earlier, the party announced that it would stage sit-ins at 510 locations across the country by blocking major roads.

In a traffic advisory issued, the Karachi traffic police warned that traffic flow could be affected due to the protests and sit-ins, with slow-moving traffic, temporary diversions and partial road closures expected on several major thoroughfares.

The affected areas included Mazar-i-Quaid, Numaish Chowrangi, Saddar, Shahrah-i-Faisal, Shahrah-i-Pakistan, UP Mor, Power House Chowrangi, Defence Housing Authority, Sea View, Shahrah-i-Orangi, Hub River Road, Super Highway and National Highway.

The traffic police advised citizens to avoid travelling to the affected areas unless necessary, and urged them to select alternative routes and allow extra travel time before setting out.

Meanwhile, according to the latest updates shared on JI Karachi’s official X account, party workers had begun staging sit-ins at the announced locations.

According to the updates, workers had blocked the road leading to Natha Khan from Shahrah-i-Faisal. The Super Highway and Hub River Road were also blocked.

Other parts of country

Meanwhile, JI workers also gathered at the designated sit-in locations in other provincial capitals, including Lahore, Quetta, Peshawar and Islamabad.

According to reports, Srinagar Highway had been blocked as protesters gathered at Golra Mor to march towards Chungi 26.

In Sindh, protesters also staged sit-ins in Thatta, Matiari, Tando Allahyar, Shikarpur and other districts.

World.title: Exhumation of Mir Raza Ali's body postponed after family objects to abrupt reconstitution of medico-legal board
World.content:
KARACHI: The exhumation of 25-year-old businessman and Institute of Business Administration graduate Mir Raza Ali’s body was postponed on Friday after his family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of the medico-legal board.

Ali’s body was found in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28. While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, investigators probing the incident continue to build their case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

His family was present at the cemetery adjacent to Tariq Road’s Rehmania Masjid for the exhumation on Friday. But, the exhumation was deferred, with the counsel for Ali’s family, Jibran Nasir, telling the media that they had informed the investigating officer that the family had rejected the reconstituted board and would not accept an exhumation by it “under any circumstances”.

Standing alongside Ali’s father, Mir Hussain Ali Khan, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts and held the police, health ministry and the Sindh government responsible for the delay.

The family could not allow the examination to be performed by members whose “qualifications and intentions were under question”, he added.

He recalled that the previous night, Hyderabad health director general dismissed the original board and reconstituted it, adding four names from Hyderabad.

Nasir claimed that following outcry over the reconstituted board, the DG health then issued a backdated notification at around 10am on Friday. “He says more members may be added [to the board], but the four chosen by him should also remain a part of it,” Nasir alleged.
